OptimizerAI, Inc. offers a commercial API on tiered dedicated/shared plans with SLA guarantees, authenticated with a project-specific API key sent over an HTTPS header. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z).

providers.name: Atmosplay
providers.description: Atmosplay was a mobile advertising technology company, founded in 2014 in Budapest, Hungary, that built interactive 3D "playable" ads and an ad-monetization platform for mobile game publishers. Its ATMIQ cloud gameplay engine let users try a game inside an ad without installing it, and its self-serve builder produced playable creatives for 3D and action games. Atmosplay shipped first-party mobile SDKs (Unity, iOS, Android) plus AdMob and MoPub mediation adapters for publishers to integrate interstitial, banner, and rewarded-video formats. Speedinvest led its Series A in 2016; the company was acquired by ZPLAY Information Technology on 2018-01-01. Its websites (atmosplay.com / atmosplay.net) are no longer operational; the surviving public developer surface is its GitHub organization of SDK and adapter repositories. This profile is maintained for network completeness as an acquired/inactive portfolio lead.

providers.name: SOUNDRAW
providers.description: SOUNDRAW is an AI music generation platform that produces royalty-free, copyright-cleared music customized by genre, mood, theme, length, and instrumentation. Beyond the soundraw.io consumer product, SOUNDRAW offers a B2B API for embedding music generation into video platforms, games, social tools, and ad tech, with Canva, Filmora, and Captions Mirage cited as integration partners.

providers.name: Codewisp
providers.description: Codewisp is an AI-powered game creation platform that lets anyone build and publish real web games from natural-language prompts, with no coding or game-development tools required. Users describe the game they want and the platform generates the code, structure, and assets automatically, supporting 2D, 3D, and multiplayer browser games with instant, prompt-driven refinement. Founded by game developer Elvin Fu and part of Y Combinator's Winter 2026 batch, Codewisp reports 2,000+ weekly active creators and 17,000+ games created, offering a browser-based block editor, a community explore and marketplace surface, and shareable instant-play links. Codewisp is a consumer creation product and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Forte Labs
providers.description: Forte builds on-chain compliance and economic tooling for games and Web3 applications. Its flagship developer product, the Forte Rules Engine, is an open-source EVM protocol that lets developers define powerful, flexible, and composable on-chain policies — for regulatory compliance, risk management, and token-economy design — without hardcoding rules into their smart contracts. The engine centers on policies, rules, trackers, and calling/foreign contracts, ships client contracts for the ERC20/721/1155/721A token standards, and is consumed through a TypeScript SDK. Forte was founded in 2019 and is backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Battery Ventures, Griffin Gaming Partners, and Canaan. This profile catalogs Forte's public developer surface — Rules Engine documentation, SDK, and GitHub organization.

providers.name: Babylon.js
providers.description: Babylon.js is an Apache-2.0 licensed, TypeScript-first open-source 3D engine and rendering framework sponsored by Microsoft and developed in the public BabylonJS GitHub organization. It targets WebGL, WebGPU, and WebXR in the browser, and DirectX, Metal, Vulkan, OpenGL, and OpenGL ES natively through Babylon Native — including a Babylon React Native binding for mobile. The framework ships as a family of scoped npm packages (`@babylonjs/core`, `gui`, `loaders`, `materials`, `inspector`, `serializers`, `post-processes`, `procedural-textures`, `node-editor`) plus a rich tooling surface — the Playground IDE, Sandbox asset viewer, Inspector, Spector.js, the Node Material / Geometry / Particle / Render-Graph editors, a community Editor, the Babylon Toolkit (Unity / Unreal exporters), and DCC exporters for 3ds Max, Maya, and Blender — all backed by the public Snippet API at `snippet.babylonjs.com` that powers shareable Playground and node-editor assets.

providers.name: General Intuition
providers.description: General Intuition is a frontier AI lab building large action foundation models that can perceive, predict, and act across space and time in both virtual and physical environments. Spun out of the gaming clip platform Medal, the company trains its spatial-temporal reasoning models on billions of action-labeled gameplay clips - recordings of exactly which buttons a player pressed and when - to teach AI agents how to move through and reason about the world. Its Mira world model powers applications across games, simulation, and robotics. Founded in 2025 and based in New York City, General Intuition has raised $454M total, including a $320M Series A at a $2.3B valuation, and is onboarding first partners to a commercial API ahead of a broader developer release.

providers.name: NAVER Z
providers.description: NAVER Z Corporation is the South Korean metaverse subsidiary of NAVER, headquartered in Seongnam, Gyeonggi Province, with additional offices in Los Angeles and Tokyo. The company builds immersive digital experiences spanning ZEPETO, its avatar-based metaverse and social app launched in 2018; ZEP, a spatial collaboration and virtual-space platform launched in 2022; and Sticker.ly, a sticker creation and sharing app launched in 2019. NAVER Z's public developer surface is ZEP Script: a first-party JavaScript SDK, CLI, and build toolchain (published on npm under the official @zep.us scope) that creators use to build in-space apps and mini-games, documented in the ZEP Guidebook at docs.zep.us with a dedicated ZEP Script API reference. NAVER Z publishes no REST/OpenAPI web API or OAuth program; ZEPETO Studio remains a Unity-based content-creation tool rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Supercell
providers.description: Supercell is the Finnish mobile game developer behind Clash of Clans, Clash Royale, Brawl Stars, Hay Day, Boom Beach and Squad Busters. Supercell operates three official public game APIs — the Clash of Clans API, the Clash Royale API and the Brawl Stars API — that expose read-only game data including clan search, global and local leaderboards, player and clan profiles, leagues, cards, brawlers, rankings and live events. Access is authenticated with a JWT bearer API token created in each game's developer portal and locked to a set of whitelisted IP addresses. Added to the API Evangelist network from a VC-portfolio lead and enriched with verified developer-surface artifacts.

providers.name: Immersed
providers.description: Immersed is a spatial-computing company that turns AR/VR headsets into portable multi-monitor workspaces for remote work, coding, and collaboration. Its free desktop agent streams up to five virtual screens into headsets such as Meta Quest, Apple Vision Pro, GalaxyXR, and Pico, adding solo focus environments plus multi-user telepresence with screen sharing and whiteboarding. Immersed is also building Visor, its own lightweight 4K-per-eye standalone headset. The company is Techstars-backed. Immersed publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web, product, security, and llms.txt surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Primodium Inc.
providers.description: Primodium Inc. (primodiumxyz) is a developer-focused studio building fully on-chain applications and games on Ethereum and Solana. It ships two on-chain games — Primodium, a space-based factory-building game, and Primodium: Empires, a turn-based prediction-market game — both built with MUD and Phaser, alongside a suite of open-source developer libraries and infrastructure: Reactive Tables (a strictly-typed reactive table library for MUD apps), a Solana DEX Indexer Stack exposing a GraphQL API over Hasura/Timescale, a tRPC transaction-sponsoring DEX server, an off-chain MUD indexer, and gasless-transaction relayers. All tooling is published open-source under the MIT license via the primodiumxyz GitHub organization and the @primodiumxyz npm scope.

providers.name: Spline
providers.description: Spline is a real-time collaborative 3D design tool with AI-driven object generation, web embedding, and animation. Spline does NOT publish a REST API for 3D scene generation as of May 2026; instead it exposes Code APIs (Web, SwiftUI, Kotlin) for embedding scenes, plus a real-time API for variables/data and webhooks for event-driven integrations.

providers.name: Manticore Games
providers.description: Manticore Games is a San Mateo-based game developer and publisher, and the studio behind Core — a free, Unreal Engine-powered game-creation platform and metaverse where a global community of creators builds, publishes, and plays multiplayer games and experiences. Core exposes a rich Lua scripting API (namespaces, types, and events for Players, Weapons, Abilities, Storage, Leaderboards, Chat, UI, and World) that lets creators program game logic directly in the editor. Manticore is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund.

providers.name: Regression Games
providers.description: Regression Games builds AI agents and bots for video games. Its platform lets studios create bots for QA testing, multiplayer simulation, game balancing, and NPC behavior with minimal code. The Unity SDK (gg.regression.unity.bots / RGUnityBots) adds AI-driven automated playtesting, UI and screenshot regression testing, replay and validation, and CI/CD integration for Unity projects, while the earlier rg-bot JavaScript/TypeScript/Python libraries let developers program bots for Minecraft and Capture-the-Flag tournaments. Distribution is via open-source SDKs and templates on GitHub rather than a hosted public REST API. Backed by a16z and NEA ($4.2M seed, 2022).

providers.name: Trass Games
providers.description: Trass Games is an a16z-backed independent VR game studio best known for Yeeps - Hide and Seek, a free-to-play social hide-and-seek and building game on Meta Quest, and Gods of Gravity, an arcade space RTS. The studio ships a Yeeps companion app for iOS and Android, sells plush, maker-kit, and apparel merchandise through Shopify storefronts at yeeps.com and godsofgravityvr.com, and runs a community licensing program for creators. Trass Games publishes no first-party developer API, but its storefronts expose agent-ready commerce surfaces including llms.txt, agents.md, a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile, and a live storefront MCP endpoint.

providers.name: OPGG
providers.description: OP.GG is the world's leading League of Legends statistics and performance tracking platform. Founded in Seoul, South Korea and launched in 2013, it grew from a LoL stats search engine into a global gaming platform serving tens of millions of monthly active users across games including League of Legends, Valorant, Teamfight Tactics, Overwatch 2, and PUBG. OP.GG surfaces summoner ranks, win rates, champion mastery, builds, tier lists, match history, and live meta trends. Its programmatic surface centers on an official, hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that gives AI agents access to LoL, TFT, and Valorant game data, plus first-party AI-readable ai.json summoner/match snapshot endpoints advertised in its published llms.txt. OP.GG is backed by 500 Global, SBVA, DS Asset Management, Dunamu & Partners, and others.

providers.name: DigiLens
providers.description: DigiLens Inc. is a Sunnyvale, California company that designs and manufactures holographic waveguide optics and augmented reality display systems for extended reality (XR). Its Crystal Waveguides are produced with a proprietary photopolymer material set, inkjet printing and a holographic contact-copy process rather than etching, and are supplied to partners including Samsung, Corning, Panasonic, Sony, Continental, Mitsubishi Chemical and Goertek for smartglasses, automotive head-up displays, smart helmets and avionics head-up guidance. DigiLens also ships ARGO, a standalone, rugged enterprise AR headset running DigiOS — an Android-based operating system with voice UI, gaze and scroll-wheel interaction, projector control and Microsoft Intune MDM certification. Developers build for ARGO in Unity or Android Studio on top of the DigiOS SDK and Qualcomm Snapdragon Spaces, with samples published in the digilens-ar GitHub organization and documentation on the DigiLens developer portal. DigiLens has raised a Series D led by Samsung Electronics at a valuation above $500M.

providers.name: Floreo
providers.description: Floreo is a research-based virtual reality (VR) digital therapeutics company that delivers immersive lessons teaching social, behavioral, communication, and life skills to neurodiverse individuals, including autistic children and adults. The platform runs across mobile (iPhone with Google Cardboard) and standalone VR headsets (Meta Quest 2/3/Pro, PICO), with a companion clinician portal for supervised sessions, progress tracking, and telehealth-style delivery. Floreo holds an FDA Breakthrough Device designation and participates in the FDA Total Product Life Cycle Advisory Program (TAP), and works with schools, behavioral-health providers, Medicaid programs, and research partners. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta; the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK at this time.

providers.name: DIY
providers.description: DIY.org is a safe, ad-free creative platform where kids turn ideas into real games, apps, and websites — guided by AI tools like Vibe Coding and KidsGPT and reviewed by human moderators. Serving over 500,000 young creators, it pairs game-building templates, AI image and art tools, badge-based learning, and 75+ standards-aligned courses with parent and classroom dashboards, SSO, and safety controls. Originally a maker community for kids, DIY is backed by Kleiner Perkins and Slow Ventures.

providers.name: Forte
providers.description: Forte is a Web3 economic infrastructure company building compliance and economic tools for games and digital-asset economies. Its flagship product is the Forte Rules Engine, a free, open-source, EVM-compatible on-chain policy engine that lets smart-contract developers define composable, adaptive rules (KYC gates, OFAC/sanctions screening, vesting schedules, circuit breakers, and other economic guardrails) without hardcoding logic into their contracts. The Rules Engine ships a TypeScript SDK and Solidity client contracts, and is complemented by a ZK Policy Engine for privacy-preserving policy enforcement. Forte is backed by a16z, Canaan Partners, and Trinity Ventures.

providers.name: Common Sense Machines
providers.description: Common Sense Machines (CSM) builds 3D world models with image-to-3D and 3D world simulation APIs aimed at games, robotics, and synthetic data. The CSM Cube product family released a single-click model pipeline with mesh-parts-based topology in early 2026. API access is bundled with mid-tier and enterprise CSM subscription plans.

providers.name: Dreamforge
providers.description: DreamForge.ai is an AI-powered game creation platform for building, iterating on, and publishing 2D and stylized 3D games directly in the browser. Creators use AI to generate gameplay systems, game-ready art and textures, animation, and playable web builds, then share public play pages under dreamforge.ai/play. The platform pairs a creator-facing web studio (including an Asset Studio) with a consumer application distributed on Steam, iOS, and Android. Founded in 2025 and based in Miami, Florida, DreamForge is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). DreamForge supports stylized 3D world generation, textures, voxels, and billboarding workflows; native 3D model generation is not currently provided. No public developer API, SDK, or developer portal is published at this time.

providers.name: Razer
providers.description: Razer is a global lifestyle brand for gamers that designs gaming hardware (Blade laptops, mice, keyboards, headsets and other peripherals), software (Synapse, Cortex) and services. For developers Razer operates the WYVRN immersive gaming platform, exposing the Razer Chroma RGB SDK and REST API for controlling 16.8-million-color lighting across devices, the Razer Sensa HD Haptics and THX Spatial Audio SDKs, Razer ID for user sign-in, and the Razer Gold / Razer Silver virtual-currency payment and rewards APIs for in-app monetization across 34,000+ integrated games and apps.

providers.name: Games24x7
providers.description: Games24x7 is a Mumbai-headquartered Indian online skill-gaming company founded in 2006 by Bhavin Pandya and Trivikraman Thampy, operating consumer real-money and casual gaming platforms rather than a developer API business. Its portfolio spans RummyCircle (online rummy), My11Circle (fantasy cricket, football, kabaddi and ludo) and Wowzy (a three-dice ludo variant), backed by Tiger Global, The Raine Group and Malabar Investment. The company publishes engineering writing on distributed systems, Cassandra, Amazon Aurora, ksqlDB and React Native through its Resources section, runs the TechXpedite accelerator, and maintains a small public GitHub organization (games24x7-opensource) plus one first-party npm package for AI-assisted Appium test automation. As of August 2026 it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation, no machine-readable specification, and no partner or affiliate API of its own.

providers.name: Goals
providers.description: Goals (playgoals.com, formerly goals.co) is a free-to-play competitive football (soccer) video game studio backed by Northzone. It positions itself as a gameplay-first football game — "No scripts, no excuses, just football" — with fast, skill-based competitive matches, unique player squads, card-pack collection, ranked leaderboards, and multiple game modes across Steam, Xbox, PlayStation, and the Epic Games Store. A companion app lets players manage squads and open packs. This profile was surfaced as a Northzone portfolio company (consumer sector) and added to the API Evangelist network; the studio publishes a consumer game and a community surface (Discord, guides, leaderboards) but no public developer API.

providers.name: Tech Soft 3D
providers.description: Tech Soft 3D builds developer SDKs and enterprise applications that power 3D data exchange, visualization, and analysis across engineering, manufacturing, and design. Its HOOPS toolkits (Exchange for CAD data translation and access, Visualize for high-performance 3D graphics, Access, Mesh, Solve, and Envision) are licensed to OEMs and independent developers building CAD, CAM, CAE, and PLM software, and it also distributes Siemens Parasolid and Polygonica. Alongside the native toolkits it publishes the HOOPS Visualize Web Components (open, first-party npm packages), SpinFire enterprise viewing/conversion apps, and OEM technologies such as AutoCAD OEM, Inventor OEM, and RealDWG. Tech Soft 3D is backed by Battery Ventures.

providers.name: Eksab
providers.description: Eksab is a Cairo-based daily fantasy sports and football-prediction platform for the MENA region. Founded in 2017 by Aly Mahmoud, it lets fans predict the scores and outcomes of live football matches, earn points based on the accuracy of their picks, and win prizes through free and paid competitions. The platform has grown to over 700,000 registered users making more than a million picks each month, and in 2022 became the exclusive fantasy sports partner of the Egyptian Premier League. Eksab is backed by 500 Global (500 Startups), 4DX Ventures, and others across roughly $3.7M in seed funding. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Eksab is a consumer mobile/web product and does not currently publish a public developer API surface.

providers.name: Rockstar Games
providers.description: Rockstar Games is an American video game publisher headquartered in New York City and a wholly-owned subsidiary of Take-Two Interactive Software (NASDAQ: TTWO). Best known for the Grand Theft Auto and Red Dead Redemption franchises, Rockstar operates online services for GTA Online and Red Dead Online, the Rockstar Games Launcher PC client, and the legacy Rockstar Games Social Club identity / authentication platform. Rockstar does not publish a public developer portal; its HTTP API surface is internal and consumed only by first-party clients (game executables, the Rockstar Games Launcher, and Rockstar's mobile companion apps). The most visible public-facing API is its OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0 identity provider at signin.rockstargames.com, which exposes standard /connect/authorize, /connect/Token, /connect/introspect, and /.well-known/jwks endpoints. Grand Theft Auto VI is scheduled to launch on November 19, 2026 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S and will include a "significant online mode" succeeding GTA Online.

providers.name: Kixeye
providers.description: KIXEYE Inc. is a video game developer and publisher founded in 2009 and headquartered in Victoria, British Columbia, with staff across Canada and the United States. KIXEYE creates, develops, and publishes massively multiplayer online real-time strategy (MMORTS) games for browsers, tablets, and smartphones, including Battle Pirates, War Commander, War Commander: Rogue Assault, and Rise of Firstborn. An early innovator in the free-to-play genre, KIXEYE operates long-lived live-service game worlds with monthly events, alliances, and competitive leaderboards for millions of players worldwide. KIXEYE is part of the Stillfront Group. KIXEYE publishes no public developer program or partner API; its api.kixeye.com host is a private game-services backend that exposes an OpenID Connect discovery document and JWKS for token verification. The company does maintain a public GitHub organization of open-source infrastructure libraries (chassis, kixmpp, janus, scout) used to build its own cloud services.

providers.name: Over
providers.description: Overworld is an open-science AI research lab building interactive world models - AI-generated video environments that respond in real time to text prompts and controller input at game-level framerates. Its open-source World Engine is a Python inference library that loads Waypoint world models and LoRA adapters from HuggingFace to generate playable, promptable worlds locally or in the browser. Founded by Louis Castricato (CEO) and Shahbuland Matiana (Head of Mathematical Research), both formerly of CarperAI and Stability AI, the team operates openly and publishes its infrastructure as public open-source repositories. Overworld does not currently expose a hosted REST API; its primary developer artifact is the first-party world_engine Python SDK.

providers.name: Zibra AI
providers.description: Zibra AI is a Ukrainian deep-tech company building AI-powered real-time volumetric rendering and compression technology for VFX, gaming, virtual production, film, and TV. Its flagship product, ZibraVDB, compresses OpenVDB volumetric datasets to roughly five percent of their original size while preserving visual quality, enabling real-time playback of smoke, fire, fog, and other volumetric effects. Zibra ships a native C++ ZibraVDB SDK (DirectX 12, Vulkan, and Metal on Windows, Linux, and macOS) alongside plugins for Unreal Engine, Houdini, and Unity, with Blender support in progress. It exposes no public REST/HTTP API; integration is through the SDK and digital-content-creation plugins. Surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Motif
providers.description: Motif is an AEC (architecture, engineering, and construction) software company building an intelligent, browser-based workspace for building design. Founded in 2023 by former Autodesk leaders Amar Hanspal and Brian Mathews, Motif unifies sheet review, live 3D streaming, AI-assisted visual exploration, and real-time collaboration in a single cloud platform that bridges 2D and 3D workflows as a step toward making Building Information Modeling (BIM) a practical reality. The company has raised $46M led by Redpoint Ventures (seed) and Alphabet's CapitalG (Series A), and was named to Forbes' 2025 Next Billion-Dollar Startups list. Motif is a collaboration SaaS product for design and construction teams; it publishes product learning docs and a help center but does not yet expose a public developer API — a plugin/API surface is part of its stated long-term strategy.

providers.name: Tripo3D
providers.description: Tripo3D (by VAST) is an AI 3D generation platform with text-to-3D, image-to-3D, mesh refinement, and texturing APIs producing game-ready 3D assets. The Tripo API uses an async task-based REST pattern at https://api.tripo3d.ai/v2/openapi/task. Authenticate with API key.

providers.name: Activ Surgical
providers.description: Activ Surgical is a Boston, Massachusetts digital surgery company building intraoperative surgical intelligence for the operating room. Its flagship product, the ActivSight Intelligent Light imaging module, attaches to existing laparoscopic and robotic surgical systems and renders augmented-reality overlays on a standard monitor, letting surgeons see physiology the naked eye cannot. ActivPerfusion delivers dye-free, real-time blood-perfusion imaging using laser speckle contrast imaging, while ActivICG supports conventional indocyanine green visualization of structures such as bile ducts. The module is powered by the ActivEdge platform, a hardware-agnostic computer-vision, AI and machine-learning stack the company is building to turn intraoperative data into real-time surgical guidance. Activ Surgical performed the first autonomous robotic soft-tissue surgery in 2018, received FDA 510(k) clearance for ActivSight in April 2021 and CE Mark approval in December 2022, and sells on a subscription model with no capital-equipment purchase. The company publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable API contract as of this profiling pass; its public technical surface is regulatory (EU MDR declarations of conformity, ISO 13485:2016) and clinical (peer-reviewed studies and white papers).

providers.name: Gameforge
providers.description: Gameforge AG is a German publisher of free-to-play online and browser games, headquartered in Karlsruhe, Germany. Its catalog includes long-running titles such as OGame, Ikariam, Metin2, AION, NosTale, and other strategy and MMO games played across dozens of localized game servers. Gameforge's flagship title OGame exposes a public read-only game-data API that returns highscores, player and alliance rosters, universe/planet layouts, and per-server metadata as XML feeds (with an opt-in JSON representation), plus a separate access-controlled API that approved third-party tool developers can request for combat and report data. Gameforge also runs a coordinated vulnerability disclosure program through Bugcrowd. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Fab.com
providers.description: Fab.com is a digital content marketplace operated by Epic Games, where creators buy and sell 3D models, materials, environments, VFX, audio, and game-ready assets. Launched in October 2024, Fab consolidated four of Epic's prior storefronts — the Unreal Engine Marketplace, the Sketchfab Store, Quixel, and the ArtStation Marketplace — into a single catalog with unified licensing, and integrates into Unreal Engine, UEFN, and the Epic Games Launcher. The fabcom entry was originally added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio lead for the earlier, unrelated Fab.com flash-sale design-commerce company (2011–2015), which wound down before the domain passed to Epic Games; see x-identity-note. Fab publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification as of this pass — the surface captured here is its documentation, support, and security-disclosure posture.

providers.name: Illumix
providers.description: Illumix is an enterprise-grade spatial AI company spun out of Stanford's Computer Science Department, providing a core stack for real-world location intelligence that runs at the edge with centimeter-level precision. Its hardware-agnostic platform delivers sub-second localization and 3D mapping across mobile devices, AR/VR wearables, and robotics using standard cameras — with no LiDAR or GPS dependency — combining multimodal vision-language AI with long-term memory that learns behavior over time. Illumix serves AI/XR wearables, enterprise and logistics, defense and security, location-based entertainment, and robotics, with deployments referenced for Disney, Six Flags, Cedar Fair, MGM Resorts, Warner Bros, Verizon, and Sony. The company markets developer APIs and an SDK as part of a full-stack offering, but publishes no public developer portal, reference documentation, or machine-readable API specification at this time.

providers.name: Parallel Universe
providers.description: Parallel Universe Inc. (Parallel Studios) is the Toronto-based game studio behind Parallel, a free-to-play sci-fi trading card game, and the broader Parallel Universe franchise that includes Colony, an AI agent simulation game, and Sanctuary, a third-person extraction shooter. The studio anchors the Echelon Prime web3 gaming ecosystem, where players truly own their cards and in-game items as blockchain assets and the PRIME token powers governance and rewards. Backed by a16z (Andreessen Horowitz) and Paradigm, Parallel is a consumer game franchise distributed via the web, Epic Games, Steam, the Apple App Store, and Google Play. It publishes no public developer / REST API surface today; this profile captures the studio's public web, community, and legal properties as harvested by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Backbone
providers.description: Backbone is a mobile gaming company that makes the Backbone One controller — a snap-on gamepad for iPhone and Android — and the Backbone app, a mobile gaming platform that unifies a player's game library across cloud gaming, console Remote Play, and streaming services with game discovery, capture, and social features. The company sells hardware and accessories through a Shopify-hosted storefront (backbone.com) that exposes an agent-commerce surface via the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) MCP endpoint and Shopify Customer Account OIDC. Backbone is a portfolio company of Index Ventures. This profile was enriched from Backbone's public web surface; the company publishes no first-party developer API.

providers.name: Genopets
providers.description: Genopets is a free-to-play, move-to-earn NFT game built on the Solana blockchain that gamifies an active lifestyle. Players nurture a digital pet — a Genopet — that evolves from real-world physical activity tracked via step counting, then battle, craft, stake, and trade in-game NFTs and Habitats. The economy pairs the GENE governance token with the in-game KI utility token earned by moving. Genopets is developed by a studio backed by Pantera Capital and operates a consumer mobile/web game rather than a public developer API; no OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Betr
providers.description: Betr (Betr Holdings, Inc.) is a Miami-based real-money gaming and sports media company founded in 2022 by Joey Levy and Jake Paul on a $50M Series A. Betr operates a consumer "real money gaming super app" spanning Betr Picks (real-money pick'em daily fantasy sports across NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL, UFC and golf), a micro-betting sportsbook launched in Ohio in January 2023, a social sportsbook and social casino, Betr Arcade, and Betr Media (podcasts, creator content and digital sports programming). Betr is a business-to-consumer operator: it publishes mobile apps, a Webflow marketing site, an Intercom-hosted help center and an llms.txt discovery file, but as of this profiling round it publishes no public developer API program, no OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/GraphQL contract, and no SDKs. Its API hosts (api.betr.app, and a staging back-office API documentation host) are private and return 500/403 to anonymous callers.

providers.name: Playbite
providers.description: Playbite is a free mobile arcade app - "an arcade in your pocket" - built by Digital Media Technology SL and backed by 500 Global. The app offers an ever-expanding library of simple, casual games spanning multiplayer, rhythm, puzzle, matching, relaxing, and racing categories, with over 500,000 players who play games and earn rewards. The service is free to users and monetized through non-intrusive advertising. Playbite is a consumer-facing mobile gaming product distributed through the Apple App Store and Google Play; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal, so this profile captures its company identity, public web properties, and domain security posture rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Atari
providers.description: Atari is one of the founding brands of the interactive entertainment industry, originally established in 1972, and today operates as a global video game and consumer-hardware company. It publishes classic and modern titles, manufactures the Atari VCS console and retro hardware (Atari 2600+, Atari 400 Mini), licenses its catalog and brand, and sells games, collectibles, and merchandise through its official online store at atari.com. Atari does not publish a general-purpose public REST API; its developer surface is limited to Atari VCS content-submission guidance (developers email vcs@atari.com and use the VCS submission portal) and legacy HTML5 Atari Arcade SDK libraries on GitHub. This profile was surfaced as a Mayfield portfolio company — a nod to Mayfield's foundational 1970s venture investment in Atari — and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Z1
providers.description: Z1 is the API Evangelist network profile for the consumer social gaming app operated by Bunch Live, Inc., known publicly as Bunch and now rebranded as Mini Party (mini.party). The product lets friends hang out, play party games, and video chat together in real time on mobile, and connects with external services such as Discord. Bunch raised early venture funding (including a $3.8M round) and is tracked here as a 500 Global portfolio company. Bunch formerly operated a Bunch Developer Platform (the "Party Kit" voice/video SDK for iOS, Android, and Unity plus a Party Reservation API), but that developer program has been discontinued and the company currently publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal — this profile captures its identity, legal surface, and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Hidden Door
providers.description: Hidden Door is an interactive storytelling platform where roleplay meets fan fiction, letting players step into imaginative worlds and shape branching narratives through their choices. Players pick a pre-built world, add modifiers, create a character, and experience a unique story with a full cast of characters, where every playthrough differs. Creators can build playable worlds in as little as thirty minutes, then share, publish, and get paid when others play. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Homebrew and Northzone and added to the API Evangelist network. Hidden Door ships a consumer web experience and publishes no developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time. Sector: AI / entertainment.

providers.name: Start Playing
providers.description: StartPlaying (startplaying.games) is the largest online marketplace connecting tabletop roleplaying game (TTRPG) players with professional Game Masters for systems including Dungeons & Dragons, Pathfinder, Starfinder, Warhammer, and many more. Players discover, book, and join online sessions filtered by system, platform, genre, playstyle, and GM reviews, while Game Masters build careers by hosting paid games across virtual tabletops. The platform also offers gift cards, learn-to-play one-shots for beginners, kids' games, and corporate team-building events. Surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; enrichment found a consumer web product with no public developer API.

providers.name: StatusPRO
providers.description: StatusPRO is a sports technology and gaming company founded by former professional athletes, building extended reality (XR) products that pair competitive training tools for elite athletes with immersive gaming experiences for consumers. Its flagship product, NFL PRO ERA, is an officially NFL- and NFLPA-licensed virtual reality football game for Meta Quest headsets, and its StatusPRO Visualizer powers immersive broadcast perspectives used by ESPN on NFL Live. The company operates a live-services consumer game rather than a developer platform: it publishes no public API, developer portal, or API documentation. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record; it carries no API surface at this time.

providers.name: IrisVR
providers.description: IrisVR is a virtual-reality software company for the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) industry, best known for its two products: Prospect, a desktop application that converts Revit, SketchUp, Rhino, Navisworks and other 3D/BIM models into immersive VR walkthroughs in one click, and Scope, a mobile app for viewing and sharing 360-degree panoramas on standalone and phone-based VR headsets. Founded in New York, IrisVR was acquired by The Wild in 2021, and The Wild (together with IrisVR) was subsequently acquired by Autodesk in 2022. The products and support site remain available. IrisVR does not publish a public developer API; this profile tracks its identity, packages, and public web properties in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: NeonRain, Inc.
providers.description: NeonRain, Inc. is a 500 Global portfolio company whose public product surface resolves to Playabl (playabl.ai), an AI-powered, no-code platform that lets anyone create web games and interactive experiences by chatting with AI. Users describe a game idea in plain English and Playabl's generative AI produces a playable prototype instantly, which can be refined conversationally and published to the web. Founded in 2025 and headquartered in the United States, the product targets educators, indie developers, marketers, and hobbyists. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a consumer web application with no developer-facing API, SDK, documentation, or developer portal surface.

providers.name: Playabl
providers.description: Playabl is a no-code, conversational game creation platform that lets anyone build games and interactive experiences by chatting with AI. Operated by Replkt, Inc. and backed by Y Combinator, Playabl turns natural-language prompts into playable games across genres including sports, idle, brainrot, dopamine, and think/puzzle categories, with no coding required. The product is a consumer-facing web application (playabl.ai); as of this profile Playabl does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or technical documentation surface. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from the company's public web presence.

providers.name: ThriveFantasy
providers.description: ThriveFantasy was a New York City daily fantasy sports platform focused on player-prop pick'em contests across NFL, NBA, MLB, esports, and other leagues, backed by Bullpen Capital. The company ceased operations in early 2024 after a failed funding round and a player-withdrawal crisis. It never published a public API, developer portal, or SDKs; its legacy marketing site remains online.

providers.name: Hyperpad
providers.description: Hyperpad (hyperPad) is a no-code, visual game development platform for iPad, often described as "HyperCard for iPad." Founded in 2013 and backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2014), the London, Ontario company lets non-programmers build media-rich 2D games and interactive apps using a drag-and-drop, node-based behavior system with a built-in physics engine, particle effects, animation and audio tools, and a bundled asset library, then publish them to the Apple App Store as native apps while keeping 100% of royalties. Products include the paid hyperPad app, a free hyperPad Starter edition, and hyperPad Hub, a community arcade for playing games made with the platform. hyperPad is a consumer-facing creation tool and does not currently publish a public web API or developer platform.

providers.name: Machinations
providers.description: Machinations is a visual platform for designing, simulating, and balancing game economies, tokenomics, and other complex systems. Studios and designers model resource flows as interactive node-and-connection diagrams, run Monte-Carlo simulations to predict outcomes, and balance economies before a single line of production code is written. The product spans Design, Predict, and Balance modules plus an AI Builder that generates runnable diagrams from natural-language descriptions and a spreadsheet integration. It is used by studios such as Amazon Games, Hasbro, and Zynga and taught at MIT, NYU, and Berkeley. Machinations is a Seedcamp portfolio company; at the time of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface.

providers.name: Track Titan
providers.description: Track Titan is a sim racing analytics and coaching platform that records in-game telemetry from simulators including iRacing, Assetto Corsa and ACC, the F1 series, Automobilista 2, Forza Motorsport, and Le Mans Ultimate, turning laps into time-loss analysis, AI coaching feedback, auto-installed esports car setups, and structured Academy learning content for a community of over 295,000 sim racers on PC and console. Founded by former professional sim racer and Porsche coach Max Teichert and backed by investors including Partech, Track Titan is a consumer product and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface as of July 2026 (api.tracktitan.io serves only an internal backend service).

providers.name: RACE Protocol
providers.description: RACE Protocol is a multi-chain, on-chain infrastructure for developing and deploying secure and fair web3 games. It is delivered primarily through a TypeScript/JavaScript SDK (sdk-core, sdk-solana, sdk-sui, sdk-facade) and a command-line tool (race-cli) for game bundle publishing, account management, and payment claims, rather than as a traditional REST API. Smart contracts run on Solana and Sui.

providers.name: Open 3D Foundation
providers.description: The Open 3D Foundation is a Linux Foundation project supporting the Open 3D Engine (O3DE), an open source, real-time 3D engine for building games, simulations, and other 3D applications. With Microsoft as a premier member, it provides a modular, cross-platform engine with advanced rendering capabilities.

providers.name: Players Lounge
providers.description: Players' Lounge is a skill-based competitive gaming platform where users win money by completing personalized head-to-head gaming challenges (money matches) or by staking and watching other players compete. The platform supports popular console and PC titles including Madden, NBA 2K, Call of Duty Warzone, Marvel Rivals, and others, and states it has paid out over $200M to players to date. Players' Lounge is a consumer product surfaced as a portfolio company of Canaan Partners; it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation at this time. This profile captures the company's public identity and web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Spacetime Studios
providers.description: Spacetime Studios is an Austin, Texas mobile game developer and the creator of the free-to-play "Legends" series of cross-platform MMORPGs, including Arcane Legends, Pocket Legends, Star Legends, and Dark Legends. Founded by veteran game developers, the studio operates a consumer-facing community forum, an in-game item web store, and player support channels. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the studio publishes no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, developer portal, or /.well-known discovery surface; this profile captures its verified public web properties and domain security posture.

providers.name: General Intuition
providers.description: General Intuition is a frontier AI lab, founded in 2025 and spun out of Medal, building spatial-temporal world and action models that learn to perceive, anticipate, and act in space and time. Rather than training primarily on the archive of human language, its systems learn from gameplay data, teaching machines to play, dream within compressed simulacra of reality, and improvise within the unfolding dynamics of the world. The company is developing a commercial API for gaming, simulation, and robotics partners, with broader access planned through 2026. General Intuition is backed by Khosla Ventures, which led both its $133.7M seed round (October 2025) and its $320M Series A at a $2.3B valuation (2026).

providers.name: Play Versus
providers.description: Play Versus (PlayVS) is North America's leading scholastic and collegiate esports platform, operating competitive gaming leagues for middle schools, high schools, and colleges alongside an esports curriculum and college recruitment services. The platform partners with major publishers including Riot Games, EA, Blizzard, and Psyonix, and runs its competitions and rosters through the app.playvs.com web application. PlayVS is a consumer/education product and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation surface; this profile captures its published identity, support, and policy properties. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Take-Two Interactive Software
providers.description: Take-Two Interactive Software is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Take-Two Interactive Software API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Brelyon
providers.description: Brelyon is an MIT Media Lab spin-off building headset-free virtual displays — desktop monitors that use electro-optics and computational rendering to produce monocular image depth rather than autostereoscopic 3D. Its Ultra Reality line delivers a 122-inch virtual screen filling roughly 110 degrees of field of view, alongside Ultra Reality Extend (a multi-focal monitor that renders AI-generated overlays at different depths), Ultra Reality Mini, and experimental Hyper Displays. The company is headquartered in San Mateo, California with an international office in Taichung, Taiwan, and sells into enterprise simulation, training, teleoperation and medical visualization; prosumer flight simulation, gaming, trading and content production; and automotive in-vehicle HMI integration. Brelyon ships desktop software (Brelyon Suite, Focal Studio, Visual Engine, Stream Weaver) for distortion correction, monitor merging and multi-focal content creation, but publishes no public developer program, API, or SDK.

providers.name: Improbable
providers.description: Improbable (Improbable Worlds Ltd) is a London-based technology company and venture builder. Founded in 2012, it originally built SpatialOS, a distributed simulation and networking platform for large-scale real-time multiplayer games, and later Morpheus / M² (MSquared), a network of interoperable metaverse worlds. Today Improbable operates primarily as a venture builder and capital allocator, partnering with founders to launch and scale companies across AI, Web3 and the metaverse. It is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and the SoftBank Vision Fund. Its historical developer surface centered on the SpatialOS Platform SDK, Worker SDK and the `spatial` CLI (distributed via NuGet), plus the improbable-eng and spatialos GitHub organizations; the standalone documentation, status and IMS subdomains have since been retired as the company pivoted away from a standalone developer platform.

providers.name: Loft Dynamics
providers.description: Loft Dynamics is a Swiss aviation technology company (founded 2016, headquartered in Dübendorf, Switzerland with a North American office in Santa Monica) that builds virtual reality flight simulation training devices (FSTDs) for helicopters, fixed-wing aircraft, and eVTOLs. Its simulators combine full-scale replica cockpits, dynamic motion platforms, 360-degree VR visuals, and advanced pose tracking, and were the first VR aircraft simulators to earn EASA and FAA qualification. Products include VR simulators for the Airbus H145, Airbus H125, and Robinson R22 helicopters, with Boeing 737 and eVTOL platforms in development. Customers include Alaska Airlines, the FAA, Airbus Helicopters, the LAPD, and Marshall University. The company operates the LoftHUB customer platform but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: Loftia
providers.description: Loftia is a cozy, solarpunk massively-multiplayer online (MMO) game developed by Qloud Games Pty Ltd, a remote-first indie studio founded in 2022 and headquartered in Sydney, Australia. Set across floating islands in a warm, sustainable world, players farm, craft, decorate, socialize, and build a life in the sky alongside friends in a shared world that grows over time. The studio (founded by Eric Mallon, Martina Qin, and Michael Su) raised a $5M seed round led by BITKRAFT Ventures and GFR Fund with participation from Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), and took part in a16z's SPEEDRUN gaming accelerator. Loftia is a consumer game company with no public developer API surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Lumosity
providers.description: Lumosity is a consumer brain-training platform built by Lumos Labs that offers cognitive games and personalized daily workouts targeting memory, attention, problem solving, flexibility, and processing speed. The service adapts difficulty to individual performance, tracks progress over time, and is delivered through the web and iOS/Android mobile apps. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners, the company was surfaced through VC-portfolio discovery; probing its public surface found no developer portal, public API, or documented programmatic integration — it is a direct-to-consumer product with no API surface at this time.

providers.name: Pop.in
providers.description: Pop.in is a consumer social gaming platform that connects people through real-time multiplayer games including Spades, Hearts, Dominoes, Liar's Dice, crosswords, Pop Quiz trivia, and Just Chatting. Delivered as iOS and Android apps plus a web play surface at play.pop.in, the service reports over 100M downloads and 20M active users with a 4.75+ average rating. The company is backed by 500 Global and was surfaced through its portfolio; it operates a purely consumer-facing product and publishes no public developer, API, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Sira Medical
providers.description: Sira Medical develops augmented reality software that transforms 3D radiological imaging into patient-specific holographic models projected onto real-world backgrounds. Delivered through head-mounted AR devices (such as Microsoft HoloLens) and mobile platforms, the technology helps surgeons perform preoperative planning with greater confidence, clinicians educate patients with understandable visualizations, medical schools train students on patient-specific anatomy, and medical-device makers design and validate implants. The company is backed by 500 Global, Eileses Capital, UCSF Innovation Ventures, and Microsoft for Startups. Sira Medical operates as a clinical AR software vendor and does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public identity, legal, and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Underdog Fantasy
providers.description: Underdog (Underdog Sports, formerly Underdog Fantasy) is a Brooklyn, New York based sports gaming company founded in 2020 by Jeremy Levine that operates daily fantasy sports, pick'em, and — since 2025 — federally regulated sports prediction markets on its own proprietary technology stack. Its consumer products include Classic Pick'em, Pick'em Champions, Best Ball and other Draft Games, Streaks, Team Picks, and the Underdog Predict prediction-markets exchange, delivered through iOS, Android, and web apps rather than a public developer API. Underdog reached roughly $500M in annual revenue within five years, was valued at $1.2B after a Spark Capital-led Series C in March 2025, acquired CFTC-registered derivatives infrastructure in March 2026, and in July 2026 was the subject of a proposed acquisition by IG Group. The company publishes no developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract; its public technical surface is limited to an RFC 9116 security.txt with a PGP key, a Honeybadger-hosted status page covering its API and Stats services, and the Underdog-Inc GitHub organization.

providers.name: L'Oréal
providers.description: L'Oréal is the world's largest cosmetics and beauty company, producing skincare, makeup, haircare, and fragrance products. The group operates a portfolio of over 35 brands, including Lancôme, Maybelline, Garnier, NYX Professional Makeup, Kérastase, La Roche-Posay, and Kiehl's, sold in over 150 countries. L'Oréal's primary developer surface is the ModiFace platform (a wholly owned subsidiary), which exposes an AR virtual try-on SDK and API for partner brands and retailers. L'Oréal Group itself does not operate a general-purpose corporate developer portal.

providers.name: Gen.G
providers.description: Gen.G is a global esports organization founded in 2017 (originally KSV eSports) that connects the United States and Asia, operating from Los Angeles, Seoul, and Shanghai. It fields professional teams across League of Legends, Valorant, PUBG, Counter-Strike 2, Rocket League, Fortnite, Brawl Stars, Honor of Kings, Mobile Legends, NBA 2K, Overwatch, Rainbow Six Siege, and EA FC, and runs a youth esports academy program alongside merchandise and fan-engagement businesses. Backed by Canaan Partners among other investors, Gen.G was valued at roughly $250 million as of 2022. It is a consumer esports brand and merchandise operator with a Shopify-based storefront; it publishes no public developer API, so this profile carries company identity only.

providers.name: Health Scholars
providers.description: Health Scholars — which rebranded to UpSkillAI in 2025 and now trades at upskillai.com — builds AI-powered extended reality (XR/VR) simulation training for mission-critical, hands-on work in healthcare, emergency medical services, stroke assessment and defense. The platform pairs voice-driven VR simulations with simulation management and readiness reporting, letting hospital systems, first responders and government programs run standardized protocol training on headsets without instructors or extra equipment. Customers reach it through a hosted web console at app.upskillai.com. The company publishes no public developer program: there is no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, SDK, webhook catalog or public pricing. The production backend behind its own application (api.upskillai.com, with the legacy AWS API Gateway host api.healthscholars.com) is private and rejects unauthenticated requests.

providers.name: Draxon
providers.description: Draxon is a Berlin-based company (founded 2025, backed by HV Capital and Point Nine) that provides IATA-certified virtual reality training for airport ground handling operations. The platform ships pre-configured Meta Quest VR headsets and an immersive training library covering ramp equipment such as belt loaders, tractors, pushback tugs, GPUs and towable stairs, plus safety procedures and hand signals for frontline ramp personnel. Its Trainer Hub delivers automated, IATA-compliant certification tracking with self-paced or instructor-led modules. Draxon operates as a B2B SaaS training provider and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: EyeLights
providers.description: EyeLights is a French deep-tech company building augmented reality head-up display (HUD) technology for riders and pilots. Its products project GPS navigation, speed, intercom, radar and call information into the rider's line of sight: EyeRide, a universal HUD accessory compatible with any motorcycle helmet; the GT-AIR 3 Smart, an integrated head-up display visor built into a SHOEI helmet; the APEX HUD glasses for general aviation; and Pulse Ultra, a universal Bluetooth intercom. The company sells direct-to-consumer through a Shopify storefront at eye-lights.com and runs customer support on Odoo. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio lead; EyeLights publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time, so this record captures its consumer web, identity, and security posture rather than an API contract.

providers.name: 8th Wall
providers.description: 8th Wall is a web-based augmented reality (WebAR) platform originally founded in 2016 and acquired by Niantic in March 2022. Following Niantic's 2025 sale of its gaming division to Scopely and the spin-off of Niantic Spatial, Inc. as an independent geospatial AI and XR company, 8th Wall's hosted cloud editor, login, and Niantic Studio services were retired on February 28, 2026 and the platform transitioned to a free, open-source distribution model. Existing published 8th Wall experiences continue to run through February 28, 2027. The 8th Wall stack centers on the XR Engine — a SLAM-based WebAR runtime providing World Tracking, Image Targets, Face Effects, Sky Segmentation, and World Effects — exposed to developers as a TypeScript/JavaScript SDK that integrates with A-Frame, three.js, PlayCanvas, and Babylon.js. The Distributed Engine Binary (released January 2026) ships SLAM under a binary-only license for commercial and noncommercial use, while the surrounding framework, utilities, and example projects are MIT-licensed on the 8thwall GitHub organization. 8th Wall Studio (formerly Niantic Studio) is a real-time visual editor and game engine for authoring 3D and XR experiences that can be deployed to any web host. 8th Wall does not publish a public REST or HTTP API; the developer surface is a client-side JavaScript SDK plus command-line and utility tooling distributed through GitHub.

providers.name: Lil Snack
providers.description: Lil Snack is a Manhattan Beach, California games company, founded in 2024, that builds "snackable" daily games and party games — short pop-culture puzzle, word, and trivia titles that refresh every day. It runs its own consumer destination at lilsnack.com (Clue Daily, Scattergories Daily, Swap, DownWords, Pickle, Lite Brite Daily, Wheel of Fortune TODAY, Quiz Climb, Venn, Chain, and more) and also powers games embedded inside partner consumer platforms, citing BuzzFeed, FOX, Hasbro, the Los Angeles Times, Netflix, Peacock, Prime Gaming, Reddit, and Sony. The company reports 40M+ games played and 10M+ players all-time, and monetizes through platform partnerships, sponsorships, and brand licensing. As of this profile Lil Snack publishes NO public developer surface — no API, no documentation portal, no SDKs, no public GitHub organization, and no /.well-known documents; its partner game integrations are arranged through business development rather than self-serve APIs. This API Evangelist profile therefore captures verified company identity, web properties, and probed domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Saphlux
providers.description: Saphlux is a quantum dot Micro-LED (QD-MLED) display technology company founded in 2014 out of Yale University and headquartered in San Diego, California, with additional operations in China and Japan. It commercialized semi-polar (20-21) GaN-on-sapphire epitaxial wafers to address efficiency droop and the green gap in nitride emitters, and now mass-produces NPQD quantum-dot Micro-LED devices. Its product lineup spans QD-COB and QD-COB Pro Series panels for large-format commercial and home-theater displays and the T-Series monolithic full-color micro-displays for all-day wearable AR eyewear and AI smart glasses. Saphlux is a semiconductor materials and display-module manufacturer that sells hardware to OEMs and display integrators; it publishes no public developer program, API, or SDK.

providers.name: World Golf Tour
providers.description: World Golf Tour (WGT Golf), operated by World Golf Tour, LLC out of San Francisco, is a free-to-play online golf simulation launched in 2008 that recreates more than twenty real championship courses like Pebble Beach, St Andrews, and Bethpage Black using photorealistic imagery, played by over 15 million players on web, iOS, and Android, with virtual equipment from Callaway, Titleist, and TaylorMade and integrations with SkyTrak launch monitors. The company is a Battery Ventures portfolio company and publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Pocket Gems
providers.description: Pocket Gems is a San Francisco mobile games and interactive entertainment studio founded in 2009, employing over 200 people and backed by Sequoia Capital and Tencent. It builds and operates the Episode interactive-storytelling network, Episode XOXO, and the 3D real-time strategy title War Dragons on its proprietary mobile-first Mantis Engine, with products downloaded more than 325 million times. Pocket Gems ships consumer mobile applications rather than a developer-facing API program: there is no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification. Its public developer surface is a GitHub organization and four first-party Apache-2.0 Node.js libraries published to npm under the @pocketgems scope (the internal "Todea" service stack), plus an Episode Writer's Portal used by story authors.

providers.name: Wooga
providers.description: Wooga is a Berlin-based mobile game developer founded in 2009 and a subsidiary of Playtika, specializing in story-driven casual games such as June's Journey, Ghost Detective and Pearl's Peril. Wooga publishes no public API or developer portal, but maintains an active open-source GitHub organization with its atlas Gradle plugin suite for Unity and mobile build automation, published to the Gradle Plugin Portal and RubyGems. Surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of balderton-capital and hv-capital.

providers.name: Upsight
providers.description: Upsight was a mobile analytics and marketing platform for apps and games — positioning itself as a "user lifecycle management platform" combining omnichannel analytics, integrated web and mobile marketing, ad optimization, and a DataMine SQL analytics product behind a single SDK for iOS, Android, tvOS, Unity, and Web. A Battery Ventures portfolio company, the platform is now defunct - upsight.com no longer resolves, the help.upsight.com developer docs survive only in the Internet Archive, and the GitHub org has been dormant since 2020, though the UpsightKit CocoaPods SDK and the doctor PyPI package remain published.

providers.name: Poker Skill
providers.description: Poker Skill is a mobile-first poker-training app for iOS and Android that turns learning poker into a daily habit. It teaches through interactive puzzles, bite-sized guided lessons, and daily practice reps that adapt to the player's skill level, from complete beginner to serious improver. At its core is "Showdown AI", a versioned game-theory engine that deals practice hands, plays the opponents, and grades every decision by its expected value — an approach the company says replicates the methods behind Pluribus, the first AI to beat top professionals at six-max no-limit hold'em. The product is subscription-funded with a free-to-start funnel, and is backed by Initialized Capital. Poker Skill is a consumer application and does not publish a public developer API program.

providers.name: The Meta
providers.description: The Meta is the gaming-performance company behind KovaaK's Aim Trainer (formerly "Kovaak 2.0: The Meta"), a PC esports training platform distributed on Steam that pairs guided, skill-specific training modules with Kovaak's Sandbox aim trainer and its library of 2,600+ user-generated scenarios. The platform lets FPS players measure, diagnose, and improve their mechanical aim and in-game habits, feeding back insights on weaknesses so players can target their practice. Founded by Duncan Haberly, Jay Brown, and Chris Olson and backed by Canaan (Beta Fund), Village Global, Courtside VC, betaworks, GFR, and Akatsuki Entertainment Technology (AET Fund). The Meta operates a consumer game product, a community wiki, and a Discord community; it does not currently publish a public first-party developer API.

providers.name: Tripledot
providers.description: Tripledot Studios (Tripledot Group) is a London-headquartered mobile games developer and publisher focused on data-driven casual games, with chart-topping titles including Woodoku, Solitaire, Duplica, Wordhop, Solitaire Scapes, Sudoku, Spider Solitaire and Blackjack played by more than 25 million daily active users. Founded as an independent studio and named Best Developer at the Pocket Gamer Mobile Games Awards 2023, Tripledot closed an $800 million acquisition of AppLovin's mobile games studio portfolio (ten studios) on July 1, 2025, and is backed by investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners. Tripledot publishes no first-party developer API, portal or SDKs, but its website ships a real llms.txt and a live, publicly connectable MCP endpoint (the Wix Site Visitor Assistant) for agentic access to site content.

providers.name: Alta VR
providers.description: Alta VR (legally Another Axiom LLC) is a virtual reality game studio behind Gorilla Tag, one of the most-played VR titles ever, and the newer social VR world Orion Drift. The studio builds imaginative, physics-driven multiplayer experiences centered on hand-based locomotion and social play across Meta Quest, Steam, and other VR platforms. It runs an Another Axiom Creator Program for community map-building and content creation, and publishes game code and Unity map-export tooling through its public GitHub organization. Alta VR is a portfolio company of a16z. As a VR consumer game studio it does not currently operate a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK program; its developer-facing surface is limited to open-source game code, custom map tooling, and creator resources.

providers.name: Draftea
providers.description: Draftea is a Mexico-based daily fantasy sports and real-money sports gaming platform, billed as the first daily fantasy sports (DFS) product for the Spanish-speaking world. Fans draft lineups of real athletes across soccer, American football (via an NFL partnership), basketball, baseball, and Formula 1, enter paid contests, and compete against other users for cash prizes rather than against a bookmaker. The company operates in Mexico under regulatory approval (DGAJS/SCEVF/P-06/2005-TER), distributes through native iOS and Android apps, and is backed by Sequoia, Kaszek, Bullpen Capital, Stepstone Group, and Courtside Ventures, along with athlete investors. Draftea is a consumer product company and does not currently publish a public developer API program; this profile captures its public web, support, legal, and open-source engineering surface.

providers.name: Gankster
providers.description: Gankster is a consumer competitive-gaming social platform — a web and mobile "looking for group" (LFG) network that helps players team up, practice, and compete across titles including Valorant, League of Legends, Dota 2, Counter-Strike 2, Rocket League, Fortnite, and World of Warcraft. It matches players by rank, playstyle, and reputation to find duos, five-stacks, and fill players, and lets teams organize scrims, tournaments, and recruitment. Gankster operates entirely outside the game client (no overlays or client modifications) and ships the Gankster Duos mobile app on iOS and Android. The company is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and raised $4.25M for its all-in-one competitive gaming platform. Gankster does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: InfiniGods
providers.description: InfiniGods is a gaming studio building fun, free-to-play, Web3-powered mobile games centered around ancient mythologies. Its titles — Immortal Siege, King of Destiny, and InfiniMerge — share interoperable gaming assets, items, power-ups, and currencies that span the InfiniGods Universe (IGU). Players collect blockchain assets such as the Elder Gods (a 4,488-piece Gen 0 NFT collection that unlocks abilities and boosts scoring across all titles) and the InfiniPass VIP membership (early access, bonus play, exclusive NFT drops, and in-game boosts). The company is backed by Pantera Capital. InfiniGods is a consumer game studio with no public developer/API program; this profile captures its public web, legal, community, and code-org surface.

providers.name: Kidas
providers.description: Kidas is a Techstars-backed trust-and-safety company that builds white-label scam detection and online-protection solutions for enterprises and consumers. Its ProtectMe platform monitors PC gaming and Discord voice and text channels for cyberbullying, predators, phishing, and scams, and its broader suite adds SMS scam detection, email protection, a scam-screening chatbot, and deepfake/impersonation defense that integrate into existing customer channels. Kidas markets custom builds and lists Aura, Comcast, Overwolf, Razer, Walmart, Intel, and Best Buy among its customers. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface is published as of this profile.

providers.name: Squint
providers.description: Squint is a Manufacturing Intelligence platform that uses AI and augmented reality to help industrial and frontline operations teams lower downtime and improve quality at scale. Its mobile app captures and digitizes tribal knowledge from video and real work, orchestrates workflows and work assignments across employees and locations, provides AI-powered troubleshooting and expert guidance, and delivers analytics on performance across teams and sites. Founded by Devin Bhushan, Squint began in manufacturing and serves automotive, food and beverage, oil and gas, heavy industrials, equipment, consumer packaged goods, and energy customers, expanding into healthcare and hospitality. Backed by Menlo Ventures. As of this enrichment pass Squint exposes no public developer API; its documentation and application are gated behind a Squint workspace login.

providers.name: Statespace
providers.description: Statespace is the company behind Aimlabs (aimlabs.com, formerly statespace.gg), the leading AI-powered aim-training platform for FPS gamers. Aimlabs delivers personalized training tasks, real-time performance analytics, and game-specific tools, serving over 40 million players and operating as an official partner of Valorant and Rainbow Six Siege. Statespace is venture-backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and Lux Capital. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a consumer web/desktop product but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: Audiomob
providers.description: Audiomob is an in-game and in-app audio advertising platform that lets mobile game and app publishers monetize their titles with non-interruptive, skippable and rewarded audio ads while advertisers reach engaged gaming audiences at scale. Publishers integrate through the Audiomob Unity plugin or native iOS and Android SDKs (plus a community React Native adapter), add their games to the Audiomob developer dashboard, and configure ad units, an Ad Availability API, and server-to-server webhooks for reward and event tracking. The platform is Open Measurement (IAB Tech Lab) compliant, supports consent management via OneTrust and Sourcepoint, exposes Impression Level Revenue Data (ILRD), and integrates with mediation partners such as AdMob and LevelPlay (MAX) and mobile measurement partners including Adjust, Singular and Tenjin. The current SDK line is SDK 10. Audiomob is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners.

providers.name: B612
providers.description: B612 is a consumer selfie and beauty camera application for iOS and Android, published globally by SNOW Corporation and operated in mainland China as B612咔叽 (B612 Kaji) by Yiruike Information Technology (Beijing) Co., Ltd. The app combines a real-time beauty camera, AR stickers and scene effects, user-created and creator-published filters, and photo and video editing tools, and has been distributed through the Apple App Store and Google Play since 2014. B612 is a mobile end-user product rather than an API provider: as of this enrichment pass the company publishes no developer portal, no public API documentation, no SDKs, and no machine-readable API artifacts on any of its web properties.

providers.name: dreamgames
providers.description: Dream Games is a mobile gaming developer with offices in Istanbul and London that builds high-quality, long-lifecycle casual puzzle games, best known for Royal Match and Royal Kingdom. The company combines technology and creativity to produce polished match-3 titles played by tens of millions of players worldwide, and it was surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital. Dream Games operates as a consumer game publisher rather than an API provider: it publishes no public developer portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, or programmatic API surface. This profile therefore captures the company's real public web, legal, and security surface (website, terms, privacy, careers, help center, and a published security.txt) rather than developer artifacts.

providers.name: Playsome
providers.description: Playsome (Playsome Ltd. / Playsome Oy) is a Helsinki, Finland mobile game studio that builds free-to-play games combining deep gameplay with polished visuals under the philosophy of making "big games with a small team". Its flagship title is Friends & Dragons, a cooperative multiplayer puzzle-RPG for iOS and Android featuring 150+ collectible heroes and 700+ puzzles and dungeons. The company is backed by gaming-focused venture firms Play Ventures and EQT. Playsome does not publish a traditional developer API, but its Wix-hosted website exposes a live Wix Site MCP endpoint for agentic AI access, letting agents retrieve business details, search the site, and start bookings/purchases without scraping.

providers.name: Red 6
providers.description: Red 6 (Red Six Aerospace, Inc.) is a defense technology company founded in 2018 that builds outdoor, high-speed augmented reality for military aviation training. Its flagship product, ATARS (Advanced Tactical Augmented Reality System), pairs the EVE (Enhanced Visual Environment) helmet-mounted display — 160-degree field of view, 18,000 nits, 10ms latency, full color — with an AI-driven multiplayer network so real pilots in real aircraft can fly and maneuver against synthetically generated adversaries in real time, in daylight. A companion system, ARCADE (Augmented Reality Command and Analytic Data Environment), handles mission planning, briefing and three-dimensional debrief. ATARS has been integrated or trialed on the USAF F-16 and MC-130, the RAF Hawk T-2, Boeing's AH-64E Apache CATT, and the Lockheed Martin / Korea Aerospace Industries T-50/TF-50. Red 6 is ISO 9001:2015 and AS9100D certified. It publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract — its software surface is delivered through defense programs and OEM integrations rather than a self-serve developer platform.

providers.name: AltspaceVR
providers.description: AltspaceVR was a social virtual reality platform founded in 2013 where people gathered in shared 3D spaces for live events, meetups, classes, comedy shows and conferences. Google Ventures (GV) was an early investor. Microsoft acquired the company in 2017 and folded it into its Mixed Reality division, then announced in January 2023 that the platform would close, shutting it down permanently on 2023-03-10 in favor of Microsoft Mesh. AltspaceVR published no hosted HTTP API; its developer surface was the Mixed Reality Extension (MRE) SDK for building server-hosted 3D world extensions in Node.js, plus the earlier web-based AltspaceSDK. Every SDK repository is now archived and altvr.com redirects to microsoft.com. This profile is retained as a historical record of a terminated platform, not as a live integration target.

providers.name: Lilith Games
providers.description: Lilith Games (上海莉莉丝网络科技有限公司) is a Shanghai-headquartered video game developer and publisher founded in 2013, known for globally distributed mobile and PC titles including Rise of Kingdoms (万国觉醒), AFK Arena (剑与远征), AFK Journey (剑与远征：启程), Farlight 84 (远光84), Warpath (战火勋章), Art of Conquest (剑与家园) and a portfolio of indie games. The company operates as a consumer game publisher rather than an API platform: it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or partner API program. Its public engineering surface is the LilithGames GitHub organization, which open-sources backend and build infrastructure (Go networking and reverse-proxy tooling, build caching, Perforce virtual file system work) rather than client SDKs for a Lilith API. Surfaced as a portfolio company of IDG Capital.

providers.name: Ubiquity6
providers.description: Ubiquity6 was a San Francisco augmented-reality startup ("Capture & Edit Reality") backed by Benchmark, First Round, and Index Ventures. It built Display.land, a multiplayer 3D/AR/VR capture and creation platform, acquired Wavy AR, and was acquired by Discord in June 2021, after which its products were discontinued. Ubiquity6 never published a public API or developer program; its GitHub organization survives as a set of open-source computer vision and React Native forks, and a few internal packages remain on npm under the @ubiquity6 scope.

providers.name: Prisms VR
providers.description: Prisms VR (Prisms) is an educational technology company building what it calls the world's first spatial learning platform, where students learn core math, science, and other subjects by abstracting up from immersive, first-person physical experiences delivered in virtual reality. Founded by MIT engineer-turned-educator Anurupa Ganguly, the teacher-facing platform uses kinesthetic, embodied learning to help students grasp abstract concepts and aims to develop curious, resilient thinkers. Prisms is an a16z portfolio company; it was added to the API Evangelist network as a lead and profiled through the enrichment pipeline. As of this pass the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal surface.

providers.name: Crystal Dynamics
providers.description: Crystal Dynamics is a AAA video game development studio, best known as the home of the Tomb Raider franchise and its Lara Croft character, and part of the Embracer Group.
