The studio publishes a consumer-facing marketing website, careers portal, player support center, and news/community hub, but exposes no public developer API program, API documentation, developer portal, or SDKs. This profile entered the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio stub lead; enrichment confirms there is no public API surface to catalog at this time.

providers.name: Ergatta
providers.description: Ergatta is a connected-fitness company that makes game-based home rowing machines, pairing WaterRower-derived water-resistance hardware handcrafted in Rhode Island with a gamified software platform of interactive challenges (Endeavor, Meteor, Wavelength), live and on-demand races, scenic rows, coached classes, and custom workouts. Ergatta sells the Luxe and Lite rowers plus upgrade kits for existing WaterRower and Concept2 machines, delivered through a Shopify-hosted direct-to-consumer storefront with a membership subscription. Ergatta does not publish a public developer API; this API Evangelist profile captures its public web surface and identity for network discovery.

providers.name: Hutch Games
providers.description: Hutch Games (Hutch) is a mobile game development studio founded in London with additional studios in Dundee, Scotland and Nova Scotia, Canada. Hutch specializes in free-to-play mobile driving and car games, developing and publishing titles including F1 Clash, Top Drives, and Matchcreek Motors. The studio was surfaced as a portfolio company of Index Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. As a consumer mobile game publisher, Hutch does not currently expose a public developer API or developer program; this profile captures the company identity, public web properties, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Jam City
providers.description: Jam City is a Culver City, California mobile entertainment company founded in 2010 by MySpace co-founders Chris DeWolfe and Aber Whitcomb (with Josh Yguado), now led by CEO Simon Sim. It develops and publishes free-to-play mobile games across puzzle, casual and narrative RPG genres — including the Cookie Jam and Panda Pop franchises and licensed titles such as Harry Potter: Hogwarts Mystery, Disney Emoji Blitz and Family Guy: The Quest for Stuff — built with partners including Disney and Warner Bros. Games. The company reports over $4 billion in aggregate lifetime bookings and nearly 1.5 billion downloads across studios in Los Angeles, Burbank, San Diego, San Francisco, Buenos Aires, Montevideo and Toronto. Jam City is a consumer games publisher: it distributes through the Apple App Store and Google Play and, as of this profile, publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Kabam
providers.description: Kabam is a mobile game developer and publisher founded in 2006 and headquartered in Vancouver, Canada, operating as a wholly owned subsidiary of Netmarble. The studio builds free-to-play multiplayer titles for iOS and Android, best known for Marvel Contest of Champions, alongside Shop Titans, Transformers Forged to Fight, King Arthur Legends, and past titles such as Disney Mirrorverse and Fast & Furious games. Kabam operates studios and offices across Vancouver, Montreal, Charlottetown, Los Angeles, San Francisco, Austin, and Seoul. Kabam publishes no public developer program, API reference, or SDK surface; this profile captures its public web, legal, and support properties plus a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: Mobile Premier League
providers.description: Mobile Premier League (MPL) is a mobile skill-gaming and esports platform founded in 2018 and headquartered in Bengaluru, India, operated by Galactus Funware Technology. It distributes a catalog of casual, card, board and fantasy-sports titles inside a single app and runs tournaments and contests around them, reporting more than 100 million registered users across Asia, Europe and North America. MPL historically ran a game-developer program — a Developer Dashboard and a publish-and-monetize SDK at developer.mpl.live, documented at docs.developer.mpl.live — that let third-party studios ship a single build to the MPL app under a revenue-share agreement. That program's hosts no longer resolve, and MPL publishes no public REST, GraphQL, MCP or event API today. Following India's Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025, MPL discontinued real-money gaming in India; www.mplgames.com is the live consumer surface, principally serving the United States.

providers.name: Odyssey Interactive
providers.description: Odyssey Interactive is an independent game development studio focused on building free-to-play, cross-platform, competitive titles set in bright, hopeful, anime-inspired IP. The studio is best known for Omega Strikers, a free-to-play competitive arena game, and its mission is to "ignite the spark of competitiveness that lives within everyone" by creating community-driven games with longevity. Odyssey Interactive was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the studio publishes no public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal — its public surface is its marketing site, a Verified Creators program, downloadable game asset kits, and a Zendesk-hosted player support center. This profile captures the studio's identity and verified public links.

providers.name: Pokelabo
providers.description: Pokelabo (ポケラボ) is a Japanese mobile game development studio founded in 2007 and headquartered in Tokyo. Originally an independent social-game maker, it became a subsidiary of GREE and, as of January 1, 2025, was integrated into WFS (Wright Flyer Studios) under the GREE group. The studio develops and operates smartphone games built on licensed and original intellectual properties, including titles such as SINoALICE and Magia Exedra (Puella Magi Madoka Magica). Pokelabo is a consumer entertainment company and does not expose a public developer API; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: PortalOne
providers.description: PortalOne is a hybrid gaming platform that blends mobile games with live, interactive television-style entertainment, letting players compete inside shows and classic titles such as Atari's Breakout. Operated by PortalOne AS (Norway) and PortalOne, Inc. (United States), the company delivers its experience through native iOS and Android apps rather than a public developer platform. It is a consumer-facing entertainment product backed by Seedcamp and other venture investors; as of this profile PortalOne publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: Resolution Games
providers.description: Resolution Games is a Stockholm-based studio building games for virtual, augmented, and mixed reality platforms including Meta Quest, Apple Vision Pro, and PlayStation VR. Its titles include Demeo, Spatial Ops, Blaston, Bait!, and Ultimechs. The company is venture-backed (Creandum, GV, Partech) and runs a consumer-facing games business. It publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this API Evangelist profile tracks its public web properties (blog, support, legal pages) for discovery and enrichment.

providers.name: Rosebud AI
providers.description: Rosebud AI is an AI-powered game creation platform that lets anyone build and deploy playable 3D games and interactive worlds from natural-language prompts, a workflow the company calls "Vibe Coding" — you describe scenes, rules, and behaviors and an AI assistant named "Rosie" writes and applies the underlying JavaScript. The platform runs on a custom engine designed for AI-era game development, featuring deterministic WASM-based physics, native real-time multiplayer, instant link-based sharing, and a built-in "Juice API" for camera effects, particle systems, and spatial audio. Founded in 2019 in San Francisco by CEO Lisha Li (Ph.D. in machine learning, UC Berkeley), Rosebud AI is backed by a16z. As of this enrichment pass the company ships a hosted consumer product and publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK packages, MCP server, or developer portal.

providers.name: Sandbox VR
providers.description: Sandbox VR is a location-based virtual reality entertainment company operating full-body, free-roam VR experiences for groups of friends, families, and corporate teams across 60+ venues in North America, Europe, and Asia. Guests play social, multiplayer VR adventures — horror, action, sports, and family-friendly titles including licensed properties — using motion-tracked suits and headsets. The business spans company-owned and franchised locations, online booking, gift cards, parties/events, and an unlimited-pass subscription. Backed by a16z and Craft Ventures. Sandbox VR is a consumer entertainment operator and, as of this profile, publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation; this record captures the company identity and its public web/security posture.

providers.name: Splash
providers.description: Splash is an AI music-creation platform building games and tools for a new generation of creators. Developed by the team formerly known as Popgun AI, it has built proprietary generative-audio technology and high-quality music datasets since 2017, powering features such as Text-to-Singing, Text-to-Rap, and Generative Text-to-Music. Splash's consumer products include the Splash beat-maker app for iOS and Android, SPLASH on Roblox, the WeMix collaborative music experience, and KAIMIX. The company is backed by Khosla Ventures, Techstars, the Alexa Fund, Bitkraft, King River Capital, and Mawson. Splash publishes no public developer API or documentation surface at this time; this profile captures its public web identity in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Super Evil
providers.description: Super Evil (Super Evil Megacorp) is an award-winning independent video game studio building shared, cross-platform gaming experiences that push creative and technical boundaries. The studio is best known for the MOBA Vainglory and the shooter Catalyst Black, and has shipped licensed titles including TMNT: Splintered Fate and a Rebel Moon game (Blood Line). Surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the studio publishes only a consumer marketing website (Gatsby/Netlify) and social channels; it exposes no public developer API, documentation, SDK, OpenAPI, developer portal, or status page.

providers.name: Super Evil Megacorp
providers.description: Super Evil Megacorp is an award-winning independent video game studio building shared, cross-platform gaming experiences that push creative and technical boundaries. Founded in 2012, the studio is best known for the mobile MOBA Vainglory and has since shipped titles including Catalyst Black, TMNT Splintered Fate, and Blood Line - Rebel Moon, developed on its own in-house game engine. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and Index Ventures; it is a consumer games studio and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Tactile Games
providers.description: Tactile Games is a Danish mobile game studio headquartered in Copenhagen, founded in 2014, that builds and publishes casual free-to-play puzzle titles for iOS and Android. Its portfolio includes Lily's Garden, Penny & Flo, Makeover Match, the Cookie Cats series (Cookie Cats, Cookie Cats Pop, Cookie Cats Blast), and the Simon's Cat games. Tactile is a portfolio company of Index Ventures. It is a consumer game publisher rather than an API producer: it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal, so this profile captures the company identity, public web properties, and domain-security posture surfaced by the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Voldex
providers.description: Voldex (Voldex Entertainment) is a game developer and publisher founded in 2015 that acquires, operates, and grows platform-leading games on Roblox, including Brookhaven, Driving Empire, and NFL Universe Football, collectively reaching over 140 million monthly players. Its stated mission is to "bring people together through fun," pursuing a focused strategy of selectively acquiring and stewarding enduring Roblox experiences rather than broad portfolio expansion. Voldex publishes no public developer API, SDK, CLI, or API documentation surface — it is a consumer games studio whose products run inside the Roblox platform. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio company; it was reviewed by the enrichment pipeline and confirmed to have no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Volley
providers.description: Volley is a San Francisco voice-AI entertainment company, backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, that builds voice-controlled and connected-TV games. Its catalog includes hits such as Song Quiz, Yes Sire, and officially licensed titles like Jeopardy!, Wheel of Fortune, and Family Feud, playable on Amazon Alexa, Google Assistant, Roku, Fire TV, LG, and Samsung TVs. The company is rebranding its consumer surface as "Weekend." Volley operates as a consumer entertainment product studio and does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity and public web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: ForeVR
providers.description: ForeVR Games is a consumer virtual-reality game studio that brings classic social bar and backyard games into VR. Its catalog includes ForeVR Bowl, ForeVR Darts, ForeVR Pool, and ForeVR Cornhole, built for multiplayer play across Meta Quest, Steam VR, and PlayStation VR2. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network. ForeVR is a consumer game publisher with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation program; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Maya
providers.description: A collection of APIs for Maya, the popular 3D animation and modeling software developed by Autodesk, providing scripting and plugin development capabilities through Python, C++, MEL, and .NET interfaces.

providers.name: Playco
providers.description: Playco is an instant-play gaming company founded in 2020 by Justin Waldron, Michael Carter, Takeshi Otsuka and Teddy Cross, headquartered in Tokyo with teams worldwide. It builds HTML5 games that run inside social and communication platforms without an app install — EverWing on Facebook, Snake Squad on Snap Games, Heads Up! for Zoom, Sway Stories on TikTok and Trip Royale on LINE — and reached unicorn status on a $100M Series A. Its technology stack, described on play.co/tech, is developer tooling rather than a public web API: PixiJS (the open-source HTML5 rendering/creation engine it acquired with Goodboy Digital in 2021), Odie3D (a 3D extension framework), GCInstant (a client-side JavaScript library wrapping platform SDKs and analytics) and Replicant (a backend-as-a-service state manager for instant games). Playco publishes no developer portal, no API reference and no machine-readable contract; its public code surface is the play-co GitHub organization, which is the renamed Game Closure organization and carries the legacy devkit HTML5 game platform, js.io and ff.

providers.name: ProbablyMonsters
providers.description: ProbablyMonsters Inc. is an independent video game company headquartered in Bellevue, Washington, with a second location in Fort Worth, Texas. Founded in 2016 by former Bungie CEO Harold Ryan, it operates as a parent company that founds, funds and incubates development teams building AAA and AA interactive entertainment — publishing titles including Crimson Moon, Storm Lancers, IRE: A Prologue and Nekome. ProbablyMonsters sells finished games to players through console and PC storefronts; it is not a platform or developer-tools business. It publishes no developer program, no public API, no SDK and no machine-readable API description, and its GitHub organization carries zero public repositories. This profile records that absence with the probes behind it.

providers.name: Sanlo
providers.description: Sanlo is a multi-platform payments and monetization platform built specifically for game developers and studios. Its products let studios run live ops and accept payments outside the walled gardens of the major app stores to reduce platform commission fees: Webshop Builder (a full-stack direct-to-consumer web shop), Web Checkout (accept payments on any website, web shop, or web game), and Unity Checkout (native iOS/Android in-game checkout for Unity titles via a first-party SDK and API, with one-click checkout, fully customizable UI, and creator-code support). Card and payment collection is powered by Adyen underneath. Sanlo also offers game funding to help studios finance user acquisition and growth. The company is backed by Index Ventures and other gaming-focused investors.

providers.name: Animoca Brands
providers.description: Animoca Brands is a Web3 company focused on advancing digital property rights and building the open metaverse through blockchain technology, gaming, and digital assets. Founded in Hong Kong, the company operates a portfolio of consumer products including The Sandbox, Moca Network (digital identity), Open Campus (education), and Anichess, alongside institutional offerings such as Anchorpoint Financial (stablecoins and real-world assets) and NUVA (treasury management). Animoca Brands is also one of the most active investors in Web3, backing 600+ builders across gaming, infrastructure, real-world assets, and digital-ownership platforms. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of the SoftBank Vision Fund and added to the API Evangelist network; Animoca operates primarily as a holding and investment company and does not publish a first-party public developer API.

providers.name: Antimatter Systems
providers.description: Antimatter Systems is an education technology company building a peer-to-peer learning network where students demonstrate mastery by making memes, puzzles, and games rather than by writing essays or sitting tests. Founded by Jonathan Libov, the company raised a $2M seed round led by Version One Ventures in 2023, joined by Spacecadet, Ordinary Holdings, Haystack and Compound. Its classroom product lets teachers create meme-based activities with deadlines and instructions, invite students by shareable link, moderate submissions, restrict learners to view-only, work from a library of pre-approved templates, catch unedited-image uploads with plagiarism detection, and grade every submission in one place; the company states it should be free for schools. Antimatter also ships a Sorcerer AI instructional coach plus the consumer Antimatter: Creator and Antimatter: Universe iOS apps. The platform runs on the web at playantimatter.com. As of July 2026 the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications.

providers.name: Peak
providers.description: Peak is a consumer brain-training mobile application operated by Synaptic Labs (formerly Peak Labs) that offers cognitive exercise games and personalized workouts spanning memory, attention, problem-solving, mental agility, language, and emotion. Its games and Advanced Training Programmes are developed with researchers from institutions including Cambridge, Yale, UCL, and King's College London. Peak Pro is a subscription that unlocks 40+ games, personalized workouts, performance analytics, and an AI Coach. Peak is a mobile-only consumer product distributed via the App Store and Google Play and does not currently publish a public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Sett AI
providers.description: Sett AI is a creative performance AI platform for mobile game user acquisition (UA), offering "agentic AI" that helps game studios and performance-marketing teams research, generate, analyze, and deploy video and playable ad creatives at scale to combat creative fatigue. Sett agents connect to ad networks (Meta, Google, AppLovin, Unity, Mintegral) and MMP data to ideate concepts, generate playables and videos, and analyze creative performance. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners; the company raised a Series B bringing total funding to $57M. Sett operates a marketing and product website but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface as of this profiling.

providers.name: Tyffon
providers.description: Tyffon Inc. is a Japanese immersive entertainment company that combines creativity and technology to deliver memorable XR experiences. The studio builds VR, AR, and mixed-reality attractions - including Corridor, Kaiju Haven VR, Floria, and Island Mirrorge MR - operates the Tyffonium attraction brand, licenses its XR content to entertainment venues across Japan, and released the GARA AR platform app. A Techstars portfolio company, Tyffon publishes no public developer portal or API surface as of July 2026.

providers.name: Tap
providers.description: TAP (Training All People, Inc.) is a next-generation technician training platform for advanced and precision manufacturers. TAP combines online courses (pneumatics, electrical fundamentals, robotics, safety, and semiconductor basics) with immersive VR simulations that replicate real factory equipment and procedures, plus in-simulation quizzes, VR scenario assessments, and workforce skills-profiling dashboards. The platform lets manufacturers evaluate, standardize, and upskill their technician workforce at scale while minimizing disruption to production. Customers include Northrop Grumman, ACC, SUNY, and Dallas College. Backed by 8vc and surfaced into the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company; TAP currently publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: 1047 Games
providers.description: 1047 Games is an independent video game studio best known for the arena shooter Splitgate and its follow-up title EMPULSE, a free-to-play movement shooter. Backed by Insight Partners and Lightspeed Venture Partners, the studio ships games across PC (Steam), PlayStation, and Xbox. As a consumer game publisher it exposes no public developer API; this profile tracks its public web, legal, and community surfaces for the API Evangelist network. Added originally as a VC-portfolio lead and enriched with live domain-security and identity probes.

providers.name: End Game Interactive
providers.description: End Game Interactive, Inc. (ENDGAME) is a Bellevue, Washington video game studio founded by Yang C. Liu and Luke Zbihlyj that builds free-to-play, cross-platform real-time multiplayer titles for browser, mobile and desktop — including ZombsRoyale.io, Zombs.io, Spinz.io, BOPZ.io, Fishington, Betrayal, Super Squad, Match City Puzzle and Fate Arena. The studio describes itself as technology-driven, running small agile teams against a proprietary "ENDGAME ENGINE" alongside Unity and Unreal, with AI-assisted pipelines for asset creation, animation, sound design and voicelines. It raised a $3M seed round in 2020 from Makers Fund, Supercell, Kevin Lin and Scooter Braun among others. ENDGAME is a consumer game publisher: as of this profile it operates no public developer program, no documented API, and no machine-readable contract on any of its web properties.

providers.name: Funcom
providers.description: Funcom is a Norwegian video-game developer and publisher founded in 1993, headquartered in Oslo with additional studios in Raleigh (North Carolina), Lisbon, and Bucharest. It is best known for online, open-world, and survival titles including Dune: Awakening, Conan Exiles, Age of Conan, and The Secret World / Secret World Legends, alongside published titles such as Metal: Hellsinger, Aloft, Dune: Spice Wars, and Mutant Year Zero. Funcom is majority-owned by Tencent. It was surfaced as a Northzone portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it does not currently publish a public developer API surface, so this profile captures company identity, legal/support links, and domain-security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Futureplay
providers.description: Futureplay is a Helsinki, Finland-based mobile game studio founded in 2015 that develops free-to-play games for a global audience, having released six titles for more than 120 million players including Merge Gardens, Battlelands Royale, and Idle Farming Empire. Backed by Creandum and now part of Plarium, the studio operates in the consumer gaming sector. Futureplay publishes no public developer API, SDK, MCP server, or developer portal; player-facing support runs through a Zendesk help center, and legal terms are hosted on the Plarium company site.

providers.name: Gym Class VR
providers.description: Gym Class VR (operating as "Gym Class" by IRL Studios) is a social virtual reality sports gaming platform for Meta Quest headsets and mobile devices, offering multiplayer basketball, baseball, football, boxing, paintball, and soccer experiences where players compete, socialize, and create and share their own games. The top-rated sports title on the Meta Quest Store with a 4.8-star average across 53,000+ ratings, the company holds licensing agreements with the NBA and Major League Baseball, expanded to mobile in 2026, and has raised over $8M from Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Y Combinator, and NBA players. It is a consumer VR entertainment product with no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Immersive Gamebox
providers.description: Immersive Gamebox is a London-founded (2018) location-based entertainment company operating indoor gaming venues across the UK, US, Germany, and the UAE. Each Gamebox combines projection mapping, touch screens, motion tracking, and surround sound to deliver fully immersive, interactive games for teams of two to six players in 30-60 minute sessions. Its catalog spans licensed titles built with partners such as Netflix (Squid Game), Aardman (Shaun the Sheep), Rovio (Angry Birds), and Tetris, alongside originals, and the business runs on bookings, party and corporate packages, Game Pass subscriptions, and a multi-unit franchise model. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of index-ventures. It exposes no public web/REST API today; developer collaboration is limited to a Unity-based SDK offered to game studios building titles for the Gamebox hardware platform.

providers.name: Jackpocket
providers.description: Jackpocket is a third-party lottery courier and mobile app that lets users in supported US states order official state lottery tickets — Powerball, Mega Millions, and regional draw games — from their phone, with the physical tickets stored securely on their behalf and winnings paid out through the app. Founded in 2013 in New York City by Peter Sullivan, the company was acquired by DraftKings in 2024. Jackpocket is a consumer-facing gaming/lottery brand; it does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or webhook surface. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a network entity with its public web properties and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Junglee Games
providers.description: Junglee Games is a skill-based online gaming company founded in 2012 by Ankush Gera, operating as an independent subsidiary of Flutter Entertainment, which acquired a majority stake in 2021 in a deal valuing the company at more than $440 million. Headquartered in Gurugram with a studio in Bengaluru, the company builds and operates consumer real-money and casual gaming apps for a base of over 150 million users, with flagship titles including Junglee Rummy, the Howzat fantasy cricket and football platform, Carrom Stars, and Junglee Poker. The company positions trust, safety, and fairness as engineering priorities. Junglee Games is a consumer gaming provider and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or documented API program; this profile captures its identity, web properties, and probed security posture for the API Evangelist network. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global.

providers.name: mojiworks
providers.description: Mojiworks is a UK-based social games studio, backed by Balderton Capital, that is pioneering a game genre it calls MuGC (Multi-User Generative Creation) — living, collaborative worlds that communities and AI systems build together. Its released titles include Ready Chef Go, Trivia Party, Chef Showdown and Hatch Cats, and it is building its first MuGC world as a persistent, community-shaped city. The company publishes a public AI Ethics Policy committing to licensed training data, environmental accountability, human oversight and content-safety controls. Mojiworks does not currently expose a public developer platform, API, or SDK; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record and enrichment lead.

providers.name: Onibi
providers.description: Onibi (Onibi inc.) is a video game studio founded in 2023 by Benjamin Devienne, with a distributed team in San Francisco, London and Bordeaux drawn from Blizzard, Riot, Ubisoft, EA and Rockstar. Its first title is Tomo: Endless Blue, a procedurally generated monster-taming voxel sandbox open world announced for Steam and funded through a Kickstarter campaign plus roughly $6.5M in seed capital from SeaX Ventures, Serena, Octopus Ventures and Pix Capital. Onibi is a consumer game studio, not an API provider: as of August 2026 the game is unreleased and the studio publishes no developer portal, API reference, SDK or machine-readable specification. The Steam page states an intent to keep the game moddable, but no modding API, tooling or documentation has been published yet, so there is nothing machine-readable to catalog.

providers.name: Phoenix Labs
providers.description: Phoenix Labs is an independent video game developer with studios in Vancouver and Montreal, building immersive online worlds and community-driven games. Its titles include the free-to-play action RPG Dauntless and the cozy life-sim Fae Farm. The studio operates player-facing support and account services for its games but does not publish a public developer platform, API program, or SDKs. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Sapphire Ventures and enriched into the API Evangelist network; its API surface is currently none.

providers.name: PlayQ
providers.description: PlayQ is a Los Angeles-based mobile game developer and publisher creating free-to-play games for a global audience, including titles such as Charm King and Treasure Party. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Techstars and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass PlayQ operates a consumer-facing marketing and game-support website with no public developer portal, API documentation, or API surface; player support is routed through per-game Zendesk help centers.

providers.name: Pops
providers.description: Pops is a consumer mobile application, built by Undefined Software, Inc. and backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026), that lets users create, remix, and share AI-powered mini games with friends. Every play instantly becomes a funny gameplay/reaction video you can send to friends. Pops is available on iOS and Android and is organized around game categories such as arcade, 3D, racing, sports, puzzles, party, and reaction games. It is an end-user social and gaming product with no public API, SDK, or developer platform at this time.

providers.name: Supersolid
providers.description: Supersolid is a London, UK based mobile game developer and publisher, backed by Index Ventures, that designs and operates free-to-play mobile titles across merge, cooking, simulation, and multiplayer arena genres. Its portfolio includes Cook & Merge, Snake Rivals, Home Street, Food Street, Adventure Town, Super Penguins, and RoPets. Supersolid is a consumer-facing games studio and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this API Evangelist profile captures its public web properties (support, careers, terms, privacy) and domain-security posture. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Index Ventures.

providers.name: TaleMonster Games
providers.description: TaleMonster Games is a fully remote mobile game studio whose mission is to create games that surprise, challenge, and evolve with players. The team is united by a shared obsession for product craft and a deep love for games, and ships casual mobile titles to iOS and Android. Its debut title, Match Valley, is a casual match puzzle game published on the Apple App Store and Google Play. TaleMonster Games publishes no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or technical documentation; this profile captures its public company and product identity.

providers.name: Triumph Arcade
providers.description: Triumph Labs (originally Triumph Arcade) is a consumer entertainment and commerce company that builds mobile apps for competitive, skill-based gaming and collectibles. Its flagship products are Triumph: Play for Cash, a real-money skill-gaming platform, and Rips by Triumph, a live collectibles and trading-card ripping experience. Backed by Multicoin Capital, the company operates consumer iOS apps and publishes no public developer API surface; this profile tracks the company identity, legal, and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: videogame.ai
providers.description: videogame.ai is an AI-native game development studio that uses fleets of autonomous AI coding agents to build, ship, and operate video games. The company offers full-service game development delivered in days at the cost of a single full-time employee, along with automated live-ops pipelines, a multiplayer engine optimized for AI coding agents, an AI-native asset and media management system, and autonomous generation of ads and creative from game builds. Featured titles include Zero Hour, a narrative game set on a frozen planet, and Imperfect World, an RPG built around time-loop mechanics. Backed by a16z (SR02) and Konvoy. Surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network; the studio publishes a marketing site and contact channel but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation at this time.

providers.name: Live Aware Labs
providers.description: Live Aware Labs (LIVE AWARE) is a virtual playtesting and player-insights lab for game studios and researchers. The platform consolidates gameplay footage, player feedback, and community discussion from sources such as Discord, Twitch, YouTube, and internal playtests into a single dashboard, then applies AI to surface trends, player sentiment, and critical feedback in real time. A PC-based SDK captures video, telemetry, and in-game events, with plugins for Unreal Engine and Unity and no-code integrations into Slack, Jira, Monday.com, and OBS. Live Aware Labs is backed by a16z and was added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead; this profile is enriched from the company's public web surface.

providers.name: Mojo Vision
providers.description: Mojo Vision is a Saratoga, California semiconductor and display company building a "wafers-in, wafers-out" micro-LED platform. Founded in 2015, it originally developed the world's smallest, densest dynamic display for an AR smart contact lens, then pivoted in 2023 to commercializing micro-LED displays and optical interconnects. Its platform combines a 300mm silicon architecture with GaN-on-Silicon emitters, proprietary quantum dots and micro-lens arrays, and has demonstrated a monolithic RGB panel at 4µm pixel pitch (6,350 ppi). Target markets are XR and AI-enabled glasses, automotive heads-up displays, large-format displays, and high-density optical I/O for AI infrastructure. Partners include Marvell, DigiLens and CY Vision; investors include Khosla Ventures, NEA, Future Ventures, HP Tech Ventures, Amazon's Alexa Fund and Dolby Family Ventures. Mojo Vision is a hardware/silicon company and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: ID Planet
providers.description: ID Planet is a Web3 GameFi company building an EVM-compatible blockchain ecosystem for blockchain gaming. Its published ecosystem spans ID Planet Chain, the ID Explorer block explorer, the ID Wallet multi-chain wallet, ID SWAP (a decentralized exchange), ID PLANETXC (a centralized exchange) and an NFT marketplace, alongside first-party game titles Infinitar (5v5 MOBA), Runesoul (ARPG) and CoolGods (MOBA). The $ID governance token is issued as a BEP20 asset on BNB Chain with a total supply of 7,800,000,000 and a mining/burn distribution model. Company material is published as a GitBook whitepaper in eight languages. As of 2026-08-22 ID Planet publishes no developer portal, API reference, RPC endpoint, chain ID or machine-readable specification on any host it controls, so this profile is identity and documentation only.

providers.name: Osmo
providers.description: Osmo (Tangible Play) makes hands-on, screen-interactive learning games for iPad and Fire tablet that pair a physical reflector base placed over the device camera with digital games spanning math, coding, spelling, drawing, and problem-solving for children. Backed by Accel and GV, Osmo is a consumer educational-technology brand that sells hardware kits and companion apps direct to families and schools. As of this enrichment pass it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: AppliedVR
providers.description: AppliedVR is a virtual reality therapeutics company that combines immersive technology with proven cognitive behavioral and behavioral-science techniques to treat medical conditions, with a focus on chronic pain. Its lead product, RelieVRx, is the first FDA-authorized prescription VR device for chronic lower back pain, delivering automated, self-administered cognitive behavioral therapy in the patient's home. AppliedVR also offers the SustainVR and ITx immersive therapeutics platform and the AVR Pathway patient-support system, and validates its products through clinical academic research. The company operates as a regulated digital-therapeutics / medical-device business rather than a developer-facing API platform, so it publishes no public API, SDK, or developer portal at this time. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Azra Games
providers.description: Azra Games is a mobile role-playing game studio founded in 2022 by Mark Otero and headquartered in Sacramento, California. The studio builds RPGs on its proprietary "RPG GameKit" technology, with its flagship title UnGodly, a dark sword-and-sorcery RPG. Azra Games is backed by a16z and Pantera Capital and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile. As a game studio it publishes a public website, news, careers, terms, and privacy pages but does not expose a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Harmonix
providers.description: Harmonix Music Systems is one of the world's leading independent game development studios, best known for creating blockbuster music and rhythm franchises including Rock Band and Dance Central, alongside titles such as Amplitude, Fuser, DropMix, Audica, Super Beat Sports, and Harmonix Music VR. Founded in 1995 and based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, the studio was acquired by Epic Games in 2021 and continues to invent the future of music and motion gaming. Harmonix operates a consumer-facing web presence (games, music, community, blog, and press) and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Rovio Entertainment
providers.description: Rovio Entertainment is a Finnish mobile game company founded in 2003 and headquartered in Espoo, best known for the Angry Birds franchise and a portfolio of casual and puzzle titles played by hundreds of millions of players worldwide. It operates game studios across Finland, Sweden, Denmark, Canada, Spain, and Turkey, and became part of Sega Sammy Holdings in 2023. Rovio was surfaced as a portfolio company of Atomico and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Rovio publishes a corporate/marketing website but no public developer portal, API, SDK, or well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: Wildlife Studios
providers.description: Wildlife Studios is one of the world's largest mobile game developers and publishers, founded in Brazil in 2011. It builds and operates free-to-play games played globally, with more than 4.7 billion downloads across a portfolio of over 60 titles including Zooba, Sniper 3D, Tennis Clash, War Machines, and Sky Warriors, and runs a publishing division for third-party studios. Wildlife is a consumer gaming company: its public surface is player-facing games and corporate/careers content, not a developer platform. As of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, or MCP server. Surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners and tracked in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Dare Drop
providers.description: Dare Drop is a gaming influencer marketing platform that connects game publishers and brands with content creators across Twitch, YouTube, and TikTok. The platform runs reward-driven "Dares" — challenges that incentivize streamers and creators to produce longer, more engaging content around a title, while automating creator targeting, campaign management, and reporting. Dare Drop offers influencer campaigns, ongoing influencer programs, and organic outreach, and has facilitated over 18,000 publisher Dares and distributed more than 30,000 rewards to creator communities. Its customers include game studios and publishers such as EA, Respawn, Raw Fury, Tencent, Obsidian, and Gearbox. Surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network; no public developer API surface has been found to date.

providers.name: FanDuel
providers.description: FanDuel is a major US sports betting and daily fantasy sports operator (FanDuel Sportsbook, FanDuel Casino, FanDuel Fantasy, FanDuel TV). FanDuel does not publish a public developer REST API for its sportsbook, casino, or fantasy products. Internal/private APIs power the apps and a Sportradar/SBTech-derived trading stack but are not available to third-party developers.

providers.name: RealNetworks
providers.description: RealNetworks is a Seattle-based technology company that pairs AI-powered computer-vision and secure-communication products with its long-running consumer media brands. Its portfolio includes SAFR (facial recognition for security and retail loss prevention), Kontxt (AI messaging and voice security for CPaaS platforms, Telcos, and MNOs), GameHouse (cross-device casual gaming), and RealPlayer (media playback). Product APIs for SAFR and Kontxt are delivered through authenticated partner portals rather than an open developer portal; the historical Real Developer Program (developer.real.com) is no longer live, and no public OpenAPI specification was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Geopipe
providers.description: Geopipe uses AI and machine learning to build game-ready digital twins of real-world cities and environments. It ingests raw sensor data (imagery and laser scans) and reconstructs regions as semantically-modeled, multi-level-of- detail 3D models that developers stream or download into games, simulations, training, architecture, and metaverse applications without any manual 3D modeling. Delivery is through Cesium 3D Tiles streaming for Unity and Unreal Engine, downloadable 3D meshes in common file formats, ready-to-use Unity Asset Store packs, and a first-party Unity SDK, backed by an open-source geospatial and 3D-tiles toolchain on GitHub. Founded in New York City by Christopher Mitchell and Thomas Dickerson and backed by Techstars.

providers.name: 6 Waves
providers.description: 6waves is a global mobile game publisher founded in 2008 and headquartered in Hong Kong, with offices in China, Japan, and the United States. The company partners with independent game developers around the world to publish, localize, and operate social and mobile games, offering culturalization, product guidance, live operations, marketing, platform relationships, customer service and community management, technical support, quality assurance, and VIP management. 6waves is recognized as a pioneer of top-grossing mobile game publishing, particularly in the Japanese market, and is a portfolio company of Insight Partners.

providers.name: AlmostApps
providers.description: AlmostApps is a Sacramento, California sports-gaming studio founded in 2022 that builds free-to-play mobile entertainment experiences for sports fans, blending casual gameplay with real-life sports scores and stats. Its flagship product, Tailgate, is a free-to-play mobile sports entertainment app designed to enhance the game-day experience for casual sports enthusiasts. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Parade Ventures. AlmostApps is a consumer application company and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, SDK, or API documentation; only a marketing site with Terms of Service and Privacy Policy is publicly available. This profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a company lead.

providers.name: AutoLotto
providers.description: AutoLotto, Inc. operates Lottery.com, a mobile platform that lets users in participating US states play official draw lottery games such as Powerball and Mega Millions from their phones, track tickets, view winning numbers, jackpot sizes and draw times, and collect winnings to a linked bank account. Beyond the consumer app, AutoLotto runs a business data-licensing offering that syndicates results and draw data for hundreds of lottery games worldwide to partner digital properties. AutoLotto is venture-backed (500 Global, Pantera Capital) and its parent trades publicly. As of this enrichment pass Lottery.com exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or self-service developer portal; data access is arranged through a manual "license our data" inquiry form rather than a programmatic surface.

providers.name: BIT ODD
providers.description: BIT ODD is a Helsinki-based mobile game studio founded in 2019 by former Supercell creative leads Lasse Louhento, Taneli Oksama, and Jani Lintunen. The studio hand-crafts casual mobile games driven by feeling and a sense of wonder rather than aggressive monetization, explicitly rejecting ad-spam and dark-pattern design. Backed by Index Ventures, Griffin Gaming Partners, and Makers Fund across a EUR 5M seed and a EUR 17M round, BIT ODD is a consumer entertainment company with no public developer platform, API, or SDK surface; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a portfolio lead and carries only the artifacts that can be honestly probed from its public web presence (domain security, legal pages).

providers.name: Closing Theory Studios
providers.description: Closing Theory Studios, Inc. is an independent mobile game studio founded in 2023 and based in Austin, Texas, on a mission to bring the real world into games. Its debut title, Househunt (the officially licensed ZillowGoneWild game), lets the 70 million-plus people who browse Zillow for fun buy, guess prices on, renovate, flip, and manage real houses in a casual mobile experience aimed at "non-gamers." The studio was co-founded by Ankith Harathi and Nitin Rajinikanth and raised a $2.3M round led by a16z GAMES SPEEDRUN, with participation from Powerhouse Capital and angel Seth Sivak (founder of Proletariat, acquired by Blizzard). Closing Theory Studios ships consumer mobile games on iOS and Android and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: Everyrealm
providers.description: Everyrealm Inc. is a Web3 and metaverse company building virtual communities inside in-game worlds, positioned at the intersection of gaming, entertainment, and blockchain technology. Under the banner "Connecting what matters," Everyrealm develops immersive, gamified virtual worlds and experiences, partners with gaming platforms, and invests across the broader metaverse and digital-real-estate ecosystem. The company has raised venture funding from Lightspeed Venture Partners, Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Coinbase Ventures, Brevan Howard, Hashed, and other prominent investors. Everyrealm is a consumer- and community-facing operator rather than an API-first developer platform; as of this profile it publishes no public developer portal, OpenAPI definitions, SDKs, or programmatic API surface. This entry was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile and has been enriched with public identity, legal, and domain-security signals.

providers.name: Flickplay
providers.description: Flickplay, Inc. is a Web3 social and gaming company that turns character intellectual property into portable, interactive, and monetizable experiences across user-generated content, social platforms, and real-world retail activations. Its consumer iOS app combines character-based gameplay (blind boxes, spin games, leveling), AR video and GIF creation tools, AI character chat, iOS home-screen widgets, a quest system tying gameplay to e-commerce, and a Fandom Intelligence dashboard tracking fan identity, behavior, and spend. Flickplay is a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners. As of mid-2026 the company published a suspension notice, and it exposes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal — this profile is identity-only.

providers.name: FreshPlanet
providers.description: FreshPlanet Inc. is a New York City based mobile game developer, headquartered at 200 Hudson St, New York, NY 10013, best known for the music trivia franchise SongPop. The studio builds free-to-play mobile entertainment titles for iOS and Android, combining licensed music catalogs, social multiplayer play, and live events. FreshPlanet is a portfolio company of Uncork Capital. As a consumer game studio it does not operate a public developer program or API: it exposes only a marketing site, player support via a Zendesk help center, and standard legal surfaces (Terms of Use and Privacy Policy). This profile captures the studio's real public web and legal footprint for the API Evangelist network; there is no OpenAPI, SDK, or agent surface to enrich because the company publishes none.

providers.name: Good Job Games
providers.description: Good Job Games is a global mobile gaming company founded in 2017 that designs, develops, and operates puzzle and match-3 titles for iOS and Android, including Wonder Blast and Match Villains. The studio publishes its games through the Apple App Store and Google Play rather than a developer API program, and its public web surface is limited to its marketing site, games catalog, careers ("Life at Good Job Games") pages, and legal policies. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Menlo Ventures and profiled in the API Evangelist network. No public developer API, SDK, documentation, or API reference was found during enrichment; the artifacts captured here reflect its domain security posture and public web properties.

providers.name: Grand Games
providers.description: Grand Games (Grand Games Oyun ve Yazılım) is an Istanbul-based hybrid-casual mobile game studio founded in early 2024 by Bekir Batuhan Çelebi, Mehmet Çalım, and Mustafa Fırtına, a team that previously built Zen Match at Moon Active. The studio develops genre-defining puzzle games for iOS and Android played by millions worldwide, including Magic Sort, Car Match, and Block Out, and has grown to six live titles with fivefold year-over-year revenue. It has raised roughly $103M across three rounds, most recently a $70M Series B led by Balderton Capital's Growth Fund in May 2026. Grand Games publishes consumer mobile games and does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Mission Control Games
providers.description: Mission Control Games is a mobile game studio building casual puzzle games, co-founded by Kivanc Okutur (CEO) and Murat Gurel (CTO), veterans of the team behind Merge Dragons. Headquartered across London and Istanbul (legal entity Mission Control Games Yazilim Anonim Sirketi), the studio works in small teams to create new casual puzzle sub-genres through rapid iteration and AI-assisted development. It launched publicly in April 2026 alongside a $4M pre-seed round led by General Catalyst, with participation from Arcadia Gaming Partners and e2vc. The company operates a marketing website only and publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable developer surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Mother Games
providers.description: Mother Games is a Brooklyn, New York consumer gaming studio backed by GV (Google Ventures). As of mid-2026 the company is pre-launch: it operates a public waitlist for its debut social title "Le Zoo" and runs a campus ambassador program from its Williamsburg mailbox address (223 Bedford Ave #200, Brooklyn, NY 11211). Mother Games does not currently expose any public developer API, SDK, documentation, or developer platform surface — probes of the domain returned 404 for every /.well-known/, /llms.txt, /openapi.json, /api, /docs, and /developers path. This profile tracks the company identity and public web properties in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead pending any future developer platform.

providers.name: PLAYSTUDIOS
providers.description: PLAYSTUDIOS, Inc. (Nasdaq: MYPS) is a developer and publisher of free-to-play casual and casino-style mobile and social games, including myVEGAS Slots, POP! Slots, MGM Slots Live, myKONAMI, Tetris Block Puzzle, Solitaire, Bingo, and Mahjong titles. Its differentiating platform, playAWARDS, is a loyalty rewards engine that lets players earn real-world rewards from brand partners across gaming, hospitality, dining, and entertainment. The company is headquartered in Las Vegas and went public in 2021 via a business combination with Acies Acquisition Corp. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a dcm-ventures portfolio company; PLAYSTUDIOS publishes consumer-facing games and corporate/investor properties but no public developer API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Powder
providers.description: Powder was a Paris-based gaming company, founded in 2018 and backed by a $14M Series A led by Serena with General Catalyst, Slow Ventures, Alven, Bpifrance Digital Venture and Secocha Ventures. It built AI-powered clipping software for gamers and content creators: a low-resource Windows screen recorder plus on-device machine learning that detected highlight moments in gameplay recordings and long Twitch, YouTube and Kick streams and turned them into short vertical clips, AutoEdits and automontages, with per-title models for 40-plus games including Fortnite, Valorant, Counter-Strike 2 and League of Legends, and NPU-accelerated local inference on AMD XDNA hardware. It was distributed as an end-user desktop app through Steam, the Microsoft Store and Razer Cortex, on a free tier with a $9.99/month Powder Pro subscription. Powder published no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable contract. The company has since wound down: its own apex domain now redirects every path to a first-party notice stating the app is no longer updated or maintained and that all subscriptions have been cancelled.

providers.name: Roboto Games
providers.description: Roboto Games is an independent video game development studio building Stormforge, an open-world survival crafting game where players craft, build, fight, and harness epic storms to survive in a magical fantasy world. The studio was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As a consumer game studio, Roboto Games publishes a marketing website, a careers page, and a studio blog, but exposes no public developer API, SDK, or programmatic surface — its player-facing experience is delivered through native game clients (Steam) and community channels (Discord, YouTube, Twitch) rather than an HTTP API. This profile captures the studio's public identity and web properties; no API artifacts are produced because none are published.

providers.name: SuperGaming
providers.description: SuperGaming is a Series B-funded game development studio building multiplayer games "for the next billion players" in emerging markets. Headquartered in Singapore with a studio in Pune, India, the company develops and operates titles including Indus (battle royale), Prime Rush, Prime Rush MENA, SHOWDOWN, MaskGun (110M+ installs), Tower Conquest, and Silly Royale. SuperGaming also runs SuperPlatform, a proprietary real-time multiplayer and live-ops engine that powers its own games and 15+ other titles, and offers publisher services such as co-development, LiveOps-as-a-service, localization, and user acquisition. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal for external developers; SuperPlatform is an internal engine offered through partnerships rather than a self-serve API. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z.

providers.name: Yuga Labs
providers.description: Yuga Labs is a Web3 company and the creator of the Bored Ape Yacht Club (BAYC), Mutant Ape Yacht Club (MAYC), and the Otherside metaverse, along with related NFT collections and intellectual property. Backed by a16z, Bond Capital, GV, Lightspeed Venture Partners and SV Angel, the company operates in the crypto / NFT sector on the Ethereum blockchain. It does not publish a formal, documented public developer API program; its on-chain assets are accessed via Ethereum smart contracts and third-party marketplaces (OpenSea, Blur), and Otherside exposes the forthcoming Otherside Development Kit (ODK) for building within the metaverse. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched with the available public identity and domain-security signals.

providers.name: Incite Interactive
providers.description: Incite Interactive is an AI-native gaming studio founded in 2023 and backed by Andreessen Horowitz's Speedrun program, building AI-powered emergent narrative games where the stories players tell matter more than the ones they are told. Its "Everything Story Engine" is an agentic game engine that lets anyone create AI characters and living-world scenarios, powering products such as Embark and Incite Worlds — a roleplaying sandbox of human and AI-driven characters. The founding team are veterans of Zynga, Roblox, and Manticore Games with deep expertise in language models, user-generated content, and live-game operations. There is no public developer API or documentation surface at this time; this profile captures the company's public identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: tagSpace
providers.description: tagSpace is a Spatial AI platform, part of the tagStorm group, that lets creators and brands publish interactive augmented-reality experiences and spatial content anchored to real-world places. Through its create, explore, and publish surfaces, tagSpace offers a creator-economy platform where makers showcase spatial "tags," and its tagAI layer applies AI to spatial content. It markets to brands and enterprises (B2B) with named partners including RTL, Telekom, Telstra, Warner Music Group and others. The public site is a Framer marketing presence; as of this enrichment pass tagSpace exposes no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or well-known API metadata. This profile remains an identity-only company record.

providers.name: Medivis
providers.description: Medivis is a medical technology company building AI-powered augmented reality solutions for surgery and medical education. Its flagship product, SurgicalAR, is an FDA 510(k)-cleared platform that runs on Microsoft HoloLens 2 and transforms 2D medical imaging (CT and MRI) into interactive 3D holographic visualizations for surgical planning and navigation, including FDA-cleared systems for spine and cranial procedures. Medivis also offers AnatomyX, an AR platform for anatomy and medical education. The company reports deployment across 40+ institutions and use in 2,000+ surgeries. Medivis is a Microsoft technology partner and a portfolio company of Initialized Capital. Medivis publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK; its software surface is delivered as HoloLens and iOS applications for clinical and educational users.

providers.name: Vivid Vision
providers.description: Vivid Vision is a digital vision care company that builds VR- and software-based tools for diagnosing and treating binocular vision disorders. Its products include a vision training system for amblyopia (lazy eye), strabismus, and convergence insufficiency; Vivid Vision Perimetry (VVP), a VR-based visual field test used as an endpoint in ophthalmology clinical trials for geographic atrophy, AMD, and glaucoma; and EYEBAB VT therapeutic exercises for clinical settings. Founded in 2014, the platform has been used by more than 100,000 patients across 50+ countries through eye-care practices and clinics. Vivid Vision is backed by Uncork Capital. The company is a patient- and clinician-facing vision-care provider and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface at this time.

providers.name: FanCraze
providers.description: FanCraze is an International Cricket Council (ICC) officially licensed platform for cricket collectibles, trading, and fantasy gaming, serving more than 500,000 cricket fans worldwide. Its flagship products are Grails, a digital collectibles experience where fans pull officially licensed ICC player cards (Common through Legendary), trade them with other fans, and complete themed sets; and Matchday, a free-to-play fantasy cricket game where fans build squads from their collectibles and compete on live challenges tied to real ICC tournaments including Men's and Women's Cricket World Cups, T20 World Cups, and U-19 World Cups. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and is backed by investors including Tiger Global, Sequoia, Coatue, Dapper Labs, and Coinbase Ventures. FanCraze operates as a consumer (B2C) mobile and web app and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile captures its public web identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Five Jack
providers.description: Five Jack (PT. Five Jack) is the Indonesian company behind itemku, one of Southeast Asia's largest digital-goods marketplaces for gamers. Founded in 2014 as a game price-comparison and classifieds platform, itemku grew into a full marketplace where buyers and sellers trade in-game items, currency, account top-ups, game keys, and vouchers across 200+ game categories including Roblox, Genshin Impact, Mobile Legends, Dota 2, Steam, and Growtopia. The company reached one million orders in 2018, launched its Android app and gaming blog in 2020, and became part of Bukalapak (IDX: BUKA) in May 2021. Five Jack was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. It operates a consumer-facing marketplace and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: Matcherino
providers.description: Matcherino is an esports crowdfunding and tournament-management platform that provides monetization infrastructure for competitive gaming events of every scale, from college clubs to stadium finals. Its stack covers prize-pool crowdfunding, brackets, player signups, ticketing and entry fees, streaming overlays, sponsor activation, and a publisher dashboard for distributing cash and in-game prizes. Matcherino handles global payouts to organizers and winners across 120+ countries with tax-form collection, and surfaces real-time analytics for organizers, sponsors, and publishers. The company reports having paid out more than $5.2M across 14,000+ tournaments. Matcherino is a Techstars-backed company; it does not currently publish a public API or developer platform.

providers.name: PrizePicks
providers.description: PrizePicks is a US daily-fantasy/pick-em sports operator focused on player-prop projections (more/less). PrizePicks does not publish a public developer REST API. Internal/private endpoints power the web and mobile apps but are not documented or licensed for third-party use.

providers.name: Zwift
providers.description: Zwift is a Long Beach, California online fitness company that operates a multiplayer indoor cycling and running platform combining stationary smart trainers and bikes with a 3D virtual-world game client. Riders and runners use a smart trainer, smart bike (such as the in-house Zwift Ride), treadmill, or pod to drive an avatar through fictional worlds (Watopia, Makuri Islands) and licensed real-world routes, joining structured workouts, group rides, races, training plans, and 24/7 events alongside a global community of more than a million members. The platform pairs with smart trainers and heart-rate monitors over Bluetooth and ANT+, and the Zwift Companion mobile app provides in-game messaging, ride control, and route discovery. Zwift does not operate a general public developer portal, OpenAPI reference, or open-source SDK. Its developer surface is limited to a private, application-only Structured Training API for approved training partners (TrainingPeaks, TrainerRoad, Wahoo SYSTM, JOIN Cycling and similar coaching platforms) that lets external workout builders push custom workouts into a rider's Zwift account, plus one-way activity-export connections to Strava, TrainingPeaks, Garmin Connect, MapMyRide, MapMyRun, Adidas Running, Technogym, Fitbit, Wahoo, Apple Health, and Withings. There is no public REST surface, OAuth client registration, or partner self-service available to general developers — third-party tools (community libraries, ZwiftPower, Sauce for Zwift) interact with Zwift via reverse-engineered private endpoints, not a sanctioned API. Zwift is a paid consumer subscription business; revenue comes from monthly memberships and hardware sales (Zwift Ride, Zwift Cog, Zwift Click, Zwift Play).

providers.name: E-Pal
providers.description: E-Pal is a gaming social platform with the tagline "Never Battle Alone" that connects gamers to find teammates, compete, and socialize around competitive and casual gaming experiences. Its mobile apps (iOS and Android) let users discover gaming companions ("ePals"), form squads, use voice chat, play minigames, and hang out in social spaces. Product surfaces include Games (finding great teammates for titles like League of Legends and Valorant), Chilling (social hangout spaces), and Custom personalized experiences, plus a tiered community of eStars, Legend ePals (professional-rank players), and E-Chat. E-Pal is a consumer application and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts at this time; this profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and enriched as an identity-only lead.

providers.name: Future Trash
providers.description: Future Trash is a Los Angeles-based independent, multidisciplinary creative game studio and the developer behind FOAD, a user-generated-content (UGC) native video game franchise. Founded around 2022, the team first built a vertical-slice MVP of FOAD in Unreal Engine 5 and released it in early access on Steam. After Epic Games launched Unreal Editor for Fortnite (UEFN) in 2023, the studio pivoted to building FOAD experiences natively inside Fortnite's UGC ecosystem, spanning MOBA, tycoon, and combat modes, while planning to resume the standalone UE5 core game. Future Trash raised a $5M seed round in September 2024 led by TIRTA Ventures with participation from General Catalyst. This profile was surfaced from General Catalyst's portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network; Future Trash is a game studio and publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: ThatGameCompany
providers.description: ThatGameCompany is an American independent video game studio founded in 2006 by Jenova Chen and Kellee Santiago, known for emotionally driven, art-forward titles including Flow, Flower, Journey, and the free-to-play social adventure Sky: Children of the Light. The studio focuses on creating timeless interactive entertainment that inspires human connection across all ages. It publishes no public developer API; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a technology / gaming entity and records domain-security posture from live probes.

providers.name: Cartwheel
providers.description: Cartwheel is a generative motion platform for games, film & TV, advertising, and robotics. It gives creators a new way to animate 3D characters — turning ordinary video into clean, usable character motion (video-to-motion), and posing and rendering characters as images in any visual style. Cartwheel is delivered as a hosted web studio (studio.getcartwheel.com) with exportable animation formats for downstream 3D, game, film, and social pipelines. The product is in private beta and is backed by Accel, Craft Ventures, and Menlo Ventures. At this time Cartwheel exposes no public developer/REST API; this profile captures its public web, documentation, and security surface.

providers.name: Riiico
providers.description: RIIICO is a Duesseldorf-based industrial software company building 3D-AI tools that digitalize the factory shop floor. Its platform turns reality scans (point clouds) of existing plants into CAD-ready, pre-classified 3D models, cutting 3D modeling time by up to 80% and accelerating factory retrofit, robot programming, and simulation. RIIICO integrates with NVIDIA Omniverse (OpenUSD) and Siemens Xcelerator, and counts Siemens, Volvo, and Schaeffler among its customers. It won the Siemens Inventors of the Year Award 2024 and is backed by Earlybird, PiLabs, and seed + speed. No public API, SDK, or developer documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Yield Guild Games
providers.description: Yield Guild Games (YGG) is a decentralized autonomous organization (DAO) and one of the world's first and largest web3 gaming guilds, founded in 2020 by Gabby Dizon, Beryl Li, and the pseudonymous "Owl of Moistness" out of the Philippines. YGG invests in NFTs and blockchain-game assets, lends them to players, and shares the resulting yield with its community and YGG token holders. Its onchain Guild Protocol (launched on Base) equips guilds with a modular library of smart-contract tooling for treasury wallets, programmable quests, and contribution tracking, while YGG Play acts as a publisher for casual crypto games. The company was backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), which led a $4.6M round in 2021. Note: this repository slug "yield-guide-games" preserves an upstream typo of the real company name, Yield Guild Games.

providers.name: ELKROOM CO., LTD.
providers.description: ELKROOM CO., LTD. is a consumer mobile-gaming studio and 500 Global portfolio company behind the OXO product family. Its flagship OXO Game Launcher is an Android game launcher and optimization tool that organizes a player's games and automatically tracks play history, journals, monthly reports, rankings, and community activity, and has surpassed five million downloads on Google Play. The company also builds OXO Gameplay, an AI-powered gaming content and social platform for Android and iOS, and Stricer, a cloud-based AI video analysis and highlight-editing tool on the web. ELKROOM operates consumer applications rather than a public developer API; this profile captures its public identity, product surface, and legal/policy pages. Tagline: "You Chase Glory. We Make It Legendary."

providers.name: Jam.gg
providers.description: Jam.gg, founded in Paris in 2020 as Piepacker and rebranded in 2022, built a browser-based social cloud gaming platform for playing retro and indie multiplayer games with friends with no download or install, on patented streaming technology the company said cut bandwidth requirements by roughly 15x. It passed 8 million users before pivoting to selling its cloud gaming technology B2B to game developers and publishers. Backed by Makers Fund, Serena Capital, LEGO Ventures, Kima Ventures and Kickstarter (~$15.4M raised) and a Y Combinator W20 company. Jam.gg never published an HTTP API: its developer surface was a native game-integration SDK plus a Compose Multiplatform virtual gamepad library, both shipped from the GitHub organization still named piepacker. Y Combinator's company directory now lists Jam.gg as Inactive, noting the business split into two entities in 2023 with Onibi emerging separately; the jam.gg web property no longer completes a TLS handshake and piepacker.com has left DNS.

providers.name: Pinscreen
providers.description: Pinscreen is an American AI and VFX production company founded in 2015 by Hao Li (MIT TR35 winner and professor of computer vision at MBZUAI), headquartered in Los Angeles with a branch in Abu Dhabi (UAE). It builds advanced generative AI for film production and interactive experiences, including AI lip sync, face reenactment, face swaps, de-aging, voice cloning, and photoreal 3D avatar digitization, and is known for developing the world's first real-time deepfake technology. Its Avatar Neo product generates a photoreal, riggable 3D avatar from a single photo (exportable as GLB/FBX with animation rigs) and is offered to developers as the Avatar Neo SDK: Unreal and Unity engine plugins backed by an avatar-generation API that can be deployed anywhere. Customers include Netflix, Amazon Studios, Warner Bros, Miramax, Apple, Google, Adobe, and DARPA. Backed by Lux Capital and Middle East investors.
