providers.name: Touchten
providers.description: Touchten (Touchten Pte. Ltd.) is an award-winning mobile game studio headquartered in Jakarta, Indonesia, and an early 500 Global (500 Startups) portfolio company. Its casual games - including Piper's Pet Cafe, Royal Garden Tales, Dessert Chain, Warung Chain Go Food Express, and the Teka-Teki Saku (TTS) crossword series - are published on the App Store and Google Play, are played by millions worldwide, and cater especially to the underserved women gamers market in the US and Europe. Touchten won the Google Play Indonesia Games Contest and received the Forbes Indonesia Rising Global Stars Award. The company publishes no developer portal or public API surface.

providers.name: Rangers Protocol
providers.description: Rangers Protocol is an EVM-compatible Layer 1 blockchain (Chain ID 2025) built for Web3 games and metaverse applications, using a VRF+BLS consensus mechanism to handle high-frequency transactions and a heterogeneous relay chain for true cross-chain interoperability. It features a virtual-machine ("blockchain virtualization") design, an NFT protocol emphasizing data inheritance and reuse, an on-chain oracle, and the Grand Guard Safe security tooling. Its native gas token, RPG (Rangers Protocol Gas), is also issued as ERC20 on Ethereum and BEP20 on BNB Smart Chain. The developer surface is standard Ethereum JSON-RPC plus verification-node operations; it was surfaced as a portfolio company of Pantera Capital and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Community Gaming
providers.description: Community Gaming is a web3 esports and gaming platform where players earn cryptocurrency rewards by competing in tournaments and completing quests. Players link a Sequence wallet, collect keys from quests and matches to open loot boxes and giveaway tickets, and enter prize draws paid out in USDC. The platform also serves tournament organizers with hosting tools, sponsorships, and grants. Backed by Multicoin Capital, it publishes a public knowledge center for players and organizers but does not currently document a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs.

providers.name: One More Game
providers.description: One More Game is a fully remote game development studio founded by veterans behind titles such as Warcraft, Diablo, StarCraft, and Guild Wars. The team builds delightful, social online games designed to be played with friends, emphasizing fast iteration and a mission to help players have more fun. One More Game was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. The studio publishes a consumer gaming website, a company blog, careers listings, and a GitHub organization (PlayOneMoreGame) of game-development tooling and forks, but does not currently operate a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Drone Racing League
providers.description: The Drone Racing League (DRL) is a New York-based professional drone racing property founded in 2015 by Nicholas Horbaczewski, staging first-person-view (FPV) races in which pilots fly identical, league-built quadcopters - the Racer series - through three-dimensional courses in stadiums, arenas and landmark venues at speeds above 80 mph. DRL designs its own racing drones, timing and telemetry hardware, produces and distributes its race broadcasts across NBC, Sky Sports, ProSiebenSat.1 and streaming platforms, and operates the DRL Simulator, an FPV racing game on Steam, PlayStation and Xbox that feeds the Swatch DRL Tryouts esports pipeline used to recruit professional pilots. The company was acquired by Infinite Reality (now Napster) in April 2024. DRL publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or machine-readable API specification, and as of the 2026-08-04 enrichment pass its primary web properties (thedroneracingleague.com, drl.io) were not completing a TLS handshake.

providers.name: EasyAR CRS API
providers.description: EasyAR CRS (Cloud Recognition Service) is a cloud image-recognition solution that lets developers manage up to 100K image-targets online and recognize them from camera key-frames. It provides HTTP web-service APIs for target management and recognition, with request-signing/token authentication on per-instance regional base URLs.

providers.name: ironSource
providers.description: ironSource is a Tel Aviv-based mobile game growth platform, acquired by Unity Technologies in a $4.4B all-stock deal that closed in November 2022 and is now operated as part of Unity's Grow Solutions group. The company builds an end-to-end suite for mobile game developers spanning ad monetization, user acquisition, and ad operations. Its flagship product LevelPlay is a unified in-app bidding and ad mediation platform that brokers Rewarded Video, Interstitial, and Banner ad demand across the ironSource Ads network, AdMob, AppLovin, Meta Audience Network, Pangle, Mintegral, Unity Ads, Vungle, and dozens of other ad sources. ironSource Ads is its self-serve ad network and user-acquisition platform offering CPI, CPE, ROAS-optimized, and SKAdNetwork-aware campaign management. Adjacent products include Aura (an on-device content marketplace for carriers and OEMs that originated from the 2021 Bigabid/Soomla portfolio and earlier hardware OEM deals), Tapjoy Offerwall (acquired 2022) for rewarded engagement, and Ad Quality for ad-content monitoring. Developer access is via a REST surface hosted at platform.ironsrc.com — including the Monetization Reporting API (v5/v4), ironSource Ads Reporting API, Application API (v6), Campaign API suite (Campaigns, Audiences, Country Groups, Bidding, Assets, Creatives), SKAN Reporting API, and Cost API — authenticated with Bearer tokens issued from the platform dashboard. Real client integration is delivered via native SDKs (iOS, Android, Unity, Flutter, React Native, Adobe AIR, Xamarin) plus the LevelPlay mediation adapter ecosystem published on github.com/ironsource-mobile. As of 2026 the developers.is.com knowledge center 301-redirects to docs.unity.com, consolidating ironSource documentation inside Unity Grow alongside Unity Ads. No public OpenAPI, Postman collection, or JSON Schema bundle is published by ironSource for the REST surface; documentation is human-readable HTML on docs.unity.com/en-us/grow.

A Qiming Venture Partners portfolio company, Xiudan publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API artifacts as of July 2026 - this profile records the company identity and probe results for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Distance
providers.description: Distance (Distance Technologies) is a Helsinki-based frontier-tech company pioneering glasses-free extended reality (XR) built on computational optics and lightfield technology. Its systems turn transparent surfaces — vehicle windshields, aircraft canopies, and head-mounted visors — into intelligent heads-up displays without screens, overlays, or wearable glasses. Products include the Acuity visual-intelligence platform and Acuity OS for defense, the Field Operator HUD (FOH) head-mounted system in field trials across NATO countries, and panoramic lightfield HUDs for automotive ADAS and navigation. Distance is backed by GV (Google Ventures) and partners with defense, aerospace, and automotive organizations including Kia, Supacat, Galvion, Patria, and General Dynamics. The company publishes no public API or developer program; this profile tracks its identity and public web surface in the API Evangelist network.

Co-founded by Chris Bell, Lexie Dostal, and Stephen Bell and based primarily out of Portland and Los Angeles, Gardens raised a $31.3M Series A co-led by Lightspeed Venture Partners. providers.name: Third Dimension AI
providers.description: Third Dimension AI is a spatial-generation company building high-fidelity 3D worlds and simulation for embodied AI, autonomy, robotics, gaming, and entertainment. Its core product, SuperSim, models the world across the full fidelity spectrum - from real-world reconstruction of scenes captured from sensor data to open-ended generative simulation - so autonomy teams can validate, train, and deploy AI systems and close the simulation-to-reality domain gap without hand-built 3D art. Founded by Tolga Kart (CEO) and Piotr Sokolski (CTO), with Oxford professor Christian Rupprecht as Chief Researcher, the team draws on experience from Wayve, Tesla, Google, Luma AI, Nvidia, Niantic, Amazon, and Unity. The company raised $7 million and is backed by Felicis. As of this profile it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; enrichment captured its identity and probed its domain security posture.

Light & Wonder operates customer-facing support portals for both gaming and iGaming partners.

providers.name: Createra
providers.description: Createra is a user-generated-content (UGC) gaming metaverse platform backed by Andreessen Horowitz, built by the Code Infinity team associated with the youth-coding company Codemao. The platform lets creators build and publish infinitely engaging 3D worlds and games directly in the browser, founded on the belief that creativity is a talent that everyone possesses. Its Box3 creation platform published a first-party JavaScript web SDK to npm as @box3/web-sdk. As of a July 2026 probe the createra.fun website returns no response over HTTP or HTTPS, no developer portal, documentation, API reference, OpenAPI definition, or /.well-known discovery surface could be located, and the npm SDK has not been republished since January 2023 — this profile therefore records Createra as a dormant company with no active public API surface.

providers.name: YoloRekt
providers.description: YOLOrekt is a social, hyper-gamified DeFi prediction-markets dApp where users bid on the short-term future price of crypto assets such as ETH, BTC, and MATIC, or provide in-game liquidity to earn game fees and YOLO rewards. Built on the Polygon network for high transaction speed, negligible fees, and full EVM support, YOLOrekt is delivered as Ethereum and Polygon smart contracts (including a first-of-its-kind synced dual-token issuance across both chains) rather than a traditional REST/GraphQL API. Backed by Pantera Capital and surfaced into the API Evangelist network as a crypto portfolio company; the yolorekt.finance domain no longer resolves and the project appears dormant, with its surviving public surface being the YOLOrekt GitHub organization, community bug-bounty programs, and the YOLOrekt Medium publication.

providers.name: agavegames
providers.description: Agave Games is a mobile game publisher based in Istanbul, Turkey, founded in 2021 by Alper Oner, Burak Kar, and Ali Baran Terzioglu. The company specializes in casual puzzle games played by millions, with titles including Find the Cat, Wonder Link, What The Hex, Soda Match, and Art Block Puzzle across iOS and Android. Backed by Balderton Capital and Felix Capital (Series A, December 2024), Agave Games is a consumer-facing gaming company; it publishes no public developer portal, API, or documentation surface. This profile was surfaced as a Balderton Capital portfolio company and enriched with a live domain-security probe and identity hygiene.

providers.name: BLAST
providers.description: BLAST is a Danish esports and gaming entertainment company headquartered in Copenhagen, founded in 2016. It produces and operates premier competitive gaming tournaments and leagues (notably Counter-Strike BLAST Premier) and runs the blast.tv streaming and fan-engagement platform, delivering live events, broadcasts, and interactive esports content to a global audience. Backed by Creandum, Heartcore, Maki.vc, and Vaekstfonden, BLAST was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead company. No public developer API, portal, or documentation surface was found during enrichment; this profile captures verifiable identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Brain Jar Games
providers.description: Brain Jar Games is a fully-remote independent video game studio founded by AAA industry veterans who have shipped franchises including Mass Effect, Dragon Age, RIFT, and Call of Duty. The studio builds bold, vibrant, music-driven action games designed to be shared; its debut title, Dead as Disco, blends kinetic gunplay with rhythm-synced choreography. Brain Jar Games is backed by Menlo Ventures and Transcend, having raised $12.2M across seed funding, and operates a four-day, 32-hour work week with team members across North America, Europe, and Turkey. The company publishes no public API, SDK, or developer platform; this profile tracks it as a venture-portfolio lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Drill Creative
providers.description: Drill Creative, Inc. is a US-based video game development startup founded in 2023 in Cary, North Carolina, and backed by a16z's Speedrun accelerator. The studio builds original, high-quality gameplay experiences for user-generated content (UGC) platforms, the coin-op / family-entertainment-center (FEC) market, and PC and console storefronts. Its early releases are built on Fortnite via Unreal Editor for Fortnite (UEFN), including "Elimination Confirmed," a 16-player competitive first-person shooter, and "Robo Bash," an arcade-style four-player fighting game. Drill Creative is a games company rather than an API provider: it publishes no public developer portal, API, SDK, or technical documentation, so this profile carries company identity only and no API artifacts.

providers.name: Endless Studios LLC
providers.description: Endless Studios LLC is a game development learning platform where aspiring creators learn to build video games through real, pro-studio projects. Its Endstar game engine lets creators code and collaborate in real time, while structured programs (Launchpad for beginners, Capstone for advanced participants) pair learners with 30+ game-industry mentors, expert playtesting, and collaborator matching across design, art, and programming. Learners build portfolios of shipped games to show potential employers. The company runs university, government, and partner programs (including a UAE national game-making competition) and is a 500 Global portfolio company. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; no public developer/API surface was found during enrichment (consumer/creator-facing product on the studio.endlessstudios.com app).

providers.name: GlamSt
providers.description: GlamSt (GlamST LLC) builds customized virtual makeover and try-on solutions for beauty brands and retailers, combining augmented reality (AR), artificial intelligence, and machine learning to power virtual makeup and cosmetics try-on across mobile, web, and in-store experiences. Founded with offices in San Francisco, Montevideo (Uruguay), and Wilmington (Delaware), the company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. GlamSt was acquired by Ulta Beauty in 2018 and integrated into Ulta's digital innovation team; it exposes no public developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface, so this profile is identity-only.

providers.name: Puzzlium
providers.description: Puzzlium is a mobile puzzle platform and social network built around the tagline "Play. Create. Compete." Founded in 2014 by veteran puzzle designers Serhiy Grabarchuk, Serhiy Grabarchuk Jr., Peter Grabarchuk, and Mehmet Murat Sevim, the iOS and Amazon Kindle app lets a community of hundreds of thousands of solvers and creators play, generate, publish, and compete with interactive puzzles. Based in San Jose, California and backed by 500 Startups (500 Global), Puzzlium is a consumer application that does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Take Two
providers.description: Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc. (NASDAQ: TTWO) is a leading developer, publisher, and marketer of interactive entertainment for consumers worldwide, headquartered in New York City. The company delivers its products principally through three wholly owned labels — Rockstar Games, 2K, and Zynga — spanning console, PC, and mobile platforms via physical retail, digital download, online platforms, and cloud streaming. Franchises include Grand Theft Auto, Red Dead Redemption, NBA 2K, Borderlands, and mobile titles such as Words With Friends and Toon Blast. Take-Two is a publicly traded interactive entertainment holding company; it does not publish a public developer API program, developer portal, or API documentation at the corporate level. This profile was surfaced as a general-catalyst job-board listing and carried into the API Evangelist network as a lead; enrichment found no public API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Synthesis AI
providers.description: Synthesis AI was a San Francisco synthetic-data company, founded in 2019 by Yashar Behzadi, that generated photorealistic, pixel-perfectly labeled images of humans for training computer-vision models. It sold that capability as an API: FaceAPI for labeled facial imagery and, from November 2021, HumanAPI for whole-body 3D digital humans, plus an Identities API for selecting subjects. Jobs were described as JSON documents (identities, expressions, gaze, head turn, hair, accessories, bodies and clothing, gesture animations, camera and light rigs, HDRI environments) and submitted through a command-line client or web console, with rendered output downloaded by job ID. The company raised a $17M Series A in 2022 on more than $24M total funding and was dissolved during 2024-2025. Its API is gone: synthesis.ai is a parked Gandi holding page reachable only over HTTP, and docs.synthesis.ai and api.synthesis.ai no longer resolve. What survives publicly is the Synthesis-AI-Dev GitHub organization (17 public repositories, including the Human API input-JSON appendix and the client tooling) and the official synthesisai package on PyPI.

The product is a business-to-consumer collecting and squad-building experience delivered through its mobile apps and website at matchday.com. As of this enrichment pass, Matchday does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or documentation surface: probing api.matchday.com, docs.matchday.com, and developer.matchday.com returned no reachable developer hosts, and the marketing site is a single-page application. This profile therefore carries company identity plus a domain-security probe rather than API artifacts, and remains a lead to revisit if a public API surface is launched.

providers.name: Oculus VR
providers.description: Oculus VR is the pioneering virtual reality company founded in 2012 and acquired by Facebook (now Meta) in 2014. Its Rift, Go, and Quest headsets defined consumer VR, and the Oculus brand has since been folded into Meta Quest and Meta Horizon OS. The former developer.oculus.com and oculus.com properties now redirect to Meta's developer platform. There is no distinct public REST/OpenAPI surface; developers build against SDK-based tooling (Unity, Unreal Engine, native OpenXR, and the Meta Spatial SDK) rather than a hosted web API. Backed originally by a16z; consumer VR/AR hardware and platform.

providers.name: Heyzap
providers.description: Heyzap was a mobile-game advertising, discovery, and monetization company. It began as a social game-discovery network and pivoted into a mobile ad mediation platform, offering iOS, Android, Unity, Cordova, and Adobe AIR/ANE SDKs that let game developers serve and mediate ads across networks such as AdMob, AppLovin, Vungle, Chartboost, AdColony, and Facebook Audience Network. Heyzap was acquired by Fyber (RNTS Media) in 2016 and its brand was later folded into Digital Turbine. Heyzap never published a public REST API; its developer surface was the mobile ad-mediation SDKs distributed via GitHub (github.com/Heyzap) and package registries. The heyzap.com domain is now parked/for-sale and the developer documentation site no longer resolves; this profile preserves the historical, first-party SDK artifacts that remain publicly available. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures.

providers.name: Placenote
providers.description: Placenote (Vertical AI Inc.) was a San Francisco company that built a cloud-hosted persistent augmented-reality toolkit — a "Persistent AR" SDK that let developers save, reload, and share ARKit/Unity spatial maps so digital content stays anchored to a physical location across sessions and devices. It shipped native client SDKs for iOS (Swift, via the PlacenoteSDK CocoaPod) and Unity, plus multiplayer AR samples such as PlaceInvaders and web mesh-viewing examples. The product was consumed as mobile SDKs backed by a cloud mapping/localization service rather than a public REST API, so no OpenAPI or web API surface was published. The company is now defunct: placenote.com no longer resolves to a live product (the domain is parked) and the docs/cloud service are offline. The Placenote GitHub organization and the published SDKs remain the only live, first-party developer surface, which is what this profile captures.

providers.name: Crater Studios
providers.description: Crater Studios is an AI-native game studio that builds core AI systems for game design, decision making, and live operations, trained on real player behavior in production environments. The company uses its own live game launches as production laboratories, shipping titles such as Dwarven Realms, Gravebound, and Doomspire on Steam while building agentic tooling around them - a GDD Maker that turns raw concepts into production-ready game design documents, a conversational decision engine wired to live telemetry, automated playtesting agents, content moderation, and localization. Crater publishes a set of playable browser prototypes on craterstudios.ai subdomains as proof that its design agents can produce working core loops. Surfaced as an a16z portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass Crater Studios publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable specification - its AI systems are internal platform infrastructure rather than a developer product.

providers.name: Drop
providers.description: Drop (formerly Massdrop) is a consumer e-commerce brand operated by Corsair that sells limited-edition, community-driven products across mechanical keyboards, audiophile gear, and licensed gaming collaborations (Fallout, Cyberpunk 2077, The Witcher, Call of Duty and others). Founded in San Francisco and backed by Cowboy Ventures and other investors before its acquisition by Corsair, Drop runs a direct-to-consumer storefront at drop.com with a Zendesk-based support helpdesk. It is a retail brand with no public developer API program; this API Evangelist profile tracks it as a company in the network.

providers.name: Unleashed Games
providers.description: Unleashed Games is an independent game studio founded by industry veterans (World of Warcraft, Medal of Honor, Monopoly Go!) and backed by a16z Speedrun, building socially-driven cooperative games. Its flagship title Haven is a cross-platform co-op RPG for families and friends spanning PC, Mac, console, and mobile, with procedurally generated maps, village building, and collaborative combat. The studio publishes no public developer platform or API surface today.

providers.name: Airborne Entertainment
providers.description: Airborne Entertainment was a Montreal, Quebec mobile entertainment company founded in 2000 that published and distributed premium mobile content and applications for carrier decks and early smartphones, including games, ringtones, ring-back tones, images, video and informational content, often under licensed consumer brands. The company raised a $22M round in July 2004 with participation from Insight Partners and Verizon, sold a majority stake to Japan's CYBIRD Co., Ltd. in 2005, was taken back by management in a 2008 buy-out, operated afterwards as Airborne Mobile, and was acquired by Bandsintown in October 2010. It no longer operates as an independent company: both airborneentertainment.com and airbornemobile.com are parked domain-sale listings, and the company never published a public developer portal, API, or SDK surface. This profile is retained as an API Evangelist network history record.

providers.name: Blue Vision Labs
providers.description: Blue Vision Labs was a London-based computer-vision company that built the first city-scale augmented reality cloud — crowdsourcing centimetre-accurate 3D maps of entire cities from images captured by car-mounted smartphone cameras, then letting developers use visual positioning to place shared and persistent AR content that every device sees in the same real-world spot. It emerged from stealth in March 2018 with a $14.5M round led by GV, alongside Accel and Horizons Ventures, and offered invite-only early access to iOS and Android SDKs covering San Francisco, New York City and London. Lyft acquired the company in October 2018 and made it the UK hub of its Level 5 self-driving division. The developer platform is retired: bluevisionlabs.com no longer resolves to a web host, the documentation and SDK downloads are offline, and no public API surface remains.

providers.name: Metafy
providers.description: Metafy is a consumer marketplace for gaming coaching and mentorship, connecting players with expert coaches and professional gamers for personalized one-on-one lessons, VOD reviews, and guides across popular competitive titles. Metafy operates a consumer web platform at metafy.gg and, as of this enrichment pass, publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation; the only machine-discoverable surface found was an RFC 9116 /.well-known/security.txt security contact. Surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures.

providers.name: MoonActive
providers.description: MoonActive is a mobile game developer and publisher best known for the casual titles Coin Master and Pet Master. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As a consumer gaming company MoonActive publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; the enrichment pass captured its security and domain posture only (a published RFC 9116 security.txt with a security contact and disclosure page, plus probed TLS/SPF/DMARC).

providers.name: Singularity6
providers.description: Singularity 6 is a Los Angeles-based video game development studio founded in 2018 by a team of experienced developers, several of them Riot Games alumni, with the mission of forging alternate worlds that deepen players' lives. The studio is the developer and publisher of Palia, a free-to-play community simulation MMO where players build a cozy life, craft, farm, fish, and explore a shared social world with friends. Palia launched into open beta on PC and Nintendo Switch and has grown to millions of registered players. Singularity 6 was acquired by Daybreak Game Company in 2024. The company operates a consumer gaming business and does not publish a public developer API program; this profile documents the company's public web presence rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Summoners Arena
providers.description: Summoners Arena is a blockchain-based, multi-genre play-to-earn game universe set in the antique lore of Summonia, where players summon, evolve, and battle NFT heroes across PvP modes (Arena, Battleground) and PvE content (Dungeon, Campaign), with an in-game NFT marketplace supporting hero renting, equipment collection, and forging. Backed by Pantera Capital, it operates in the Web3 / crypto gaming sector. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; the company publishes a consumer game and community surface but no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or well-known discovery documents were found.

providers.name: Fantasmo
providers.description: Fantasmo builds CPS (Camera Positioning System), a computer-vision positioning technology it positions as a "camera-powered GPS replacement" delivering hyper-accurate localization that works indoors and in dense urban environments where satellite GPS degrades, using only a device camera and a data connection rather than additional infrastructure. Its target applications span micromobility (scooter/bike tracking and theft prevention), robotics navigation, mobile augmented-reality experiences, and automotive lane-level positioning. Fantasmo was a Techstars-backed startup and was acquired by Niantic in 2022; the public fantasmo.io site remains online but exposes no developer portal, API reference, SDK, or OpenAPI surface at this time. This profile was enriched from the provider's public web presence and live DNS/TLS/HTTP probes.

providers.name: Surglasses Inc.
providers.description: Surglasses Inc. (SURGLASSES) is a medical technology manufacturer of augmented reality surgical guidance systems and medical education products. Its portfolio includes AR-guided surgical navigation for orthopedic, spine, and neurosurgery procedures (the Foresee-X AR surgical glasses), 3D computer surgical navigation and planning software, and the Asclepius AI Table and Virtual Dissection Table for anatomy, radiology, and histopathology education. Backed by 500 Global. The company operates as a B2B medical-device manufacturer and publishes no public developer, API, or SDK surface at this time.

providers.name: Darewise
providers.description: Darewise Entertainment is a European game studio founded by AAA industry veterans — game director Benjamin Charbit (Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag) and engine tech lead Samuel Kahn (Ubisoft Snowdrop, Crytek CryEngine) — with offices in Paris, London and Barcelona. It builds Life Beyond, a free-to-play sci-fi MMO on Unreal Engine 5 set on the alien world Dolos, combining Web3 asset ownership (NFTs and ERC-20 tokens) with player-driven settlement and governance. Animoca Brands announced the acquisition of a majority stake in April 2022, and the studio now trades as Life Beyond Studios. The original darewise.com website last served content in April 2025 and the host now refuses TCP connections on 80 and 443. Darewise publishes no API, developer portal, or API documentation of any kind; the only machine-readable developer artifact it has ever released publicly is an open-source AsyncAPI generator template that emits Unreal Engine C++ from an AsyncAPI 3.x document, published to npm under its own scope.

providers.name: Elsewhere
providers.description: Elsewhere (Elsewhere Communities Inc.) is a San Francisco based video game studio founded in 2024 by Paul Sawaya, previously co-founder and CTO of Human Interest. The studio was part of cohort 001 of a16z SPEEDRUN, the Andreessen Horowitz accelerator for games and interactive media. Elsewhere describes itself as "a new kind of video game studio emboldened by the desire to rethink the industry", treating artificial intelligence as a normal technology and building games that use generative AI in a humanistic direction rather than a dystopian one. The studio previously worked on a multiplayer roguelike — games "that feel like an adventure you go on with your friends, and the adventure is never the same twice" — and is currently building something new. Elsewhere is a consumer game studio with no public developer platform: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no API, no developer portal, no SDKs, and no machine-readable discovery documents.

providers.name: First Day Entertainment
providers.description: First Day Entertainment Inc. is a Sunnyvale, California game studio building AI-powered games, founded by Stephen Gou (formerly a founding engineer at Cohere) and Mike Mei, and funded by the a16z SPEEDRUN accelerator (batch 002) and MiraclePlus. The studio ships two titles - Heroes of Magic & Cards, a poker deckbuilding roguelike distributed on Steam, and Mana Land, a single-player RPG in which players adventure alongside conversational AI companions, published on itch.io. First Day Entertainment is a consumer games company; it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API artifacts as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Hike
providers.description: Hike Private Limited is a New Delhi consumer internet company founded in 2011 by Kavin Bharti Mittal. It is best known for Hike Messenger, launched in December 2012 and at its peak one of India's largest homegrown messaging apps, which the company retired in January 2021 to pivot into the Rush Gaming Universe — a mobile-first skill-gaming platform that layered Web3 ownership and play-to-earn mechanics over roughly fourteen casual titles. Hike raised approximately $261M across seven rounds from investors including SoftBank, Tencent, Tiger Global and Polygon, and reached unicorn valuation in 2021. In September 2025, after India's Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act banned real-money gaming, the founder announced a complete wind-down of the company and of Rush. As of August 2026 hike.in still resolves but serves an HTTP 502 behind an expired certificate, and every developer-facing subdomain is NXDOMAIN; the company publishes no API, developer portal, or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Second Dinner
providers.description: Second Dinner is an independent, remote-first video game studio headquartered in Irvine, California, founded in 2018 by a group of former Blizzard Hearthstone developers including Hamilton Chu, Ben Brode, Yong Woo, Jomaro Kindred and Michael Schweitzer. Its debut title, MARVEL SNAP, is a fast-paced digital collectible card game built in Unity that won Mobile Game of the Year at both The Game Awards and the DICE Awards along with an Apple Design Award, and the studio has since been reported to be building its next title on the Godot engine. Second Dinner raised a $100M Series B led by Griffin Gaming Partners in January 2024. The studio ships consumer games rather than developer platforms: it publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable specification, and its public engineering footprint is a small GitHub organization of Unity build and test tooling forks.

providers.name: TrueFlip
providers.description: TrueFlip was an international anonymous blockchain lottery with instant payouts, open-source draw code, and a transparent prize fund, launched in 2017 with an Ethereum token ICO and backed by Pantera Capital. The company's GitHub organization has been dormant since 2018, and the trueflip.io domain is suspended at the registrar (clientHold) with no DNS records; by early 2026 the domain was serving unrelated crypto-casino affiliate content. No public API, developer documentation, SDK packages, or machine-readable surface was found. Profile retained as a Pantera Capital portfolio record.

providers.name: Unikrn
providers.description: Unikrn was an esports betting and entertainment company founded in November 2014 by Rahul Sood and Karl Flores, headquartered in Seattle and backed by investors including Mark Cuban, Ashton Kutcher, 500 Global, and Pantera Capital. The platform offered real-money and token-based wagering on competitive video game tournaments (CS:GO, League of Legends, Dota 2, and more) and ran a $30M ICO for its UnikoinGold (UKG) cryptocurrency in 2017, which it later disabled as part of a 2021 SEC settlement. Unikrn was acquired by Entain in August 2021, and the unikrn.com betting site was permanently closed on October 20, 2023. The domain now serves only a farewell notice; the company publishes no APIs, developer portal, or public technical artifacts.

providers.name: Cryptoys
providers.description: Cryptoys is an Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) backed Web3 digital collectibles company that lets fans buy, own, and play with blockchain-based interactive toys featuring licensed characters from Disney and Star Wars alongside original IP. Products are sold as blind boxes containing randomized digital toys across multiple power tiers and rarity levels. The company has since rebranded and now operates its consumer experience as Digitoys at digitoys.io, while retaining its identity account service at auth.cryptoys.com. Cryptoys is a consumer-facing collectibles platform and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web and identity surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: forgame
providers.description: Forgame Holdings Limited (HKEX 00484) is a Hong Kong-listed technology holding company founded in 2009 and headquartered in Shenzhen, China. It operates across cloud/light gaming, fintech, electronic trade, and cloud storage. Its web and mobile game publishing platform 91wan, run by PRC entity Guangzhou Weidong Internet Technology Co., Ltd., has distributed over 100 web games and attracted more than 200 million registered players. In 2016 the group obtained an internet micro-lending (fintech) license in the PRC, and since 2019 has explored e-sports and virtual-reality games. Forgame is tracked by API Evangelist as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners; no public developer API or documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Jetapult
providers.description: Jetapult is a capital and support firm focused on scaling mobile game studios, combining operator-first funding with hands-on systems for monetization, user acquisition, market expansion, and operational efficiency. Its GamePac AI toolset helps indie studios create, grow, and monetize their games. Jetapult is backed by Accel and operates as a partner-and-capital platform for gaming studios such as Holy Cow Studio and UMX Studio. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Jetapult does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Metatheory
providers.description: Metatheory, Inc. is an independent studio of builders that makes games and, through an AI-led software division, tools built for makers. The team describes itself as builders, dreamers and doers applying what they have learned making games to software, building in public and sharing what they learn. Metatheory has been surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and Pantera Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the public site (metatheory.gg) is a single-page marketing site with no developer portal, documentation, API, OpenAPI, SDK, or public developer surface; the only public contact is support@metatheory.gg.

providers.name: Mira
providers.description: Mira is a San Francisco-based consumer hardware startup building AI-powered smart glasses positioned as an always-on "second brain." Founded in 2024 by Harvard builders AnhPhu Nguyen and Caine Ardayfio (rebranded from Halo), the camera-free glasses pair a dual-waveguide display, microphone, and iOS companion app to deliver live transcription, real-time translation across 60+ languages, hands-free AI assistance, and searchable memory of everyday conversations. Mira raised a $6.6M seed round led by General Catalyst and began shipping its first devices in January 2026. It is a privacy-first consumer wearable with an iOS companion app and does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Rovio
providers.description: Rovio Entertainment is a Finnish mobile games company best known for the Angry Birds franchise. Founded in 2003 and headquartered in Espoo, Finland, Rovio operates multiple game studios and became part of Sega in 2023. It is a consumer entertainment company; its public web presence covers games, careers, press, and support, and it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub for enrichment.

providers.name: Theorycraft Games
providers.description: Theorycraft Games is an independent video game studio backed by a16z, best known for developing SUPERVIVE, a free-to-play hero shooter / MOBA-battle-royale hybrid. Surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a consumer game and community presence but no public developer API, developer portal, API documentation, SDK, or OpenAPI surface; the corporate site is in maintenance mode.

providers.name: Dream11
providers.description: Dream11 is India's largest fantasy sports platform, operated by Sporta Technologies Private Limited and part of the Dream Sports group founded in 2008 by Harsh Jain and Bhavit Sheth and headquartered in Mumbai. Launched as a freemium fantasy game in 2012, it lets 140 million-plus users draft virtual teams and compete in free and paid contests across cricket, football, kabaddi, basketball and hockey, scoring on the real-world performance of the athletes they pick. Dream11 is a consumer, mobile-first product with no public consumer API program; its engineering organization does maintain public open-source infrastructure (Kong rate-limiter and circuit-breaker plugins, the Odin deployment tool) on GitHub and publishes an engineering blog.

providers.name: Take-Two Interactive Software
providers.description: Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc. is a leading developer, publisher, and marketer of interactive entertainment. The company operates through its publishing labels: Rockstar Games (Grand Theft Auto, Red Dead Redemption), 2K (NBA 2K, Borderlands, Civilization, BioShock, Mafia), Private Division, and Zynga (mobile games). Headquartered in New York City, Take-Two is a Fortune 500 company with studios across North America, Europe, and Asia. No public developer API is currently available.

providers.name: All3D
providers.description: ALL3D, Inc. is a San Francisco AI-powered visual content platform that replaces traditional product photography for ecommerce brands and agencies. Users upload a product photo and its real-world dimensions, build a scene from inspiration images and props, and generate 4K studio and lifestyle images, influencer/UGC-style video, editable 3D models, 360-degree spins, product configurators, and AR "view in room" experiences accurate to real-world scale. Additional tools cover magic erase, item replacement, scale adjustment, bulk generation across hundreds of SKUs, team review/approval workflows, and direct publishing to Shopify and Amazon. Enterprise plans add API access and managed services. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bullpen Capital and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.description: Coolso develops wearable gesture-recognition technology. Using patented sensing that detects muscle-vibration signals processed through its own AI model, Coolso recognizes individual finger movements and strength levels with low-latency response, from a wrist-worn device or an ordinary smartwatch's accelerometer and gyroscope without dedicated hardware. Founded by Sheng-Kuei Hsu, Wei-Lin Lee, and Jack Wu and based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, the seed-stage company is backed by 500 Global and Alchemist Accelerator and targets AR/VR interaction, with potential expansion into medical rehabilitation and sports equipment. Coolso publishes no public API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.description: Level Headed Games (Level Headed, LLC) is an independent video game studio building an original online cooperative multiplayer game. The studio describes itself as passionate about making immersive experiences that let players express themselves and have fun with their friends, and is building "fun, surprising, and heavily social video game worlds." Development is community-involved, with an open call for co-op players to join an Alpha playtest community and an email announcement list. As of this enrichment pass the studio publishes only a single-page marketing site with no announced title, no public developer surface, and no API, SDK, documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: MoonFrost
providers.description: MoonFrost is a cozy life-sim RPG developed by Oxalis Games Ltd., set in a world ravaged by constant meteor storms where players farm, fish, craft, and build their dream home. Positioned as a Web3 game, it is backed by crypto investor Pantera Capital and is available to wishlist on Steam and the Epic Games Store, with a community on Discord. As of this profile, MoonFrost publishes no public API, developer documentation, SDK, or developer portal — it is a consumer game rather than an API provider, so this record is identity-only pending any future developer surface.

providers.name: PKO Inc.
providers.description: PKO is a collective and investment group operating at the intersection of technology and entertainment. Describing itself as a community of founders, creators, execs, artists, angels and investors with more than 700 members, PKO runs online and offline networking events, mixers and collaborations, and invests in startups across metaverse, virtual worlds, VR/AR, web3 (crypto, NFTs, DAOs), the creator economy, gaming and esports, social media, platforms, marketplaces, communities, streaming video, and content and media. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. PKO publishes no public API, SDK, or developer surface; founders submit pitches by email.

As of July 2026 the company publishes no public API surface, and its primary domain veer.tv redirects to veervr.com, which no longer resolves.

providers.name: Wildcard
providers.description: Wildcard is a PvP collectible-card-based MOBA (multiplayer online battle arena) developed by Playful Studios and currently in Early Access on Steam. Players pick Champions, assemble decks of Summon creature cards, and compete in real-time strategic arena battles where deck-building matters as much as mechanical skill. The game ships collectible cosmetics (Wildpass, Flair, Wildfile) with a web3 angle — the Wildpass is a Polygon NFT collection tradeable on Magic Eden — and is backed as a portfolio company of the crypto venture firm Paradigm. Its backend gaming services are built on Beamable and Unreal Engine. No first-party public developer API, SDK, or documentation portal is published; this profile is a company/lead record in the API Evangelist network. Sector: gaming.

providers.name: Dots
providers.description: Dots is a mobile games studio founded in 2013 by Paul Murphy and Patrick Moberg, known for minimalist, calming puzzle games including Dots, Two Dots, and Dots & Co. The studio focused on well-designed, easy-to-approach games and player-friendly monetization, measuring success by how players feel rather than aggressive in-app spending. Backed by Northzone, Slow Ventures, Tencent, Greycroft, and CrunchFund, Dots was acquired by Take-Two Interactive in August 2020. This is a consumer gaming company with no public developer API surface; it was added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio stub and this enrichment pass confirmed it exposes no API, SDK, or documentation.

providers.name: Elodie
providers.description: Elodie Games is an independent video game studio founded in 2019 and headquartered in Venice, California, building endlessly-playable cross-play PvE cooperative games for PC, console, and mobile. Co-founded by Christina Norman (design leadership on Mass Effect 1-3, League of Legends, and League of Legends: Wild Rift) and David Banks (former executive producer of League of Legends at Riot Games), the studio is focused on deeply social, cross-platform gameplay so friends and family can play together regardless of device or skill level. Elodie's Series A was co-led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Galaxy Interactive. Elodie publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation portal; its backend stack (AWS, Kotlin, gRPC/Protobuf, DynamoDB, MySQL) is internal-only, so there is no API artifact surface to enrich for this provider.

providers.name: Iconic
providers.description: Iconic (Iconic Interactive) is an AI gaming studio building real-time AI systems for video games and interactive storytelling — "Digital Actor" technology that lets game characters listen, react, and evolve alongside the player by combining speech recognition, large language models, and text-to-speech into low-latency conversational performances. Founded by veterans of GTA, Forza, Just Cause, and Sleeping Dogs with AI researchers from Cambridge and Imperial College, the company is backed by Northzone. Its flagship title, The Oversight Bureau, ships a demo on Steam. Iconic operates a marketing site, a Labs surface, and a technical blog; it does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDKs. This profile was surfaced as a Northzone portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Iconicgames
providers.description: Iconic Interactive (iconicgames.io) is a game development studio building real-time AI systems for gameplay and interactive storytelling. The team combines game developers and AI scientists with credits on major franchises including GTA, Forza, and Just Cause, and is developing a game demo, "The Oversight Bureau," available on Steam. The company is backed by Kindred Ventures. As of this enrichment pass the studio publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or developer documentation; this profile captures its public identity and the security posture of its web domain. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Kindred Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Instaplay
providers.description: Instaplay is an AI-native social gaming platform that turns plain-text prompts into playable multiplayer games with no coding required. Users describe a game idea in natural language ("a two-player pong game where paddles shrink after every point") and the platform generates a playable prototype that can be tested, remixed, and shared via link within seconds. It supports party, co-op, competitive, local, online, and solo formats. Founded in San Francisco and part of Y Combinator's Summer 2026 batch, Instaplay frames games as a training ground for world models and embodied agents on the path to AGI.

providers.name: Methodical Games
providers.description: Methodical Games is an independent AAA game development studio building award-winning multiplayer games, describing itself as "built by developers, for developers." Founded by veterans of Infinity Ward, Respawn Entertainment, Epic Games and Santa Monica Studio, its lean team has shipped and shaped franchises including Call of Duty, Titanfall, Apex Legends, Fortnite, Gears of War and God of War Ragnarok. The studio emphasizes a developer-driven process of fundamentals, quick iteration and collaboration to craft immersive, long-lived multiplayer experiences. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As a game studio it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal surface at this time; this profile captures its identity and public web presence.

providers.name: Odyssey Ai
providers.description: Odyssey is an AI research lab building general-purpose world models — causal, multimodal systems that understand and simulate physical environments, generating long-form interactive video simulations from text or image prompts rather than text. Its research includes Odyssey-2 (a flagship world model producing multi-minute interactive simulations), Starchild-1 (a real-time multimodal world model), Agora-1 (a multi-agent world simulator), and PROWL-1 (a reinforcement-learning framework for adversarial environment exploration). Odyssey positions world models as foundational AI for robotics, gaming, healthcare, education, and 3D visual asset generation, and raised a $310M Series B. The company is a portfolio company of DCVC. At the time of this profile Odyssey publishes research, writing, and interactive demos but exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Altera
providers.description: Altera is an applied AI research company founded in December 2023 by former MIT computational neuroscientist Robert Yang, building "digital human beings" — autonomous, collaborative, and socially intelligent AI agents. Its research began with multi-agent experiments in games such as Minecraft and Roblox (agents that can play alongside a person like a friend), and produced Project Sid, a large-scale AI-agent civilization powered by its PIANO architecture. The team is drawn from MIT EECS, the Stanford NLP Group, Google X, and Citadel. Altera raised a $2M pre-seed and a $9M seed (backers include a16z SPEEDRUN, Patron, First Spark Ventures, and Eric Schmidt) and has since rebranded to Fundamental Research Labs following a $33M Series A led by Prosus. Altera is a research organization and does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or client SDKs; its only public developer surface is the altera-al GitHub organization (the project-sid research codebase).

providers.name: bash.gg
providers.description: bash.gg was a browser-based indie game marketplace built on Solana (founded by Kyle Zappitell, a former Xbox engineer) that let independent developers sell games directly in the browser without the ~30% platform commissions charged by Steam, Xbox, Apple, and PlayStation, with 10% royalties routed back to developers on resale. It entered the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead and was kept as a stub. Re-probed on 2026-07-20, the company remains defunct - the bash.gg domain is parked for sale on the GoDaddy/Afternic aftermarket (NS delegated to afternic.com, null MX, SPF "-all"), there is no live developer portal, API, or documentation, and the company GitHub organization (github.com/bash-gg) exists but publishes zero repositories. Wayback captures show the site only ever exposed Next.js/NextAuth internal routes (/api/auth/session), never a public developer API. No provider artifacts could be searched, generated, or derived. No fabrication was performed.

providers.name: BrainTripping
providers.description: BrainTripping is a whimsical Markov-chain language game founded by Matthew Huebert in the Y Combinator Summer 2012 batch. It lets players step inside the vocabularies of famous historical and modern figures and compose their own sentences, constrained to that person's word patterns. The company is no longer active as a startup; today the BrainTripping GitHub organization publishes open-source ClojureScript tooling such as cljs-live, magic-tree, and the Lark editor. The public surface is a single-page ClojureScript web app at braintripping.com and it exposes no public REST API, SDK, or developer platform.

providers.name: Caffeine
providers.description: Caffeine was a social broadcasting and live-streaming platform founded in 2016 by former Apple designers Ben Keighran and Sam Roberts, and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Greylock Partners. Built on a proprietary WebRTC-based real-time video distribution network, Caffeine positioned itself as a low-latency, social-first alternative to Twitch for gaming, entertainment, and — in its later years — live sports, partnering with roughly 200 sports organizations and reaching tens of millions of monthly users. The company published open-source broadcasting tooling under its caffeinetv GitHub organization (libcaffeine, caffeine-rtc, an OBS plugin, and the CaffQL GraphQL code generator) but never shipped a public, documented developer API program. Caffeine announced it was ceasing operations, and its web presence is now a shutdown notice; this profile is retained as an a16z portfolio lead and is archival rather than an active, integrable API provider.

providers.name: CTRL-labs *
providers.description: CTRL-labs was a neurotechnology company founded in 2015 in New York City (originally Cognescent) by Thomas Reardon, Patrick Kaifosh, and Tim Machado, building a non-invasive neural interface: a wrist-worn band that reads surface electromyography (sEMG) signals from motor neurons to decode intended hand and finger movements for human-computer interaction. Its developer hardware was the CTRL-kit, and it acquired the Myo armband patents from North. In fall 2019 CTRL-labs was acquired by Facebook and folded into Facebook (now Meta) Reality Labs, where the technology became the basis of Meta's neuromotor wristband for AR glasses (detailed in a July 2025 Nature paper). The company no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no public API, SDK, or developer platform; this record is retained as an acquired-company lead.

providers.name: Emergent VR *
providers.description: Emergent VR was a San Francisco Bay Area virtual-reality startup backed by GV (Google Ventures), where it is listed in the portfolio with the asterisk GV uses to mark exited companies. The enrichment pass found no live company web presence: the former emergentvr.com domain now resolves to an unrelated third-party blog, and the company's GitHub organization (github.com/EmergentVR, created March 2015) holds only ten repositories, all of them OpenCV builds and a fork of Google's cardboard-unity SDK, with no activity after June 2016. No developer portal, documentation, API, SDK, or event surface exists for this company, so no API artifacts were produced. Sector: consumer / virtual reality.

providers.name: GGFolks
providers.description: GGFolks (Good Game Folks) is a small, experimental independent game-development group that publishes its work as open source on GitHub under the ggfolks organization, with the tagline "We make good feels." Its repositories are early-stage games and supporting tooling rather than a commercial API product: platform is a TypeScript social-multiplayer web game framework (the `tfw` package, MIT-licensed), moncher is a monster-ranching social game, spaced is a web-based space editor, chatapp is a Dart messaging experiment, and ggdobj/esl provide shared C#/Unity client-server and simulation code. GGFolks does not publish a public developer portal, hosted API, OpenAPI definition, or released client SDK, so it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile with no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Hasbro
providers.description: Hasbro is a global play and entertainment company committed to making the world a better place for children and their families through brands and franchises including NERF, MAGIC: THE GATHERING, MY LITTLE PONY, and TRANSFORMERS. This repository tracks public APIs, developer resources, and machine-readable API artifacts associated with Hasbro. No public developer APIs have been published at this time.

providers.name: Lego
providers.description: The LEGO Group is a Danish toy company and the world's largest manufacturer of interlocking plastic building bricks. The company extends its brand across video games, theme parks, movies, educational products, and licensed sets for children and adults. LEGO does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; consumer-facing systems and partner integrations are closed. A public GitHub organization hosts internal engineering tooling and open-source contributions.

providers.name: Mobcrush
providers.description: Mobcrush Streaming, Inc. was a Santa Monica, California live-streaming technology company, founded in 2013 by Royce Disini with James Hurley, Travis Rogers and Stephen Dao, that made it possible for mobile gamers to broadcast gameplay straight from an iOS or Android device with no capture card, no desktop encoder and no third-party software. Its differentiator was simulcast: a creator went live once and Mobcrush relayed the same broadcast simultaneously to Twitch, YouTube, Facebook, Twitter and Periscope at no extra charge, which turned the product from a competing destination into distribution infrastructure for creators who already had audiences elsewhere. The company added an advertising and sponsorship layer in 2018 ("Go Live, Get Paid") and operated Mineville, one of six official Minecraft server partners under agreement with Microsoft, reaching more than twenty million players a year. It raised roughly $35.9M across its rounds, including an $11M Series A in September 2015 led by Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers and a $20M round in 2016, with First Round Capital and Lowercase Capital also participating. Super League Gaming announced its acquisition of Mobcrush on 11 March 2021 and closed it on 2 June 2021 for approximately 12.6 million shares of common stock; the acquirer now trades as Super League Enterprise, Inc. and does not carry the Mobcrush brand forward as a product. Mobcrush ran a JSON web API at www.mobcrush.com/api/ that backed its own site and mobile apps, but it never published a developer portal, an API reference, a first-party SDK or any machine-readable specification, so there is no public API surface to catalog — and the mobcrush.com domain, while still registered, no longer resolves at all. This profile is retained as a historical record.

providers.name: Omni Creator Products
providers.description: Omni Creator Products (OCP) is a game development platform company founded in 2021 and based in Raleigh, North Carolina, operating fully remote. Its mission is to "empower every player to become a creator" by making game creation and modding accessible, intuitive, and magical. OCP's products include Muse, a game designed as a scaffold for user-generated content (UGC), and Creator Lab, a toolset that lets players remix and build upon existing games. The company raised a $16.25M Series A in 2022 with investors including a16z (Andreessen Horowitz). As of this enrichment pass OCP publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation, or OpenAPI surface, and its GitHub organization (ocpgg) has no public repositories.

providers.name: Pahdo Labs
providers.description: Pahdo Labs is a venture-backed consumer game studio (an a16z portfolio company) building anime-inspired action-RPG and world-creation experiences. Its public engineering footprint is a game-technology stack rather than a public API product: the pahdolabs GitHub organization publishes forks and modules for the Godot game engine (including a React loader for Godot, a prediction-and-rewind network synchronizer, a Tracy profiler integration, FMOD audio, GodotSteam, and FishNet networking). As surfaced from an a16z portfolio harvest, Pahdo Labs does not publish a developer portal, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, hosted MCP server, SDK for third-party integration, or a documented public API surface at this time. This profile captures the company's real identity and open-source game-engine tooling for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: 12 Gigs
providers.description: 12 Gigs, Inc. — later operating as Super Lucky Casino Inc. and renamed Super Free Games, Inc. — was a San Francisco-based mobile game developer founded in 2011. The studio began in social casino games (Super Lucky Casino) before pivoting to casual and word titles such as Word Collect, Word Nut and Trivia Star. It was acquired by Stillfront Group in December 2020 for approximately USD 150 million upfront and now operates as a Stillfront studio; its former superluckycasino.com domain now redirects to stillfront.com. The company exposes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK.

providers.name: 13th Lab
providers.description: 13th Lab was a Stockholm-based computer vision startup founded in 2012 that built SLAM (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping) technology for mobile devices, letting phones detect and track 2D and 3D objects through the camera in real time. Its products included the PointCloud iOS SDK, the PointCloud library, and the Minecraft Reality app. Backed by Creandum, GP Bullhound, and angel investor Gustav Soderstrom, the company was acquired by Oculus VR (Facebook) in December 2014 for a reported SEK 195M (~$25M), where its team went on to develop standalone inside-out tracking for VR headsets (Oculus Insight). 13th Lab no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no live website, developer portal, or API surface; this profile is retained as a historical identity record.

providers.name: 7k7k
providers.description: 7k7k (7k7k.com) is a Chinese online casual gaming portal operating a consumer-facing website that aggregates hundreds of free browser-based mini games across action, role-playing, strategy, puzzle, and two-player categories. Surfaced as a portfolio company of the venture firm Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The 7k7k property is a consumer web destination and publishes no public developer platform, API, SDK, or developer documentation; enrichment probes confirmed no OpenAPI, no .well-known discovery documents, and no security-disclosure or trust-center program at this time.

providers.name: 8sec
providers.description: 8SEC was a hybrid-casual and hyper-casual mobile game studio based in Lyon, France, founded in 2015 and later opening a second office in Paris. Over a ten-year run it published more than 90 free-to-play mobile games for iOS and Android — Jump Race!, Turbo Taxi, Trivia.io, Untie! and Human Puzzle among them — collectively driving roughly 50 million downloads, and positioned itself as a full-stack studio spanning game design, development and publishing. UK publisher Kwalee invested EUR 1.5 million in January 2024 and took over publishing duties across the entire 8SEC catalogue. THE STUDIO IS NOW CLOSED — the shutdown was reported in October 2025, with all seven staff, including cofounders Louis Croquet and Louis Giraud, seeking new roles. The company's own site at 8sec.games is no longer deployed — the domain resolves to OVHcloud shared hosting serving a "Site not installed" 404 behind a certificate that does not cover the hostname — and the Teamtailor careers page returns 404. 8SEC was surfaced into the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio lead; it never published a public developer API, SDK, machine-readable specification or documentation surface, and it no longer exists to publish one.

providers.name: Angelic
providers.description: Angelic (Angelic: Dark Symphony) is a dark, story-rich cinematic turn-based Strategy-RPG from Angelicore Game Studios, where players lead neo-human angels through tactical missions, impossible choices, and cosmic horror. Originally launched as a Web3 / metaverse gaming project backed by Pantera Capital, the title is now distributed as a premium PC game on Steam and the Epic Games Store. Angelic publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation surface as of this profile; it is a consumer game studio rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Appionics
providers.description: Appionics Holdings Limited is a Hong Kong mobile applications and games company that operated under the consumer brand name "Animoca". Co-founded by Yat Siu and David Kim, and emerging out of the Outblaze group, Appionics developed and published cross-platform games and apps for iOS and Android, claiming more than 150 titles and over 40 million downloads during 2011. In 2014 the company spun off part of its app portfolio, along with a set of licensed intellectual-property game rights, into Animoca Brands Corporation Limited (ASX AB1), which listed on the Australian Securities Exchange in January 2015 and later pivoted to blockchain gaming and NFTs. Appionics itself never published a developer program, and today has no live web or API surface of its own.

providers.name: Ares Interactive
providers.description: Ares Interactive is a game developer and publisher founded in 2024 by veteran industry leaders, operating studios in San Francisco and Berlin. The company builds player-first games designed to evolve with their communities and grow into enduring franchises, with a current portfolio that includes Baseball Hits, Heroes vs. Hordes, and The Walking Dead: Aftermath. Ares Interactive is backed by General Catalyst and was added to the API Evangelist network as a consumer/gaming portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing and careers website but no public developer API, documentation portal, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Artillery Games
providers.description: Artillery Games (also known as Artillery) was an early-stage technology startup backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) that built browser-based, real-time multiplayer strategy games and an associated JavaScript game engine. The company was acquired by GitHub in 2017 and no longer operates as an independent entity; its former artillery.com domain now redirects to a domain-sale marketplace. It was added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio lead, but exposes no public developer API, documentation, SDK, or other surface to enrich via the pipeline.

providers.name: Avegant
providers.description: Avegant is an augmented reality display technology company that develops light engine technology bringing high-performance visuals to lightweight AR glasses designed for everyday wear. Its flagship product, the AG-30L2 LED light engine, is described as the world's smallest LED light engine for augmented reality. Avegant is a venture-backed hardware company (a portfolio company of 500 Global) focused on the optical and display components that power the next generation of AR eyewear rather than on a public developer platform. No public API, SDK, or developer documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Azarus
providers.description: Azarus was a consumer startup that built an interactive engagement and rewards layer for live game streaming and esports, letting viewers take part in real-time interactive experiences and earn blockchain-based crypto rewards while watching streams on platforms like Twitch. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, Azarus was acquired by Coinbase in April 2021 to build interactive experiences into its consumer products. The former azarus.io domain now 302-redirects to a YouTube video and exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, packages, or other machine-readable surface; this profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead with no live API to enrich.

providers.name: baoyugame
providers.description: baoyugame (Guangzhou Baoyou Network Technology) is a Chinese game development and publishing studio founded in 2011 and headquartered in Guangzhou, focused on the research and development of mobile games and web (browser) games. Its founding team came from established studios including NetEase, and it operates multiple internal game studios with a development team of roughly 100 people, shipping turn-based RPG, ARPG, and strategy titles. The company is venture-backed, appearing in the portfolios of Qiming Venture Partners, Morningside Venture Capital, and Jiuhe Capital. baoyugame publishes a consumer game website only and exposes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface, so this profile carries company identity rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Battlebound
providers.description: Battlebound was a Los Angeles-based blockchain / play-to-earn game studio founded in May 2021 by former Riot Games technical artist Adam Hensel (pseudonym Damos), with a team drawn from Blizzard, Ubisoft, NCSoft and Riot Games. In March 2022 it raised a $4.8M seed round led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) with participation from Play Ventures and Dapper Labs. Its titles were Evaverse, a Steam-published social metaverse game using NFTs as playable avatars, and an in-development RPG codenamed Anterris (also referenced as "Project A"). The studio wound down amid the collapse of the web3 gaming market; as of 2025 it is defunct and the battlebound.com domain is parked and listed for sale. The company never published a public API, SDK, or developer platform, so there is no API surface to catalog or enrich.

providers.name: BeBop Sensors
providers.description: BeBop Sensors was a Berkeley, California smart-fabric sensor company founded in 2014 that designed and manufactured flexible, fabric-based pressure and touch sensors for OEMs across robotics, medical devices, automotive interiors, and virtual reality. Its best known products were haptic VR gloves and "intelligent sensing technology" surfaces that turned ordinary materials into multi-touch, pressure-sensitive inputs. The company raised a $10M+ Series A led by Bullpen Capital and shipped custom sensor hardware paired with bespoke firmware and integration software for enterprise customers. BeBop sold engineered hardware under contract rather than a self-serve developer product, and never published a public API, developer portal, or SDK. The company is no longer operating and its former domain has been repurposed by an unrelated third party.

providers.name: Believer
providers.description: The Believer Company (Believer) is a global games company headquartered in Los Angeles that develops and publishes player-focused interactive entertainment for players worldwide. Assembled from veterans behind titles such as Words With Friends, League of Legends, Destiny, and Plants vs. Zombies, and backed by a16z and Lightspeed Venture Partners, Believer builds next-generation game worlds with an emphasis on community, player investment, and immersive experiences. As of this profile, Believer publishes a company site and a careers surface but no public developer portal, API, documentation, or programmatic developer surface — so this entry carries company identity only, with no API artifacts to enrich.

providers.name: Big Fish Games
providers.description: Big Fish Games is a casual-games publisher and digital storefront offering downloadable and online casual, hidden-object, match-3, puzzle, card, and social-casino titles for Windows, macOS, iOS, and Android. Founded in Seattle in 2002 and now part of Aristocrat's Pixel United, the company distributes thousands of games through its bigfishgames.com storefront and mobile apps. It operates as a consumer-facing games company and does not currently publish a public developer API program, OpenAPI definition, or partner API surface; this profile tracks its public web presence for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Bigger Games
providers.description: Bigger Games is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of index-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: entertainment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: BigScreen
providers.description: Bigscreen is a social virtual-reality company founded in 2014 by Darshan Shankar. Its flagship Bigscreen app lets people watch movies, mirror their Windows PC desktop, play games, and hang out with friends inside shared virtual rooms across major VR platforms. In 2023 the company shipped the Bigscreen Beyond, an ultra-compact, custom-fit OLED PC-VR headset, followed by the Beyond 2 line. Bigscreen is a consumer VR hardware and software company backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and other investors; it does not currently operate a public developer program or REST API. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Bionic Panda Games
providers.description: Bionic Panda Games was a cross-platform mobile social games company founded in March 2010 by Charles Hudson (CEO) and Mike Jimenez (CTO), headquartered in San Francisco, California. The studio focused on Android-first social and casual titles, shipping Aqua Pets (a fishing and aquarium simulation that reached several million downloads and a top-100 grossing spot on Android), Vacation Slots, and PicAPic Camera. It raised seed funding from SoftTech VC, Norwest Venture Partners, Google Ventures, 500 Startups, and angel investors before ceasing operations. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company; the studio published no public developer API, so this profile carries identity and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: Blue Frog Gaming
providers.description: Blue Frog Gaming is a small independent game studio founded in 2007 by Matt Maroon and backed by Y Combinator (Summer 2007 batch), based in Akron, Ohio. The company builds browser-based and social strategy games, best known for Starfleet Commander — a persistent, multi-universe game of resource management, alliance building, and fleet combat — along with Stardrift Empires (built with Syfy Games) and the sci-fi MMO ShadowRift. Blue Frog Gaming is a consumer game developer rather than an API-first platform: as of this profile it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API description. This record is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it will be upgraded if and when a public API surface is discovered.

providers.name: Bonfire Studios
providers.description: Bonfire Studios is an independent video game development studio based in Irvine, California, focused on building original interactive entertainment, including its announced title Arkheron. Surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network, Bonfire Studios does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or other programmable developer surface, so there are no API artifacts to enrich; this profile is maintained as a company record and an ongoing lead should a developer surface emerge.

providers.name: Born
providers.description: Born (formerly Slay) is a Berlin-based consumer AI company founded in 2022 by Fabian Kamberi (CEO), Jannis Ringwald, and Stefan Quernhorst. Born builds AI characters and companions designed for shared, social experiences rather than isolating one-to-one chatbots. Its flagship product Pengu is a co-parented virtual pet with more than 15 million registered users, and the company is expanding into a multi-character platform called Friends and a photorealistic voice-and-video companion experience called Life. Since 2022 Born has launched five consumer social apps that reached #1 globally on the App Store. It raised a $15M Series A in September 2025 (participants include Accel, Tencent, and Laton Ventures), bringing total funding to roughly $25M. Born is a consumer mobile-app maker and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Boyd Gaming
providers.description: Boyd Gaming is a multi-jurisdictional casino entertainment company that owns and operates 28+ gaming properties across 10 U.S. states. The company offers casino gaming, hotel accommodations, dining, entertainment, and sports betting through its Boyd Sports platform. Boyd Rewards is the company's loyalty program spanning all properties, accessible via web portal and mobile app.

providers.name: budcreate
providers.description: BUD (budcreate.xyz, app at joinbudapp.com) is an AI-powered 3D UGC (user-generated content) interactive content platform where millions of creators build, play, and share immersive experiences and games. It is a consumer mobile creation and social platform spanning avatars, 3D worlds, mini-games, and AI-assisted content generation. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile. As of this enrichment pass, BUD publishes no public developer program, API documentation, SDKs, or discovery/.well-known surface — it is a consumer application, not an API provider.

providers.name: Buffd
providers.description: Buffd is a gaming and esports consumer application, delivered as an installable Progressive Web App (PWA) at buffd.gg, surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network.
