The company was linked in the venture-portfolio source to the now-defunct juked.gg esports property; buffd.gg is the live product surface. As of this enrichment pass, Buffd publishes no public developer program, API, OpenAPI, SDK, or documentation surface, so this profile carries identity and domain-security signals only, awaiting a developer surface to enrich further.

providers.name: Carbonated
providers.description: Carbonated Inc. is a mobile game developer founded in 2015 by industry veterans from Zynga, Electronic Arts, and Blizzard. The studio builds hardcore PvEvP (player-versus-environment-versus-player) games for phones and uses AI to help drive moment-to-moment gameplay. Its debut title is Mad World, currently in early-access sign-up. Carbonated also operates Carbyne, a proprietary live-ops platform that lets the team instantly modify almost every part of the game experience through a comprehensive set of web tools, built to support multiple games. Carbonated is a portfolio company of Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). As of this profile Carbonated publishes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal; this record captures the company identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: CardMonster Inc.
providers.description: CardMonster turns ideas and brands into games. The company designs and publishes premium IP-based tabletop titles with global partners such as Disney and Krafton, and builds CardMonster Forge, an AI-powered tool that helps creators turn their own ideas into playable digital prototypes. From physical board games to an online playtesting platform, CardMonster connects creativity and technology to make game creation faster, smarter, and more accessible. Backed by 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass CardMonster publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification; this profile captures company identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: chushou
providers.description: Chushou (触手TV / 触手直播) was a China-based mobile game live-streaming platform, at one point among the largest mobile-focused game streaming services in China, letting players broadcast and watch mobile gameplay. It was backed by Qiming Venture Partners and Tencent and is surfaced here as a portfolio lead. As of this enrichment pass the company's public web presence at chushou.tv is unreachable (the server returns empty replies) and it exposes no documented developer API, SDK, or portal, so this profile remains an inactive/defunct lead with no live API surface to enrich beyond DNS/TLS-level signals.

providers.name: Core Loop
providers.description: Core Loop is a game studio founded in 2020 by Vincenzo Alagna and Dan Chao, veterans of Machine Zone, GREE, and Funzio, building a modern cross-platform MMO at the intersection of massively multiplayer online games and web3. The studio is developing an AI-directed, dynamic world that evolves based on the actions of the community, with a blockchain-based, player-driven virtual economy in which participants truly own the assets they craft or earn and can potentially make a living in the game long-term. The game targets both PC and mobile. Core Loop raised a Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz, with participation from Galaxy Digital, Block.one, 1Up Ventures, Dune Ventures, and others, and operates as a remote-first team headquartered in Oakland, California. As a game studio, Core Loop does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, MCP server, or developer portal, so this profile is identity-only.

providers.name: CrowdMob
providers.description: CrowdMob was a mobile gaming and app-monetization startup surfaced as an a16z portfolio company. Enrichment probing on 2026-07-20 found no operating API surface: the company no longer appears in the a16z portfolio listing, and the crowdmob.com domain is now operated by an unrelated affiliate-marketing publisher (AffiliateBay) as a WordPress "growth marketing agency" landing page. No developer portal, documentation, API reference, specs, SDKs, packages, or /.well-known/ discovery documents exist. Retained as a historical/defunct record rather than an active API provider.

providers.name: Cult of the North
providers.description: Cult of the North (established November 2022 under the codename "Seidr") is a Stockholm, Sweden-based video game studio co-founded by former EA general manager Adam Schaub and former King SVP Marcus Jacobs, and backed by a seed investment from Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). The studio drew talent from King, Activision Blizzard, EA, Embark Studios, Resolution Games, and FunPlus, and set out to build large-scale, next-generation multiplayer PvP experiences for PC and console in Unreal Engine 5 — first the debut title codenamed "Project Gundalf" and later the free-to-play strategy war game "We Will Be Gods." As a consumer game studio it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile carries company identity only. Industry reporting in 2025 indicated the studio wound down operations.

providers.name: Datost
providers.description: Datost Inc. is a New York applied research lab building hardware and intelligent systems that operate in your environment without demanding constant attention — "computers that come after the screen." Its first public product is ED1TH, a 25-gram pair of AI augmented-reality smart glasses with a 640x480 green Micro-LED in-lens display readable in direct sunlight, hot-swap battery cells, a companion steel smart ring for gesture control, and a privacy-first design with zero cameras and a single hardware-mutable microphone. ED1TH runs ED1TH-OS and handles email, calendar, turn-by-turn navigation, live translation, and meeting transcription in the wearer's field of view. Datost is backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026) and OpenAI. As a consumer hardware and applied-research company, Datost does not currently publish a public web API, OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: DNA Games
providers.description: DNA Games was a social game studio founded in 2009 by Jon Lee and Shaun Haase in the San Francisco Bay Area, building technology for real-time social game optimization on the Facebook platform. The studio shipped Casino City, Bar World, and Slot City, casino and lifestyle simulation titles that together reached more than 20 million players, with Casino City becoming a leading casino simulation game on Facebook. The company raised roughly $2 million in venture funding from Battery Ventures and Bain Capital Ventures before being acquired by Zynga in May 2011, one of a rapid series of Zynga studio acquisitions during that period. Post-acquisition the founders and core team were absorbed into Zynga to seed a new internal game studio, and DNA Games ceased to operate as an independent company. As of the July 2026 enrichment pass the company publishes no website, developer portal, documentation, or public API surface; the dnagames.com, dna.games, and dnagames.io domains are all parked or listed for sale by third parties and are not operated by the company.

providers.name: Donnerwood Media
providers.description: Donnerwood Media was an early-stage social gaming and social entertainment company founded in 2005 by Sean Ryan and based in San Francisco. It operated Meez.com, an avatar-building platform that let consumers create customized 3D avatars usable across the web as personal identifiers, alongside a portfolio of social game properties. The company raised roughly $15.7M from Battery Ventures, transcosmos, and Allen & Company. It is now defunct — the Meez service went offline in December 2017 and its domain expired in March 2018 — so it exposes no live website, developer portal, or API surface.

providers.name: Doodle Mobile
providers.description: Doodle Mobile (Asia) Limited is a developer and publisher of casual mobile games for Android, founded in 2010 and backed by KPCB and Innovation Works, with research and development centers in Beijing and Shanghai and more than 300 million downloads across its catalog. Its titles include Restaurant Live, Dino Island (Dragon), and Fast Racing 3D, and it also partners with third party developers to publish games worldwide. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; enrichment found a static brochure website with no public developer API, SDK, documentation, or portal.

providers.name: Drivetime
providers.description: Drivetime (Drive.fm) was a voice-activated, hands-free in-car entertainment platform founded in 2018 by Niko Vuori, Justin Cooper, and Cory Johnson (veterans of Zynga and Rocket Games). The consumer mobile app delivered interactive trivia games, storytelling, quizzes, news, and audiobooks designed to be safe to play while driving, running on Amazon Alexa and Google Assistant, and partnered with the Jeopardy game show for a channel narrated by Alex Trebek. The company raised roughly $15M across seed and later rounds, with backing from Canaan Partners, Makers Fund, the Amazon Alexa Fund, Google Assistant Investments, Sinai Ventures, Fuel Capital, and Access Ventures. Drivetime was a business-to-consumer product and never published a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; as of this profiling the drive.fm / drivetime.fm domain and the associated App Store and Google Play listings no longer resolve, indicating the product has been discontinued.

providers.name: Edge Markets
providers.description: EDGE Markets builds financial infrastructure for high-throughput gaming and trading environments, positioning itself as the "financial backbone for a new asset class." Its product line spans EDGE Boost, a high-limit debit platform (up to a $1,000,000 daily limit) with built-in responsible-gaming controls and activity tracking; EDGE Connect, a private payment rail and closed-loop settlement layer that replaces traditional consumer card networks to cut transaction costs and chargebacks; and EDGE Pro, a banking platform (in development) for market makers and institutional investors. The company has raised a $29.2M Series A and partners with gaming and betting operators. As of this profile the company publishes a marketing and newsroom presence only — no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation surface has been found.

providers.name: Encore Music Technologies
providers.description: Encore Music Technologies, Inc. ("Encore") is a consumer live-music technology company based in Los Angeles, California, founded in 2020 by Ian Edelman, Jonathan Gray, and recording artist Kid Cudi. Its mobile app lets artists perform live inside custom augmented-reality environments directly from a phone while fans join, react, and pay artists in real time through gamified microtransactions such as a ten-cent "clap." The company raised a $9M seed round led by Battery Ventures in February 2022, with participation from 468 Capital, Kayak Ventures, Parade Ventures, and others. Encore ships consumer iOS and Android apps rather than a public developer platform; as of this pass it exposes no documented public API, and its marketing website (clapforencore.com) does not currently resolve to a live server.

providers.name: EQL Games
providers.description: EQL Games is a Louisville, Kentucky based lottery-industry technology company that operates as an original game studio, third-party content aggregator, and boutique licensor for the global iLottery market. Its iLottery Marketplace aggregates a catalog of 300+ games from 24 partner studios behind a single integration point for lottery operators, while its EQL Labs innovation division builds original instant-win and eInstant titles that fold in licensed intellectual property and live sports. The company also represents brands across lottery verticals (instant scratch and eInstant) and reports serving 8 lottery clients. EQL Games was surfaced through Bullpen Capital's portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes a marketing and corporate web presence but no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification at this time.

providers.name: Escher Reality
providers.description: Escher Reality was an augmented reality and computer vision startup founded in 2016 by Ross Finman (CEO) and Diana Hu (CTO), with roots in the MIT Sandbox program. It built cloud backend services for cross-platform, persistent, multi-user mobile AR — shared experiences that neither Apple ARKit nor Google ARCore offered at the time — letting multiple users interact with the same virtual objects anchored to the real world. The company raised roughly $3 million and was based in Sunnyvale, California. In February 2018 Escher Reality was acquired by Niantic (creator of Pokemon GO); its team and technology were folded into the Niantic Real World Platform (now Lightship), and the standalone company and its developer/SDK offering were discontinued. This API Evangelist profile is retained as a historical record; there is no independent, active API or developer surface to enrich.

providers.name: ESPL
providers.description: ESPL (Esports Players League) is a Singapore-headquartered global esports tournament network and platform, founded in 2019, building an open, grassroots-focused ecosystem for amateur competitive gaming. It runs ESPL-branded online and on-ground tournaments across Asia, Europe, and the Americas with a mobile-first focus alongside PC and console titles, operated from its Singapore headquarters with regional offices in Cologne and Los Angeles. ESPL is a portfolio company of 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups), which led its seed round in 2020. As of this enrichment pass ESPL publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or documentation surface, and its espl.co domain did not resolve (DNS SERVFAIL) at probe time; this profile is maintained as a company identity record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Fifth Door
providers.description: Fifth Door is a San Francisco-based, Y Combinator-backed (Fall 2025) AI-native gaming startup founded by Amir Ghazvinian and Daniel Kan that lets anyone create, share, and play games simply by describing what they imagine, with no coding required. Its generative-AI platform turns natural-language prompts into playable, customizable games, aiming to collapse the time, cost, and technical complexity of traditional game development for players, creators, and studios. Backed by Felicis, the company runs a consumer web app and does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation.

providers.name: FunFair
providers.description: FunFair began as FunFair Technologies, a blockchain gaming company that built Ethereum-based casino infrastructure (the Fate Channels state-channel technology and the FUN ERC-20 token) to let operators run provably-fair, on-chain casino games. The funfair.io domain now redirects (302) to FunFair Ventures (funfair.ventures), an early-stage Web3 venture firm run by the same team that invests across DeFi, gaming, infrastructure, NFTs, CeFi, social, travel, and DePIN, and sponsors the Blockchain Gaming Alliance. FunFair exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or documentation portal; its historical surface was on-chain smart contracts rather than a hosted REST/HTTP API. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of pantera-capital and enriched with live domain-security probe data.

providers.name: Gamefam
providers.description: Gamefam is a gaming studio that builds and operates high-quality branded games and interactive experiences for Gen Z and Gen Alpha audiences on platforms such as Roblox and Fortnite. It develops games, media campaigns, and amplification programs for 50+ brand partners (including LEGO, Adidas, Disney, and Netflix) and runs creator-facing programs such as Dev X and its Creator Fund. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. As of this enrichment pass Gamefam publishes no public developer API, portal, SDK, or OpenAPI surface — its products are consumer game experiences distributed through third-party platforms.

providers.name: Gravity Sketch
providers.description: Gravity Sketch is a 3D design and modeling application built for spatial creation, letting designers sketch, model, and iterate on concepts in virtual reality (Meta Quest, PC VR) and on tablet. It is widely used across automotive, footwear, industrial, and product design for early-stage ideation and collaborative review, backed by a cloud collaboration platform (LandingPad) for sharing and version history. The company is a creative-tools maker rather than an API-first provider; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, developer portal, or documented webhook surface. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel, GV, and Point Nine and captures the company identity plus a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: Gridsnap
providers.description: Gridsnap is a Los Angeles-based gaming studio founded in 2024 and part of the a16z Speedrun Cohort 002. The studio builds interactive worlds for community, powered by user-generated content (UGC), primarily using Unreal Editor for Fortnite (UEFN). Its work spans three areas - developing original IP, partnering with influencers to create community spaces inside Fortnite, and investing in emerging game developers by taking stakes in their projects while providing development support. Gridsnap publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation; this profile is a company identity record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: GTR
providers.description: GTR (Global Top Round) was a mobile game accelerator program that annually selected roughly ten indie mobile game studios, providing them global publishing connections, real global game-market and network access, mentorship, and fundraising support through a six-month accelerator program and the Global Top Round global mobile game conference. It was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. As of enrichment (July 2026) the company website globaltopround.com no longer resolves (no DNS A/NS records) and GTR appears to be defunct; it exposes no public API, developer platform, documentation, or SDK, so there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Happy Elements
providers.description: Happy Elements is a mobile game developer and publisher, backed by DCM Ventures, best known for free-to-play titles such as the Ensemble Stars! rhythm/idol franchise and Merc Storia. Operating across China and Japan, the company builds consumer entertainment games distributed through the Apple App Store and Google Play rather than a public developer API. Added to the API Evangelist network as a consumer-sector portfolio profile; enrichment found no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface, so the only machine-verifiable artifact is a probed domain-security posture for happyelements.com.

providers.name: Heroic Story
providers.description: Heroic Story was a Web3 gaming studio building a collaborative, community-owned tabletop role-playing game world — a Dungeons & Dragons-style on-chain MMORPG powered by smart contracts and NFTs on Polygon. Founded by Jay and Scott Rosenkrantz, it raised a $6M seed round in November 2022 led by Upfront Ventures with participation from Multicoin Capital and Polygon, bringing total financing to roughly $7.4M. As of this profiling the primary domain heroicstory.com resolves to a parked GoDaddy lander with no active product, documentation, developer, or API surface, indicating the project is dormant or defunct.

providers.name: Hidden Leaf Games
providers.description: Hidden Leaf Games is an independent video game development studio founded in 2019 and based in the United States. The studio builds competitive multiplayer games centered on competition, progression, and social play, with a stated mission of delivering a world-class experience where games are meant to be played together regardless of skill level or platform. The company is led by CEO David Li and President Bao Lam and raised seed funding from Lightspeed Venture Partners in 2021. Hidden Leaf Games is a consumer gaming company and does not currently publish a public developer platform, API, or SDK; this profile tracks it as a portfolio-sourced lead in the API Evangelist network for ongoing enrichment.

providers.name: Holor Media
providers.description: Holor Media was an integrated immersive media technology company founded in 2015 and based in Los Angeles and San Francisco. It focused on 360/VR content creation and distribution, building augmented and virtual reality authoring tools aimed at the next generation of social, interactive XR (extended reality) experiences, including interactive 360 apps for the Transformers film franchise. It raised seed funding from 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups), Skyline Ventures, and WI Harper Group. The company is now permanently closed and its former domain (holor.com) is a parked, for-sale listing on Afternic, so there is no active developer surface, API, documentation, or SDK to profile. This record is retained as a historical portfolio lead.

providers.name: Hortor Games
providers.description: Hortor Games (Beijing Haoteng Chuangxiang Technology Co., Ltd. / 北京豪腾创想科技有限公司) is a Chinese mobile game developer and publisher focused on casual, word, and mini-game titles distributed as standalone apps and as WeChat / Douyin mini-games. Its catalog includes idiom and word puzzle games such as 成语小秀才, plus casual titles like 肥鹅健身房 (Goose Gym), 咸鱼之王, 海岛来了, and 稻田路. The company operates consumer game landing and distribution sites across the hortorgames.com, hortorcx.com, and 666youxiting.com domains. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer API program, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: International Game Technology
providers.description: International Game Technology (IGT) is a global gaming company that delivers entertaining and responsible gaming experiences across all gaming channels and regulated segments, including lottery, gaming machines, sports betting, and digital gaming. IGT does not currently offer a public developer API program; its technical resources are delivered through licensed B2B partner channels.

providers.name: Jaunt *
providers.description: Jaunt (Jaunt VR, later Jaunt XR) was a cinematic virtual-reality and immersive-media technology company founded in 2013 and based in Santa Clara, California. It built end-to-end tools for capturing, stitching, streaming, and viewing 360-degree cinematic VR, including the Jaunt ONE professional camera and a cloud rendering pipeline, before pivoting toward volumetric AR/XR in 2018. Backed by GV (Google Ventures) among other investors, the company wound down its XR business and sold its underlying technology assets to Verizon in late 2019. This profile was surfaced as a GV portfolio company; the company is now defunct and its domains (jaunt.us, jauntxr.com) are parked/for-sale or reassigned, so there is no live developer or API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Jump Ramp Games
providers.description: Jump Ramp Games was a New York City casual mobile gaming company best known for Lucktastic, a free scratch-card, rewards, and instant-win app that launched on Android in 2014 and grew to roughly 10 million US installs across Android and iOS, consistently ranking near the top of the lifestyle category. Founded by Alex Betancur and Tony Vartanian and backed by Bullpen Capital, the company paired free-to-play casual gaming with performance-marketing and rewards technology. Jump Ramp Games was acquired by MobilityWare in September 2019, which took over the Lucktastic franchise; the jumprampgames.com domain now redirects to mobilityware.com. The company exposes no public developer, API, or documentation surface, so this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Juxta Labs
providers.description: Juxta Labs, Inc. was a San Francisco social and mobile applications startup founded around 2011 by Jared Allgood and Jayson Ahlstrom, building social games and light-social apps for teens (titles such as Zoomed In, Shadow Shapes, and Pick the Song) that reportedly reached tens of millions of users. In June 2015 the company raised roughly $1.7M from investors including 500 Global (then 500 Startups), Monashees, Alta Ventures, and Atua Ventures, which is why it surfaces in the 500 Global portfolio. The company is now inactive/deadpooled and its site (juxtalabs.com) is offline, so there is no live developer portal, documentation, or API surface to enrich. Note: an unrelated current company at juxtalabs.io (enterprise AI document automation) is a different entity and is not this 500 Global portfolio company.

providers.name: kaiheikeji
providers.description: Kaiheikeji Digital (开黑科技) is a Chinese mobile entertainment and esports social platform operating an online game "sparring"/companion marketplace, where players post demands (game, skill level, and price) and qualified players selectively take orders to play alongside clients. Backed by Qiming Venture Partners, which led a roughly $15M Series A+ round in 2018. The company operates a consumer-facing mobile app rather than a public developer API program; no public API, developer portal, or API documentation surface has been identified. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record surfaced from the Qiming portfolio.

providers.name: Kamcord
providers.description: Kamcord was a San Francisco-based mobile technology company (Y Combinator, Summer 2012) founded by Aditya Rathnam, Kevin Wang, and Matt Zitzmann. It offered an iOS and Android SDK that let game developers embed in-app gameplay recording, live streaming ("appcasting"), and social sharing to YouTube, Twitter, and Facebook, and grew to roughly 200 million device installs. The company later pivoted to a short-form mobile screen-content social network ("shots"). In November 2017 Lyft acquihired most of the ~15-person team, including co-founders Rathnam and Wang, and Kamcord wound down its consumer app, live streaming, and developer SDK by the end of 2017. The company is DEFUNCT and no longer operates any developer program or API. The kamcord.com domain has since been repurposed by an unrelated lifestyle/blog publisher and is NOT associated with the original Kamcord.

providers.name: Lagoa
providers.description: Lagoa was a cloud-based 3D visualization, rendering, and CAD publishing platform built by TeamUp Technologies Inc., billed as the first web-based platform for photoreal 3D visualization and rendering. It let artists, designers, engineers, and architects import over 40 native CAD formats, build kinematic assemblies, produce photoreal renders in the browser via its MultiOptics interactive rendering engine, publish interactive 3D product configurators, and collaborate on scenes in real time — with no local hardware or installed software. Lagoa also ran a developer platform exposing server-side Platform APIs (geometry and image transcoding, asset management, thumbnailing, user authentication, versioning) alongside an Application Framework with Application, Collaboration, and Real-time Persistence APIs for embedding browser-based 3D into third-party apps. The company acquired browser CAD tool 3DTin in September 2013. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. The company is defunct: the marketing site (home.lagoa.com), support and API documentation (support.lagoa.com) and application host all stopped resolving, the github.com/lagoa organization is empty, and lagoa.com is now a parked listing offered for sale on atom.com. No live developer, API, or documentation surface remains to harvest.

providers.name: Lost Lake Games
providers.description: Lost Lake Games is a Seattle-based independent video game studio building narrative-driven games. The studio raised a $5.1M seed round in 2022 led by BITKRAFT Ventures with participation from Lightspeed Venture Partners, 1Up Ventures, and Moon Holdings, and describes itself as being at the beginning of its next big adventure. As a consumer game developer, Lost Lake does not currently operate a public developer platform, API, SDK, or documentation surface; its web presence is a marketing site with an email signup and links to Steam, Discord, and Twitter/X. This profile captures the company's identity and public footprint within the API Evangelist network, surfaced originally as a Lightspeed Venture Partners portfolio company.

providers.name: Lowkey
providers.description: Lowkey (lowkey.gg) was a San Francisco social gaming platform that let players automatically record, review, and share their gameplay highlight clips across titles like League of Legends, VALORANT, and Among Us. Backed by Y Combinator and an a16z Series A, the company was acquired by Niantic (the developer of Pokemon GO) and the consumer product was subsequently discontinued. It was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-20 found no live public developer surface: the lowkey.gg domain no longer resolves/serves, and there is no public API, OpenAPI, documentation portal, SDK, or MCP server to harvest.

providers.name: Lytro
providers.description: Lytro was a light-field (plenoptic) imaging company founded in 2006 by Ren Ng and based in Mountain View, California. It shipped the first consumer light-field cameras (the Lytro and the Lytro Illum), which captured the entire light field so images could be refocused after the fact, and later pivoted to professional light-field capture for cinema and VR with Lytro Cinema and Lytro Immerge. Backed by a16z, Greylock, NEA and Qualcomm Ventures, the company wound down in March 2018 with much of its technology and talent moving to Google. It is defunct and publishes no public developer program or API; the lytro.com domain now 301-redirects to an unrelated light-field vendor (raytrix.de).

providers.name: Magic Circle Studio
providers.description: Magic Circle Studio is a venture-backed consumer mobile game developer building social games designed to nourish relationships through cooperation, creativity, and playful shared experiences. Its flagship title, Magic Garden, launched on iOS in July 2025 and reached one million players in its first year, following the studio's earlier titles Truffle Hogs and a Magic Circle Discord activity that won Discord's Best Chill/Party Game award. The studio received pre-seed funding from General Catalyst in 2022 and joined the a16z Games SPEEDRUN accelerator in 2023. It is a direct-to-consumer game company with no public developer platform, API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile is maintained as a network identity record.

providers.name: Magmatic Games
providers.description: Magmatic Games is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of creandum and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: consumer. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: MediaSpike
providers.description: MediaSpike was an AdTech startup founded in 2011 by Blake Commagere and headquartered in Mountain View, California, that built a native monetization platform for dynamic, programmatic product placement inside social, mobile, and virtual-reality games. Its API let game developers surface contextual in-game sponsorships and brand placements, and the network reportedly reached roughly 20 million unique users at its peak. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Google Ventures, CMEA Capital, 500 Startups, and others (a $5.2M Series A in November 2013), the company ceased operations around June 2017. mediaspike.com no longer hosts the product and currently serves only a "coming soon" placeholder; no live API, developer portal, or discovery surface remains.

providers.name: MojiLala
providers.description: MojiLala was a marketplace for stickers, GIFs, and emoji that offered a content API and mobile SDKs so developers could embed searchable sticker and animated-sticker packs into messaging and social apps. Backed by 500 Global, the team subsequently pivoted to LEO AR (leoapp.com), a consumer augmented reality application for creating, transforming, and sharing AR experiences. As of this profiling the original MojiLala developer surface at mojilala.com is offline (returns HTTP 403/530) and the active property, leoapp.com, is a single-page marketing/app site that publishes no public developer API, documentation, or well-known discovery endpoints. This profile is retained as a network lead; no live API artifacts were discoverable.

providers.name: Mountaintop.gg
providers.description: Mountaintop (Mountaintop.gg) was a remote-first independent video game studio founded in 2020 by veterans of Blizzard, Respawn, Riot, and Bungie, led by Oculus co-founder Nate Mitchell. Backed by a Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), the studio built Spectre Divide, a free-to-play 3v3 tactical PvP shooter featuring its signature "Duality" two-body mechanic. The game launched in 2024, but the studio wound down and Spectre Divide's online services were shut down in 2025. Mountaintop is a consumer game studio, not an API provider, and publishes no developer API, SDKs, or developer portal, and its public web and support surfaces are now offline. It remains cataloged in the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio company with no active API surface.

providers.name: N3twork
providers.description: N3TWORK Studios Inc is a mobile and blockchain gaming studio behind role-playing titles including Legendary: Game of Heroes, Legendary: Heroes Unchained, and Triumph. N3TWORK was previously known for its mobile game network and free-to-play publishing/user-acquisition platform, and was backed by GV (Google Ventures) among other investors. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or technical documentation surface; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record. Sector: consumer / gaming.

providers.name: naturalmotion
providers.description: NaturalMotion is a mobile game developer founded in 2001 and now operating as part of Zynga under Take-Two Interactive, with games downloaded over six billion times across more than 175 countries. Known for titles such as CSR Racing, Star Wars Hunters, and the Euphoria and Morpheme animation technologies, the company builds and publishes consumer mobile games. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass NaturalMotion publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: Neon Wild
providers.description: Neon Wild is a personalized children's entertainment platform backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) through its SPEEDRUN games program. Founded in New York by Troy Kirwin, it uses AI to transform a child's likeness into the hero of interactive digital books and narrative experiences distributed via the Apple App Store and Google Play. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or MCP surface, and its former neonwild.com Squarespace site has expired. This profile remains a portfolio-lead stub in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Ngmoco *
providers.description: Ngmoco * is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of gv, ivp, norwest-venture-partners and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: consumer. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: NOD Games
providers.description: NOD Games is a Seoul-based blockchain game studio founded in 2019 by CEO Chanki Lee, building entertaining game content and open, player-owned game platforms where gamers and communities own and trade in-game digital assets as NFTs. Its marquee titles are League of Kingdoms, a free-to-play 4X MMO strategy game with tradable Land NFTs and the LOKA token, and Crypto Sword & Magic, an RPG whose heroes, equipment, and pets are recorded on-chain with game logic running in smart contracts. The company is backed by a16z crypto. As of this enrichment pass NOD Games publishes no first-party developer program, public API, SDK, or GitHub organization; its official domain nodgames.com resolves to an unconfigured Wix parking page and the League of Kingdoms domain no longer resolves, so there is no live API surface to catalog.

providers.name: North
providers.description: North (formerly Thalmic Labs) was a wearable-computing hardware company founded in 2012 in Kitchener, Ontario by University of Waterloo graduates Stephen Lake, Matthew Bailey, and Aaron Grant. It first shipped the Myo gesture-control armband, which read electrical muscle activity to wirelessly control computers and other devices, and later pivoted to Focals, consumer smart glasses with a heads-up display. A Y Combinator Winter 2013 company that raised over $140M, North was acquired by Google in January 2020 and wound down; its products and consumer-facing website (bynorth.com) were discontinued. This profile is retained as a network record. North published no public API, developer portal, or SDKs, so there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: nWay
providers.description: nWay is a San Francisco-based multiplayer game developer and publisher founded in 2011, known for real-time synchronous PvP titles including Power Rangers: Legacy Wars (70M+ downloads), Power Rangers: Battle for the Grid, and the Web3 mech-combat game Wreck League. Its proprietary nWayPlay engine powers fast-paced cross-platform multiplayer across mobile, PC, and console. nWay was surfaced as a portfolio lead of cowboy-ventures. As a consumer gaming studio it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or documented API surface; enrichment probes of its website, /.well-known/security.txt, and /llms.txt returned no API artifacts.

providers.name: Parhelion Studio Co.
providers.description: Parhelion Studio Co. is an anime-focused game studio based in Ann Arbor, Michigan, and a portfolio company of a16z (Speedrun Cohort 002). Founded by a team that met at the University of Michigan, the studio builds live-service anime mobile and PC games — including gacha titles and the tactical anime trading card game Echoes of Astra — publishing across Steam, the Apple App Store, and Google Play. Their mission is to make anime a global medium and to create long-lasting IP through games and technology. Parhelion Studio is a consumer entertainment company; a public, scan of its website (parhelion.gg), app-store listings, and the a16z Speedrun profile found no developer-facing API, SDK, MCP server, webhook, or other machine-readable API surface. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio lead and enriched to confirm it has no public API program at this time.

providers.name: Peak Games
providers.description: Peak (Peak Games) is a global mobile game developer headquartered in Istanbul, Turkey, best known for the casual puzzle titles Toon Blast and Toy Blast, which reach roughly 40 million monthly active users worldwide. The studio was acquired by Zynga in 2020 and operates teams across game development, art, big data and data science, and cloud platform engineering. Peak publishes consumer mobile games and does not expose a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation; this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Penn National Gaming
providers.description: Penn National Gaming (now operating as Penn Entertainment) is one of the largest and most diversified regional gaming and racing companies in the United States, operating casinos and racetracks across multiple states. No public APIs have been documented at this time.

providers.name: PG Studios
providers.description: PG Studios is a full-service creative media company offering animation, film production, and creative media services. The studio operates specialized divisions spanning animation production, filmmaking, audio and music composition, and game development. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global, PG Studios is a creative-services business rather than an API provider: its public website markets studio capabilities and a client portfolio, and it publishes no developer API, SDK, documentation, or developer portal. This profile has been through the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline; the honest result is that there is no public API surface to catalog.

providers.name: PixOwl
providers.description: PixOwl is a mobile game studio, originally known for the early mobile version of The Sandbox and titles such as Doodle Grub, later acquired by Animoca Brands. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass the pixowl.com domain is a defunct redirect loop behind Cloudflare with no public developer portal, documentation, or API surface; only live domain-security posture (TLS/DNS) could be probed.

providers.name: Platogo
providers.description: Platogo Interactive Entertainment GmbH is a Vienna, Austria based social casino gaming studio that builds and operates free-to-play slot and casino apps for mobile and web. Its flagship titles are Slotpark, a premium Vegas-style social slots app used by millions daily, and Gaminator, one of the largest social casino gaming communities on the web. The company localizes its games into more than 13 languages and works alongside industry partners including Greentube and Novomatic. Platogo is backed by Seedcamp. No public developer API, SDK, or technical documentation is currently published; this profile captures the company identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Polyup
providers.description: Let'sMOD (formerly Polyup) is a Sunnyvale, California company founded in 2015 that builds a consumer platform where users aged 8 and up can play, modify, remix, and share short 3D microgames and AI-powered interactive memes. Originally a computational-thinking and math learning tool under the Polyup brand, the product has evolved into a generative-AI-driven microgame and viral-content community at letsmod.com. Let'sMOD is a 500 Global portfolio company. It exposes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal today; its public GitHub organization contains only internal CLI tooling and configuration. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched via live domain-security probing.

providers.name: Portals
providers.description: Portals (theportal.to) is a browser-based, Web3 metaverse and social gaming platform where users can play, collect, and create in a connected universe of interoperable virtual worlds. Players embark on quests, collect rare loot and digital collectibles, and build their own spaces, all directly in the browser without a download. Built on the Solana blockchain, Portals is a consumer-facing metaverse experience backed by Multicoin Capital. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead; as of this enrichment pass Portals publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface, so this remains a company/identity profile rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Quago Technologies LTD
providers.description: Quago Technologies is a gaming analytics and fraud-detection company that uses machine learning and mobile device sensor data to protect and optimize mobile games. Its platform analyzes in-game behavioral and device-sensor patterns - without collecting personally identifiable information - to detect and manage cheating, identify user-acquisition (CPA) fraud, predict player churn, and optimize monetization and lifetime value. Quago is delivered to mobile game studios as an embedded SDK plus a backend analytics service rather than a public developer API; it was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Radiant Entertainment
providers.description: Radiant Entertainment was an independent video game studio co-founded by brothers Tom and Tony Cannon, who also created the Evolution Championship Series (EVO), the premier fighting-game tournament. The studio was backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and is known for the free-to-play fighting game Rising Thunder and the voxel city-building title Stonehearth. Radiant Entertainment was acquired by Riot Games in 2016 and its team was folded into Riot; the studio no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface. This profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Rascal Games
providers.description: Rascal Games is a game development studio founded by Rick and Jon, both experienced entrepreneurs previously at Blitz.gg and Discord. The studio is building "Project Wayward," a group-based PvE action-adventure game inspired by Sea of Thieves, Valheim, and Fortnite, with an emphasis on cooperative multiplayer experiences. Rascal Games raised a Series Seed round backed by a16z SPEEDRUN and industry veterans including Mitch Lasky. As a pre-launch game studio, Rascal Games publishes a marketing and careers site but exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or technical documentation surface at this time. This profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; the enrichment pass confirms there is currently no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Reality Reflection
providers.description: Reality Reflection is a technology studio, surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global, whose website (realityreflection.com) is currently "under recovery" and points to two active projects, MOSS LAND (moss.land, which describes itself as "Infrastructure for the AI Civilization") and ROCKET.RUN (rocket.run). An enrichment pass on 2026-07-20 found no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, SDK, .well-known metadata, llms.txt, or security program for the company; the only machine-verifiable surface is the domain's live TLS/DNS security posture.

providers.name: Rec Room
providers.description: Rec Room is a cross-platform social gaming and user-generated-content platform where players hang out, play, and build their own rooms and games using in-app creation tools (Rec Room Studio and the visual Circuits scripting system). It runs on PC, PlayStation, Xbox, Meta Quest VR, iOS, and Android with a shared avatar and economy. Founded in 2016 (originally as Against Gravity) and headquartered in Seattle, the company is backed by Index Ventures among other investors. Rec Room publishes a consumer platform at rec.net; no official public developer API or documented developer program was found during enrichment (the site is served behind Cloudflare and an internal api.rec.net host exists but is undocumented/unofficial).

providers.name: Revolving Games
providers.description: Revolving Games is a mobile-first game studio and publishing company operating two independent gaming studios with a team of 150+ gaming-industry veterans. Its flagship title is War of Nova, a sci-fi 4X space-strategy mobile game for iOS and Android spanning base-building, empire-building, and competitive multiplayer live-ops gameplay. Backed by Pantera Capital, the company was surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; as of this enrichment pass it publishes a consumer marketing website only and exposes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: RTFKT
providers.description: RTFKT (pronounced "artifact") was a digital-fashion and collectibles studio founded in 2020 by Benoit Pagotto, Chris Le, and Steven Vasilev, known for NFT-based virtual sneakers, wearables, and the CloneX avatar collection created with artist Takashi Murakami. Backed by an a16z-led seed round, the company was acquired by Nike in December 2021 and operated as a Web3 / metaverse brand. Nike announced it was winding RTFKT down in December 2024, with operations ceasing by the end of January 2025. RTFKT was a consumer/collectibles brand and never published a public developer platform, API, SDK, or documentation surface; its remaining web presence is a frozen static archive page. This profile records that verified absence of an API surface.

providers.name: Scoreloop
providers.description: Scoreloop was a Munich, Germany based mobile social gaming company that provided a cross-platform SDK adding social features to mobile games - online leaderboards, achievements, player challenges, friend invites, and in-game virtual currency and monetization. The Scoreloop SDK supported Android, iOS, Windows Phone, Samsung Bada, Marmalade/AirPlay, and Unity 3D, and at its peak was used by more than 3,000 game developers. The company was backed by earlybird and was acquired by Research In Motion (BlackBerry) in 2011; the standalone Scoreloop platform and its developer service were subsequently wound down. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio lead - there is no live public API, developer portal, or documentation surface remaining (the scoreloop.com domain now serves a suspended page and no developer host resolves), so no API artifacts are available to harvest.

providers.name: Seriously
providers.description: Seriously Digital Entertainment is a mobile game studio best known for the Best Fiends match-3 puzzle franchise, a bug-versus-slug adventure set in the world of Minutia and available on iOS and Android. Founded in Helsinki with a Los Angeles presence and backed by Northzone, the studio was acquired by Playtika. It is a consumer entertainment company: its public web presence (seriously.com, which now redirects to bestfiends.com) is a game marketing and community site with app-store download links and social channels. Seriously publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface, so this API Evangelist profile carries company identity and a domain-security probe only.

providers.name: SHRAPNEL
providers.description: SHRAPNEL is a AAA free-to-play extraction first-person shooter developed by Neon Machine and built on a dedicated Avalanche blockchain subnet. Early access launched on PC in February 2024, with a Steam listing and a player-driven economy: modding and creator tools for building skins and maps, a marketplace for tradable in-game items, and the SHRAP token. Neon Machine has publicly announced a Web3 developer API platform named GameBridge, but as of this profile it is not yet publicly documented — SHRAPNEL exposes no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI, or docs portal, and shrapnel.com sits behind Cloudflare bot protection. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Polychain and tracked in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Skypunk
providers.description: Skypunk is an independent game studio headquartered in San Diego, California, founded in 2021 to build new science-fiction multiplayer games. The studio is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and has raised approximately $750K in early funding. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Skypunk is a consumer game developer, not an API producer: its public presence is a studio marketing site and it publishes no developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs, or any external API surface at this time.

providers.name: Slime Sandwich
providers.description: Slime Sandwich was an online gaming company that developed in-browser 3D games. It was founded in 2009 in Englewood, Colorado by Douglas Glover, Vadim Ugov, and former Photobucket CEO Alex Welch, and raised a $2.75M Series A round backed by Battery Ventures. The company has since permanently ceased operations and its slimesandwich.com domain is no longer active (now a parked/for-sale listing). It was originally surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment; enrichment confirms there is no live company website, developer portal, documentation, or public API surface to profile.

providers.name: Small Giant Games
providers.description: Small Giant Games is a Helsinki, Finland based mobile game studio best known for the hit puzzle-RPG Empires & Puzzles. Founded in 2013, the studio was acquired by Zynga in 2018 (now part of Take-Two Interactive) and continues to operate its live free-to-play mobile titles. As a consumer mobile gaming company it publishes player-facing games and support resources rather than a public developer API. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Creandum and EQT Ventures and processed by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline, which found no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, package/SDK, or /.well-known discovery surface — only a live consumer marketing website.

providers.name: Space Ape
providers.description: Space Ape Games is a London-based mobile game studio founded in 2012 and now part of Supercell, known for live-service mobile titles including Beatstar, Fastlane: Road to Revenge, Transformers: Earth Wars, Samurai Siege, and Rival Kingdoms. The studio operates in the consumer gaming sector and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDK; its primary web presence redirects to Supercell. This profile was surfaced as an Accel portfolio lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline, which found no public API surface and captured domain-security posture for the studio domain.

providers.name: Space Runners
providers.description: Space Runners is a digital fashion company that designs and launches digital wearable NFTs for metaverses in collaboration with celebrities and brands. Positioned at the intersection of Web3, gaming, and consumer fashion, the company produces branded digital sneakers, apparel, and wearable collectibles for use across metaverse platforms. Backed by Accel and Pantera Capital, Space Runners operates a consumer-facing brand and marketplace rather than a developer platform; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Super
providers.description: Super (super.gs) is an early-stage consumer entertainment application built by Outpace Studios and backed by Bullpen Capital, positioned around the tagline "Entertainment you can cash out." As of mid-2026 the product is pre-launch: the public site is a single-page marketing and waitlist experience with no published developer platform, API, SDKs, or documentation. This API Evangelist profile tracks Super as a portfolio lead and currently carries only a live domain-security probe of super.gs; it will be enriched further if and when the company ships a public API surface.

providers.name: Survios
providers.description: Survios is a virtual reality game studio that develops and publishes immersive VR titles across major platforms including PlayStation VR, Steam, Meta Quest, Xbox, and Nintendo Switch. Known for award-winning games such as Raw Data, Creed: Rise to Glory, The Walking Dead: Onslaught, Sprint Vector, Electronauts, and Alien: Rogue Incursion, the studio describes itself as one of the world's leading VR games studios. Backed by Lux Capital, Survios operates as a consumer games company; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal surface.

providers.name: Syntertainment
providers.description: Syntertainment was an entertainment technology startup founded in 2012 in Berkeley, California by game designer Will Wright (creator of SimCity and The Sims), Avi Bar-Zeev, and Anya Wright, emerging from the Stupid Fun Club collective. The company set out to explore the intersection of entertainment and reality, blending real-world data and player experiences with game-like interactive media. It raised roughly $5M from investors including Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Mayfield, SV Angel, and former Electronic Arts CEO John Riccitiello. The venture never shipped a public consumer product and is no longer active; its website (syntertainment.com) is offline and it exposes no public developer program, documentation, or API surface. This profile was surfaced from an a16z portfolio list and enriched to reflect the company's real, historical status.

providers.name: t4game
providers.description: t4game (呈天游 / Bstonegames) is the brand of Beijing Chengtian Network Technology Co., Ltd., a Chinese online-game developer and operator founded in 2008 and headquartered in Beijing. The company designs, publishes, and operates mobile, PC, and web-based games — including titles such as 醉江湖online (Drunk Rivers and Lakes Online) and 诛神传奇/诛神online (Zhushen Online) — spanning role-playing, real-time strategy, and shooting genres. Its public presence at t4game.com is a consumer-facing game portal (player login, registration, and recharge), company and culture pages, a product catalog, game/media news, and recruitment listings. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of the venture firm Qiming. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer program: no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, CLI, MCP server, or other machine-readable API surface could be found.

providers.name: TeamUp Inc.
providers.description: TeamUp Inc. operates fanZ (fanzapp.io), a gamified football (soccer) fan-engagement mobile app for iOS and Android. fanZ combines fantasy football (fantaZ), social following of teams, leagues and players, prediction challenges and mini-games, a rewards system of points, badges and digital collectibles, an official merchandise store, and global leaderboards, plus news, match highlights and video content. The product is a consumer-facing mobile application operated by Wathbah for Information Technology and backed by 500 Global; no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Tipp24
providers.description: Tipp24 is a German consumer online-lottery brand — a business-to-consumer service where players place bets on the outcomes of state and international lottery draws (secondary lottery / lottery brokerage) over the web and mobile apps. The brand is operated by ZEAL Network SE, a publicly listed company headquartered in Hamburg, Germany, whose email infrastructure (SPF/DMARC) still resolves to zealnetwork.de. Tipp24 is a regulated consumer gambling product; it exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs, and its web properties (tipp24.de, tipp24.com) sit behind Cloudflare bot protection. This profile originated as an Earlybird VC portfolio lead and was processed by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline, which confirmed the absence of an API surface and captured the domain security posture of the brand.

providers.name: Trendy Entertainment
providers.description: Trendy Entertainment was a Gainesville, Florida video game studio best known for the Dungeon Defenders tower-defense action-RPG franchise. Insight Venture Partners acquired the studio in 2012 for ~$18.2M and exited in 2019 when founder Augi Lye led an employee buyback and rebranded the company as Chromatic Games (chromatic.games). The only developer-facing surface the studio ever shipped is the Dungeon Defenders Development Kit — an Unreal Engine 3 game-mod SDK distributed as free Steam DLC — not a public web/HTTP API. Enrichment pass found no OpenAPI, REST API, developer portal, or client SDK registries: this is a games company with no programmable API surface, so most scored artifact types are N/A rather than missing.

providers.name: Trion Worlds
providers.description: Trion Worlds was an American video game developer and MMO publisher founded in 2006 in Redwood City, California by Lars Buttler and Jon Van Caneghem, and backed early by Trinity Ventures among others. It developed and operated massively multiplayer titles including Rift, Defiance, Trove and Atlas Reactor, published ArcheAge in Western markets, and ran the Glyph game-distribution client. The company was acquired by German publisher Gamigo in October 2018 and disbanded shortly after; its games, the Glyph platform and the trionworlds.com domain are now operated by Gamigo. Trion Worlds never published a public developer API or developer program, so this network profile carries company identity and domain-security signals only. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Trinity Ventures.

providers.name: TSM
providers.description: TSM (Team SoloMid) is a North American esports and gaming lifestyle organization, surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners in the consumer sector. Its public web presence at tsm.gg redirects to the official TSM Store (tsmshop.com), a Shopify-hosted storefront selling TSM apparel and accessories. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-21 found no first-party developer API surface: no developer portal, no API documentation, no OpenAPI, no resolving developer/api/docs subdomains, and no real /.well-known/ discovery documents (every probed path returned the storefront catch-all page). This profile is retained as a consumer-brand lead with only domain-security signals captured.

providers.name: Ursula
providers.description: Ursula is a Brazil-based AI startup building AI-native characters. Founded by an Emmy-winning team with experience at Pixar, Unity, Blizzard, and Google, it combines LLMs, symbolic AI, and long-term memory to power emotionally aware digital beings that evolve and connect with users across games, apps, and digital worlds. Ursula is a seed-stage Prosus Ventures portfolio company surfaced for the API Evangelist network. It publishes no public developer API program, and at enrichment time its Framer-hosted website at ursula.ai returned HTTP 404 (site unpublished) while the domain retained valid TLS and SPF/DMARC records.

providers.name: Virtualtech Frontier
providers.description: Virtualtech Frontier (VTF) is a creative technology company that designs immersive experiences by combining human creativity with technology across immersive centres and installations, experiential events and exhibitions, AI-powered audience engagement, metaverse and virtual worlds, and extended reality (XR/AR/VR). It operates the no-code metaverse-building platform Mitoworld and the Lumiworks service, with offices in Kuala Lumpur, Beijing, Dubai, Tokyo, and Singapore, and clients including HP, AIA, Nestle, Laneige, Dynatrace, and Omega. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global. No public developer API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: VR Motion
providers.description: VR Motion Corp develops virtual-reality driver-training simulation systems, marketed under its RealDrive product, delivering true-to-life driving simulations that the company says achieve over 70% greater skills retention than traditional training. It serves commercial fleets, last-mile delivery operations, first responders, and driving schools. VR Motion is a 500 Global portfolio company. As of the 2026-07-21 enrichment pass its public web presence is a marketing site with no developer API, docs, SDK, or developer portal, so there is no machine-readable API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Wave
providers.description: Wave is a virtual entertainment company that produces interactive, avatar-driven virtual concerts and immersive live music experiences known as "Waves." The platform streams stylized, real-time performances from major recording artists — including The Weeknd, Justin Bieber, John Legend, J Balvin, and Alison Wonderland — as animated avatars across VR headsets, desktop, mobile, and social video platforms, letting fans attend and interact with shows from anywhere. Wave is a consumer-facing entertainment and media product (accessed at wavexr.com) rather than a developer platform; as of this profile it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation. It was surfaced as a venture-portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network, where this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Weeby
providers.description: Weeby is a mobile/social game company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead for enrichment. Its listed website, gameclosure.com, now redirects to Playco ("the Game Closure team is now a part of Playco"), and no public API, developer documentation, SDK, or MCP surface could be found for Weeby as of July 2026. The profile is retained as a portfolio-graph node with a probed domain-security artifact rather than an active API producer.

providers.name: Win-Win
providers.description: Win-Win (trywinwin.com) is a charitable-fundraising platform that gamifies giving. Participants compete in tournaments hosted by celebrities and influencers, predicting head-to-head matchup outcomes and making tax-deductible donations to charitable causes while climbing leaderboards to win prizes and experiences. Win-Win also offers B2B tooling for nonprofits and corporations to launch their own gamified fundraising campaigns, alongside a consumer mobile app. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company. No public API or developer surface is currently published.

providers.name: Windwalk Games
providers.description: Windwalk Games is a gaming-focused company whose mission is "Creating Communities Through Gaming." The company builds and grows player communities and audiences around games and gaming brands. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Windwalk Games operates a single marketing website (windwalk.games) and publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable developer surface, so there are no API artifacts to catalog.

providers.name: WiTag
providers.description: WiTag Inc is an augmented reality mobile gaming company founded in 2016 by Thomas Suarez that built AR laser tag gameplay using only a smartphone's built-in sensors and radios, with no extra hardware. Lightspeed Venture Partners led a seed investment in 2017. As of July 2026 the company appears dormant, its website witag.co no longer resolves in DNS, no app is listed in the Apple App Store, and no public API or developer surface was found.

providers.name: Within
providers.description: Within (Within Unlimited, Inc.) is a Los Angeles virtual-reality studio founded in 2014 by Chris Milk and Aaron Koblin, both alumni of Google's Data Arts team. Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) led the company's 2016 Series A. Within builds Supernatural, a VR fitness service for Meta Quest headsets that pairs live human coaches with rhythm-mapped workouts set in 360-degree virtual locations; its earlier work spans immersive 360 video and AR (Clouds Over Sidra, Wonderscope). Meta Platforms acquired Within in February 2023 after the FTC's challenge to the deal failed, and it now operates as a Meta studio. Within is a consumer VR product company and publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal; its primary domain within.com is currently parked. This profile is retained as an a16z portfolio lead with no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Yoom (fka Tetavi)
providers.description: Yoom (formerly Tetavi) is an Israeli deep-tech company founded in 2016 that develops volumetric video and markerless performance-capture technology using proprietary AI and neural networks. Its products include YoomTrack, a studio-grade markerless motion-capture system that captures full-body, hand, and facial motion simultaneously, and the YOOM Volumetric plugin for Unreal Engine (distributed via Epic Games' Fab marketplace) that plays back volumetric capture content in real time. Yoom serves gaming, film, TV, VFX, and immersive-media studios and is backed by Insight Partners. The company distributes its technology as game-engine plugins (Unreal Engine, Unity, Autodesk Maya, MotionBuilder) rather than as a public web API; as of this pass it publishes no REST/GraphQL API, developer portal, SDK on a public package registry, or OpenAPI specification.

providers.name: YouStake
providers.description: YouStake is a peer-to-peer sports staking and sponsorship marketplace, founded in 2013, that lets fans invest in skilled poker and esports players in exchange for a share of their tournament winnings. Players list their buy-ins and backers can stake them for as little as $20, structured as a person-to-person sponsorship agreement rather than gambling. The consumer platform has since rebranded and now operates as StakeKings (youstake.com redirects to stakekings.com), which also offers white-label staking-marketplace software to partners. It is a business-to-consumer web application with no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or published API documentation.

providers.name: Zed.run
providers.description: Zed.run is a digital horse racing platform where players buy, breed, and race NFT racehorses, originally built on the Ethereum and Polygon blockchains and developed by Virtually Human Studio. Players collect uniquely bred digital racehorses as non-fungible tokens, enter them into skill- and bloodline-based races, and trade them on a secondary marketplace. Zed.run was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the public API host (api.zed.run) returns a "zed shutdown" message, indicating the developer/API surface is currently discontinued or paused, so no live API artifacts could be harvested.

providers.name: Zengaming
providers.description: Zengaming builds gaming marketplaces and community products focused on helping gamers manage and monetize their digital assets. The company is best known for LootBear, a CS:GO / CS2 skin rental and marketplace platform, alongside an eSports social network that connects players and teams to compete and get discovered. Zengaming reports serving over 6 million users across its products and is backed by 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass the company operates a consumer-facing marketing site only (an Unbounce landing page); no public developer API, documentation, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface could be found.

providers.name: VICI Properties
providers.description: VICI Properties is an experiential real estate investment trust (REIT) that owns one of the largest portfolios of gaming, hospitality, and entertainment destinations in the United States, including Caesars Palace and the Venetian Resort Las Vegas. The company holds long-term triple-net leases with leading gaming operators. No public developer API or developer portal has been identified; VICI engages investors and partners through corporate and investor relations channels.

providers.name: Duane Morris
providers.description: Duane Morris LLP is a Philadelphia-headquartered, full-service U.S. and international law firm founded in 1904 by Russell Duane, Steven Heckscher, and Roland S. Morris. Chaired by Matthew A. Taylor, the firm describes itself as "a law firm with more than 900 attorneys in offices across the United States and internationally" — with a U.S. footprint spanning the East Coast, Texas, the Mountain West, and California, plus international offices in London, Singapore, Vietnam (Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City), Shanghai, Myanmar, and joint ventures/alliances reaching Mexico and Latin America. An Am Law 100 firm since 2001, Duane Morris is known for depth in intellectual property (including patent prosecution and PTAB practice), trial and appellate litigation, real estate, corporate transactions, employment, healthcare, cannabis, and life sciences. The firm publishes an extensive LexBlog-powered thought-leadership network of more than 50 practice-area blogs, all of which expose RSS 2.0 feeds via the standard WordPress /feed/ convention. Duane Morris does not expose any public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI spec, GraphQL endpoint, webhooks, status page, or developer portal; the GitHub organization github.com/duanemorris exists but has no public repositories. The firm's only machine-readable surfaces are the RSS feeds of its blog network.

providers.name: Gaming and Leisure Properties
providers.description: Gaming and Leisure Properties, Inc. (NASDAQ: GLPI) is "the nation's first real estate investment trust focused on acquiring real property assets leased to gaming operators." Headquartered in Wyomissing, Pennsylvania, GLPI's portfolio comprises 71 premier gaming and related facilities across 21 states, totaling more than 29.3 million square feet and over 15,100 hotel rooms, leased on a triple-net basis to operators including Penn Entertainment, Caesars Entertainment, Bally's Corporation, Boyd Gaming, the Cordish Companies, and Hard Rock. No public developer API, data feed, or GitHub organization has been identified; GLPI engages investors, tenants, and partners through corporate and investor relations channels only.

providers.name: Playtika Holding
providers.description: Playtika Holding is an Israel-based mobile gaming company and Fortune 1000 firm that develops and publishes free-to-play casual and casino-themed games such as Slotomania, Bingo Blitz, and Caesars Slots. The company operates a portfolio of social and casual mobile gaming titles distributed through major app stores and uses data-driven engagement and live operations to monetize its global player base. Playtika does not publish a public developer portal or external API.

providers.name: Talofa
providers.description: Talofa Games is a consumer mobile game studio, backed by Insight Partners, that builds location-based and fitness-driven games where real-world movement powers play. Its titles include Run Legends, a cooperative running RPG for iOS and Android in which players' real-world runs and steps fuel monster battles, and Monster Walk, a walking game currently in closed beta. The company distributes through the Apple App Store and Google Play and runs its community on Discord. As a consumer game publisher it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this API Evangelist profile tracks it as a company with no API footprint.

providers.name: Talofa Games
providers.description: Talofa Games is a mobile game developer and publisher backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). The studio builds social fitness games that turn real-world physical activity into cooperative multiplayer play. Its flagship title, Run Legends, is a free-to-play running RPG available on iOS and Android in which players' real-world runs and walks power team battles against monsters, and its newer title Monster Walk is in closed beta. Talofa Games is a consumer mobile-gaming company and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this API Evangelist profile captures its company identity and public web presence rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Tripp
providers.description: TRIPP is a digital mental-wellness company whose consumer app delivers immersive, interactive meditation, breathwork and mood-management experiences across virtual-reality headsets (including Meta Quest and PlayStation VR) and mobile devices. It blends guided sessions, generative visuals, spatial audio and gamified "trips" to help people manage stress, focus, mood and sleep. Tripp is backed by Mayfield. As of this enrichment pass Tripp operates a consumer-facing application and an Intercom-powered help center but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation portal; its web properties sit behind a bot-mitigation (captcha) wall, so no OpenAPI, llms.txt, or /.well-known discovery documents were retrievable.

providers.name: National Indian Gaming Commission
providers.description: The National Indian Gaming Commission (NIGC) is an independent federal regulatory agency that regulates gaming on Indian lands to protect tribal gaming as a means of generating revenue for tribal governments. The agency publishes online resources, public records, and gaming-related data through its website but does not currently expose a public web API.

providers.name: PlayFirst
providers.description: PlayFirst is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of trinity-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: gaming. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Dreamscape Immersive
providers.description: Dreamscape Immersive is an entertainment and technology company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Culver City, California, that produces story-based, full-roam virtual reality experiences in which up to six people share a physical stage and see fully rendered avatars of one another inside a virtual 3D environment. It operates location-based VR venues in the United States, licenses its platform to international operators, and is a partner in the Dreamscape Learn education joint venture. Its public surface is a consumer ticketing and booking website; as of August 2026 the company publishes no developer portal, API documentation, SDK, or machine-readable specification, and the single backend its website calls is a private, key-gated AWS API Gateway host that returns 403 to anonymous requests.

providers.name: Funway
providers.description: Funway is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500-global and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: GameStop
providers.description: GameStop is a global multichannel video game, consumer electronics, and gaming merchandise retailer operating retail stores and e-commerce sites.

providers.name: Streamloots
providers.description: Streamloots is a monetization platform for live-streaming creators and their communities, originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners. It lets streamers turn viewers into paying supporters through interactive collectible Cards that trigger on-stream moments, plus Subscriptions, Auctions, a Marathon goal timer, and Tips. The platform works across Twitch, YouTube, Kick, Facebook, and Trovo, offers creator-favorable revenue splits and bi-monthly payouts, and provides fraud protection, a points store, and browser/OBS alert overlays. Streamloots runs a backend API at api.streamloots.com that powers its apps and Twitch Extension, but does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal.

providers.name: Playcurio
providers.description: PlayCurio is a Seoul-based educational technology company that builds AR (augmented reality) play-learning products for children, pairing physical educational tools with digital content. Its catalog includes AR titles such as Curio Safari, Phonics Pop, Dictionary Pop, and Math Mates, alongside a content-IP business spanning characters like Detective Pete, Dino Tales, and 100+ Curio Safari animals, plus B2B production services (character development, 2D/3D animation, UI/UX, and live-action video). PlayCurio is consumer- and partnership-facing and publishes no developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation. Surfaced via the 500 Global portfolio and enriched here; a domain-security probe of play-curio.com is the only technical artifact this pass produced.

providers.name: Millennial Fox
providers.description: Millennial Fox, Inc. is a Los Angeles-based consumer company backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners that set out to bridge the gap between entertainment and fitness.
