Its flagship product, Tracks Battle Squad, was a socially gamified workout companion for iOS and watchOS that integrated with the Apple Health app to turn physical activity into points, badges, and accessories for a virtual 3D fox character. The app launched in 2017, was featured on Apple Music's Planet of the Apps, and has since been removed from the App Store; the company appears inactive and exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, or well-known surface.

providers.name: Dream Voyage Inc.
providers.description: Dream Voyage Inc. is an AI-driven consumer studio founded in 2023 and backed by Andreessen Horowitz through its Speedrun accelerator alongside Soma Capital. Led by co-founder and CEO Coco Chen, a former TikTok founding product manager and Tinder PM, the studio builds viral AI-powered consumer applications spanning spiritual wellness, dream interpretation, gaming, and social payments. Its products include SINE Daily Manifest (an AI spiritual-health app offering daily affirmations, astrology, birth-chart analysis, and tarot readings that went viral on TikTok), Dreamore (AI-powered dream interpretation), Vdrop (turning social media into a payment network), and RPS (a Solana-based social game). Dream Voyage ships consumer mobile apps rather than a public developer platform; as of this profile it publishes no developer portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, or documented API surface. This record is a network stub retained for discovery and future enrichment.

providers.name: Fanatics Holdings
providers.description: Fanatics Holdings, Inc. is a global digital sports platform that connects fans with the teams, leagues, players, and events they love. Founded in 2011 and led by Michael Rubin, the company operates across several business segments: Fanatics Commerce (licensed sports merchandise, e-commerce, and manufacturing), Fanatics Collectibles (trading cards and memorabilia, including Topps), and Fanatics Betting & Gaming (the Fanatics Sportsbook and online casino). It has no public developer API program or published API specification; it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile surfaced from a16z's venture portfolio.

providers.name: Tamatem
providers.description: Tamatem is a Jordan-based mobile games publisher and platform focused on the Arabic-speaking MENA market. It localizes and publishes mobile games for Arab gamers and operates Tamatem Plus (tamatemplus.com), a consumer store for game vouchers, in-game items, and top-ups with a range of local payment options. Backed by 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass Tamatem publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface — it is a consumer-facing gaming and digital-goods business, so this profile carries identity and a domain-security probe rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: TrialPay
providers.description: TrialPay was an alternative-payments and offer-based advertising company founded in 2006 and based in Mountain View, California, backed by Battery Ventures among others. Its platform let merchants and game developers offer users a product for "free" in exchange for completing an advertiser-sponsored action (a purchase, trial, or signup), with the advertiser paying the merchant — monetizing users who would not otherwise pay. TrialPay shipped web, Android, and iOS SDKs plus offer-wall and monetization APIs (e.g. GetBuyCoinsInfo / GetBuyDirectInfo) widely used in social and mobile games. Visa acquired TrialPay in April 2015 and folded the technology into the Visa Commerce Network; TrialPay no longer operates as a standalone company and its public developer surface (help.trialpay.com, trialpay.com) is offline.

providers.name: GamerzClass
providers.description: GamerzClass was a Copenhagen, Denmark-based online esports education platform, founded in 2018, that offered structured masterclasses and one-on-one coaching from professional players across titles such as Counter-Strike, League of Legends, and Dota 2. Backed by 500 Global, ByFounders, Bumble Ventures, and TrueSight Ventures, the company raised roughly USD 2.5M before being acquired by US-based esports coaching marketplace Metafy in May 2022. The gamerzclass.com domain no longer serves a live site and the company exposes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Motion Math
providers.description: Motion Math was an educational math-games company (500 Global portfolio) whose products were acquired by Curriculum Associates and folded into the i-Ready learning platform. As of the enrichment probe (2026-07-20) the motionmathgames.com domain and every subdomain (developer/api/docs) return a 301 redirect to curriculumassociates.com/products/i-ready/i-ready-learning/motionmath-shutdown, and the site shares a wildcard TLS certificate with i-ready.com. The company publishes no independent API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or /.well-known discovery surface — this profile is retained as a network record of a defunct/acquired provider with no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Tiny Comet
providers.description: Tiny Comet is an educational games studio building history-based simulation RPGs for school-aged children, founded by Emily Tierney and Anca Agapi. Its first title, Nation Survival, is an immersive educational role-playing game on the Roblox platform. The studio came out of the a16z SPEEDRUN accelerator and has raised additional venture capital from Andreessen Horowitz and Roble Ventures. Tiny Comet is a consumer gaming and edtech company with no public developer or API surface at this time; this profile captures its identity in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: In-Fusio
providers.description: In-Fusio was a mobile entertainment company founded in 1998 in Bordeaux (Merignac), France, and one of the pioneers of the mobile games industry. In September 2000 it launched ExEn (Execution Engine), the first Java-based game engine dedicated entirely to mobile devices, competing with Sun Microsystems' J2ME, and partnered with Motorola on a client-side mobile gaming API for faster action and richer graphics. The company published games and community services across more than 70 wireless carriers and 140 handsets worldwide, with distribution deals including Verizon, Sprint, AT&T, Vodafone, Orange, Telefonica Moviles and China Mobile. It split its publishing and distribution divisions in January 2006, was acquired by Zenops in May 2007, entered administration in 2008, and went into compulsory liquidation in 2009. In-Fusio is recorded in the API Evangelist network as a historical portfolio company of Insight Partners; it operates no active developer platform or public API today.

providers.name: Beryllium
providers.description: Beryllium was a Singapore- and Delhi-based sports and trading game development platform founded in 2018/2019 by Amay Makhija, best known for its consumer product Sixer — a fantasy cricket game where users bought "Up" or "Down" virtual stocks in professional cricketers, with prices moving on in-game batting, bowling, and fielding metrics. The company raised roughly $3.6M across two rounds, including a $3M pre-Series A in June 2021 led by Bullpen Capital with Genting Ventures and Velo Partners. Beryllium was acquired by Dream Sports (Dream11) in October 2023. As of this enrichment pass the company is defunct as an independent operator: sixer.gg no longer resolves in DNS, and beryllium.ai is a parked domain listed for sale on the GoDaddy/Afternic aftermarket. Beryllium never published a public API, developer portal, or SDKs, so there is no API surface for the API Evangelist network to catalog.
